(Guardian follow-up #2).\n\n## Node Spec (Node Spec, 2026-08-01)\n\n> The token **names** (`--kind-glyph-*`, `--topology-v2-radius-*`) already existed. This\n> section fills in what those names **mean** — the rationale for shape mapping, why the radius is that value, why size follows child count, and when numerals appear. Response to owner directive (2026) \"Node specs and other info should also go into the design system.\"\n> Code references use **symbol names** — line numbers silently point to wrong places if code moves by even one line (the `node-shapes.ts:201` reference in the \"Fan\" section above is that failure case, corrected here to symbol names).\n\n### 1. Shape — kind is shape, not color\n\n**Channel choice is itself part of the specification.** Kind uses shape rather\nthan color as its distinguishing visual variable. As Jacques Bertin argues in\n*Sémiologie graphique* (1967), **hue cannot express order**\n(`.claude/agents/design-infoviz.md`). This app already reserves hue for two\ndifferent meanings: **hierarchy** through the brightness/depth ladder (project\n⊃ domain ⊃ capability ⊃ element; see \"Map Ink Ladder\" below), and\n**state** through color itself (three signal tones plus power/pulse). Adding a\nthird hue meaning for the unordered category of kind would contaminate both\nworking channels, so kind is carried by shape.\n\n| kind | shape | canvas source | DOM source |\n\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `project` | hex plate | `hexPoints()` → `bodyPoints()` (`render/node-shapes.ts`) | `<polygon>` (`shared/ui/topology-v2-kind-glyph.tsx`) |\n\n| `domain` | square chip (4 pin-tick legs) | `squarePoints()` → `bodyPoints()` | `<rect>` |\n\n| `capability` | circle (no shape deformation) | `bodyPoints()` → `null` (already a circle) | `<circle>` |\n\n| `element` | square + center via-hole (drill hole) | `bodyPoints()` body + separate via arc in `draw()` | `<rect>` + center `<circle>` |\n\n\n**Both gateways must render the same mapping** — merely listing it in the table isn't enough to enforce this (consistent with the principle \"specs are enforced by lint\"). Each file has only validated consistency within itself (`node-shapes.test.ts`, `topology-v2-kind-glyph.test.tsx`), meaning nothing checked whether the two files **shared** the same mapping. The contract test `tests/contract/node-kind-shape-parity.contract.test.ts` (added 2026-08-01) fills this gap: we broke one side's mapping with a probe to confirm failure (e.g., forcing it to draw domain silhouettes as circles is immediately caught).\n\nShapes converge to circles based on `farT` (far-distance progress) — once `FULL_CIRCLE_FAR_T = 0.985` is exceeded, they are always circles. Corner radii interpolate from `minCornerRadius`(kind-specific minimum corner ratio — e.g., project is 14% of the radius) to `r`(full circle) via `interpolateCornerRadius(minCornerRadius(kind, r), r, farT)` — this is a continuous morph, not a silhouette swap (`docs/TOPOLOGY-V2-DESIGN.md` §3.1).\n\nDecorations (pin-tick, via-hole, double hairline) are material expressions rather than silhouettes and are drawn only under the radius-`farT` gate (fading at a distance). The threshold is defined by the top constant block in `node-shapes.ts` (`DOMAIN_PIN_MIN_HALF_EXTENT`, etc.) as the single source of truth — do not duplicate values in this document (duplication is the start of drift, Carbon).\n\nThe node icon set (geometry/lines, see \"Personalization\" section #21 below) never changes this mapping — only the render **style** (`glyphStyleDescriptor`) toggles between fill+sheen and stroke-only.\n\n### 2. Radius — Fixed Ladder\n\n| kind | world radius | token |\n\n|---|---|---|\n| project | 30 | `--topology-v2-radius-project` |\n| domain | 17 | `--topology-v2-radius-domain` |\n| capability | 11 | `--topology-v2-radius-capability` |\n| element | 7 | `--topology-v2-radius-element` |\n\n`radiusForKind()` (`ui/topology-world.ts`) is the single lookup point. The values themselves are a **design decision** enforcing a strict hierarchy, so lint/contract tests cannot judge them — changing them requires re-convergence at the same evidence level (45 rounds of research + systematic review) as described in the \"Map Ink Ladder\" section.\n\nWe correct the optical illusion where squares appear larger than circles by reducing their radius — `DOMAIN_HALF_EXTENT_RATIO = 0.86` (shape half-angle = 86% of circle radius), element is 92%. Even with the same `r`, a square's corner area is larger than a circle's, making it look optically inflated — this is an optical correction, so it remains a constant rather than a ramp (a list of stepped values), for the same reason we don't enforce spacing optical corrections (see \"specs are enforced by lint\" and \"spacing is not enforced\").\n\n### 3. Size Scale — magnitudeScale (child count becomes size)\n\n`computeMagnitudeScale(kind, childCount, maxChildCount, k)` (`ui/topology-world.ts`) is the single source:\n\n```\nscale = clamp(1, 1.4, 1 + k × (√childCount − 1) / √maxChildCount)\n```\n\n- **Only domain and capability are scaled.** Project usually has 1–a few per vault, making relative size comparison meaningless, and **element is defined as always a leaf**, so `childCount` is always 0 — the function filters out `kind !== \"domain\" && kind !== \"capability\"` first, immediately returning `1`(base). The answer to \"why is leaf 1.0?\" is this: leaves have no countable children.\n- **`childCount ≤ 1` also uses base (1.0)** — the previous log compression reduced nodes below the median to *below* base, creating a false signal of \"small node.\" Now it's always at least base, signaling only \"this node is unusually large\" and never \"unusually small.\"\n- **Why √?** — It's gentler than log, preventing excessive compression of gaps while still compressing large differences. The goal is to provide ranking cues (\"which is larger\"), not proportional claims like a bar chart (Shneiderman overview-first — detailed comparison is for after clicking).\n\n  ⚠️ **2026-08-01 Measurement Correction**: The `--topology-v2-radius-magnitude-k` token comment in `app/globals.css` read \"log compression\" until just before writing this section — the actual implementation (`computeMagnitudeScale`) had already switched to **√ (square root)** compression, but the comment hadn't caught up. This is left here as an example of what happens when the same fact is written in two places (code comment + this doc): one gets fixed while the other silently remains wrong. The comment has now been corrected along with this discovery.\n- **1.4 Upper Bound** — Ensures max/min stay within the same kind ladder even at a distance (e.g., a domain should never appear larger than a project, which would invert the hierarchy).\n- `k = --topology-v2-radius-magnitude-k` (0.45, `app/globals.css`) — Scale intensity. Changing this recalculates all domain/capability node sizes, so 0.45 itself is a finalized design value (requires owner approval before arbitrary adjustment).\n- **Different channel from badge numbers (§4)** — Size uses `childCount` (direct children only), while numbers use `descendantCount` (all descendants). \"Large\" and \"high number\" can yield different answers on the same screen — an intentional dual channel (preemptive size + readable number).\n- Gate: `computeMagnitudeScale` describe block in `ui/topology-world.test.ts` — project/element invariant (=1), clamp bounds, base when `childCount ≤ 1`, defense for `maxChildCount`/`k = 0`.\n\n### 4. Engraved Numbers — When and What to Count\n\n`drawEngraved()` (`render/node-shapes.ts`) draws \"engraved\" numbers using a 1px dark shadow + light face (looking pressed in rather than printed). Display conditions require **all three** to be met:\n\n1. **Kind is only project or domain** — capability/element never display (`showCount` in `topology-frame-draw.ts`).\n2. **Screen radius exceeds `ENGRAVED_COUNT_MIN_RADIUS` (13px)** — prevents numbers from appearing larger than glyphs at a distance.\n3. **`farT < 0.9`** — fades out upon entering far-distance (overview).\n\nThe number value is `node.count = descendantCount` (total descendants, a different channel from §3's `childCount`) — `ui/topology-world.ts`. Project numbers are drawn in amber (hub/Layer-0 tone), domain in neutral tone (`numeralTokens` branch inside `draw()`).\n\nGate: Display conditions (kind, radius, `farT`) are sourced from constants in `node-shapes.ts` and the `showCount` condition in `topology-frame-draw.ts`. There is **no** contract test yet to catch regression of literal values (13, 0.9) — left as technical debt (follow-up: export `ENGRAVED_COUNT_MIN_RADIUS` for a short snapshot unit test).\n\n### 5. Bridge Nodes — Placeholder, Value TBD (2026-08)\n\nThe data side is currently specifying **bridge nodes** (first-class representation of relationships connecting two projects/domains), while the visual expression (owner request \"glowing / red border\") seeks alternatives within this charter — **pending design-informatics (`design-infoviz`) review**. Glow is already on the forbidden list (`forbidden.md`), and red borders overlap with error signal tones, causing misreading. This section defines only **placeholder and gate**, not value:\n\n- A fifth row may be needed in the shape mapping table (§1) — whether bridge is a new `kind` or an additional marker on existing kinds (e.g., new emphasis on the edge itself) follows data-side decisions.\n- **Once values are finalized, they will be incorporated into the §1–§4 body, not this section** — do not isolate it as a \"bridge-only section.\" Isolation invites future audits asking \"why is bridge treated separately?\"\n- Gate follows the **`node-kind-shape-parity` pattern** (simultaneous update of canvas gateway + DOM gateway + parity test expansion) — fixing only one side splits the map, INDEX/workshop/popovers.\n- If color is added (pending design-informatics approval), it adds a **fifth** branch to the already split amber discipline (`.claude/rules/design.md` \"amber has four branches\" section — hub · brand mark · kind tone · footprint trail). Update that section and the \"Three ambers, three rules\" table below (§2026-08-01 currently 3 rows — footprint trail not yet in this table, listed as separate tech debt) in the same PR.\n\n## Brand mark — \"Hex Constellation\" (candidate A, confirmed 2026-07-18)\n\n> Source: `docs/prototypes/app-icon-concepts.html` (candidate A, 48px master + 20px thumbnail). Implementation: `src/shared/ui/brand-mark.tsx` (`BrandMark`).\n\nThe mark reuses the same shape vocabulary as the v2 kind glyph above instead of\ninventing a new one: a **hexagon** (= project shape, §2.3 \"kind = shape, not\ncolor\") with **six vertex nodes** (graph nodes) and **spokes** converging on a\n**center hub** — the hub is stroked amber, the same single-exception amber\ntone as the v2 hub ring (§2.3.6, `--color-status-warning` family /\n`#d4b478`). Large it reads as a constellation graph; small it collapses to\nthe hexagon — the mark is never a separate pictogram bolted onto the product,\nit's the same shape language shrunk to a badge.\n\n**Two detail levels** (`BrandMarkProps.detail`):\n\n- `\"full\"` (default) — spokes + six vertices + hexagon + amber hub. Use at\n  ≥32px — nav rail avatars, in-app headers, marketing surfaces.\n- `\"compact\"` — hexagon outline + amber hub only, spokes/vertices dropped.\n  Use at ≤24px (favicon, macOS Dock at small sizes, dense chrome) where thin\n  spokes would just be noise.\n\n**Color contract**: lines and vertices use `currentColor` so a caller can tone\nthe mark via CSS `color` (e.g. dim it inside a disabled state) — this is the\none shared-UI SVG allowed to do that, because it is a monochrome brand glyph,\nnot a data mark. The amber hub is a fixed constant\n(`BRAND_MARK_AMBER = '#d4b478'`) exported alongside the component, because it\ncarries fixed brand meaning (hub node) independent of surrounding text color.\nStatic, non-React SVG/PNG exports (`app/icon.svg`, macOS `.icns`/`.ico`) can't\ninherit CSS `currentColor`, so those bake the same indigo (`#8b97ff`) +\n`#d4b478` amber as literal fixed values — this is the one place hardcoded hex\nis correct instead of a token reference, because the file has no DOM to read\ntokens from.\n\n**Where it ships**:\n\n| Surface | Asset | Detail |\n|---|---|---|\n| In-app avatars/headers | `<BrandMark />` (`src/shared/ui/brand-mark.tsx`) | full/compact via prop |\n| Browser favicon | `app/icon.svg` | compact, transparent background |\n| iOS/PWA home-screen icon | `app/apple-icon.png` (180×180) | full, dark squircle ground |\n| PWA manifest icon | `public/brand-icon-512.png` | full, dark squircle ground |\n| macOS `.app` bundle icon | `src-tauri/icons/{32x32,64x64,128x128,128x128@2x,icon}.png` + `icon.icns` + `icon.ico` | compact ≤64px, full ≥128px — same dark squircle ground as the PWA/apple icon (app-icon special case, §\"Absolute rules\" exception: app icons allow vertical gradient backgrounds) |\n\n\nGeneration pipeline for the raster/macOS set: render the HTML composition\n(squircle + inline mark SVG) at each exact pixel size with a headless\nbrowser, then `iconutil`/hand-rolled ICO packer assemble `.icns`/`.ico` from\nthe renders — no separate rasterizer script; the browser is the renderer of\nrecord so every size stays crisp instead of being scaled down from one master\nraster.\n\n## Cited lineage — where these rules come from\n\nThese rules are an applied reading of public, citable design thinking, not arbitrary taste.\nFull grounding + verified links in [`FOUNDATIONS.md` §4](./FOUNDATIONS.md#4-design-lineage--restraint-as-craft-cited).\n\n| Our rule | Descends from |\n|---|---|\n| Neutral greys + single indigo; ban glow/neon/gradients/glassmorphism | **Dieter Rams**, *Ten Principles* — \"unobtrusive / honest / as little design as possible\" (\"Less, but better\") |\n| Every visual mark encodes a typed fact and asserts no fact the data lacks | **Jock Mackinlay** (ACM TOG 1986) — expressiveness + effectiveness. This is the bench's rejection rule |\n| Honest, proportional relation rendering; a legend means the mark cannot explain itself | **Edward Tufte** — graphical integrity + direct labelling. **Not** data-ink as a rule: Inbar 2007 and Bateman 2010 tested it and it did not hold ([FOUNDATIONS](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-design-lineage--restraint-as-craft-cited)) |\n| `@theme` token scale; constrained spacing; \"no second coloring system\"; hierarchy by de-emphasis | **Wathan & Schoger**, *Refactoring UI* (also the Tailwind authors) |\n| Kind hierarchy + typed relations as the organizing device; lean high-signal vault | **John Maeda**, *Laws of Simplicity* — Reduce / Organize; \"subtract the obvious, add the meaningful\" |\n| Restraint as a *quality* decision (not decoration) that wins against AI-UI clichés | **Karri Saarinen / Linear**, \"Why is quality so rare?\" |\n| Invisible-detail polish (hover/focus/transition feel) without flashy patterns | **Rauno Freiberg**, \"Craft\" |\n| Motion: `transition-colors`/opacity, sub-200ms, minimal transform, `prefers-reduced-motion`; state-conveying not decorative | **Emil Kowalski**, \"Great animations\" |\n| Native-feeling motion that explains status, feedback, and continuity without overwhelming the task | **Apple Human Interface Guidelines**, Motion |\n| Design-system quality as a shared language for designers, developers, and product work; interaction detail as part of product finish | **Toss Tech** design-system writing and public Toss docs as principle sources only; do not copy Apps-in-Toss TDS/Figma UI Kit assets, components, styles, logos, or restricted UI patterns |\n| Unstyled accessible primitives + our own theming; mono for code/diagrams | **Radix Primitives**, **Vercel Geist** |\n| Topology: overview first, ego-focus + details-on-demand popover (never fullscreen on click); start focused as the graph scales | **Ben Shneiderman**, *The Eyes Have It* (1996) — \"overview first, zoom and filter, details-on-demand\"; **Cambridge Intelligence / yFiles** large-graph guidance |\n\nWhen proposing a design change, name which row it serves — or argue explicitly why it diverges.\n\n## Top-tier Quality Bar\n\nOntology Atlas should feel like a designer-grade macOS workbench for a local\nontology, not a web dashboard that happens to run in a desktop shell. The target\nis **Apple-level clarity and continuity** plus **Toss-level product finish**:\nevery action should feel calm, direct, and obviously useful, while still keeping\nthe restrained graph-workbench language that makes the product trustworthy for\ndevelopers and AI agents.\n\nThis bar changes how we judge UI work:\n\n- **Action quality** — every primary control should answer \"what happens next?\"\n  in the label, tooltip, aria label, and resulting state change. If a command\n  writes or validates the graph, the next proof surface should be one click\n  away.\n- **Motion quality** — motion is a semantic contract, not decoration. Use it to\n  confirm command feedback, preserve continuity between focused nodes, reveal\n  staged changes, or explain graph-state transitions. Keep it fast,\n  interruptible, transform/opacity-based, and fully compatible with\n  `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n- **Ontology expression** — visible UI should name the ontology handle it is\n  operating on: kind, slug, relation type, proof target, path, or graph query\n  contract. Avoid hiding the ontology behind generic document/editor language.\n- **Agent usability** — screens that change the graph should expose copyable\n  MCP/CLI proof packets or direct handoffs so Claude Code/Codex can verify the\n  same state the human just changed.\n- **Performance honesty** — graph DB-style affordances must show result\n  contracts, limits, partial evidence, and cache/query readiness. A pretty graph\n  without query evidence is not enough.\n\nReference anchors for this bar:\n\n- Apple HIG Motion: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion\n- Toss Design System overview: https://developers-apps-in-toss.toss.im/design/components.html (principle reference only; not a license to copy TDS assets or components)\n- Toss design-system article: https://toss.tech/article/toss-design-system\n- Toss / Apps-in-Toss Figma UI Kit license: https://developers-apps-in-toss.toss.im/design/prepare/figma-ui-license.html\n- Toss Slash MIT repo: https://github.com/toss/slash\n\n## Layers the agent consumes — who reads this document (2026-08-01)\n\n> Owner directive (latest practice survey as of 2026-07-31) — \"The design system for agents\" is directly tied to this product's identity (`AGENTS.md` \"agent-native, human-sovereign\"). Below is a gap analysis **mapped** to the current state of this repository based on web research results — not simply copying someone else's table of contents, but separating what exists, what doesn't, and what isn't needed. Sources are left for each item (only public publications, no asset imitation).\n\n**The \"agent\" this section refers to is the coding agent that opens this repository directly as a filesystem (Claude Code · Codex).** This differs from agents assumed by Figma MCP and Astryx JSON manifests, which access only via API **outside the repository** — this distinction separates each judgment below.\n\n### Already exists (what the 2026 industry \"missed\")\n\n| Failure patterns noted by the industry | This repo's answer | Evidence |\n\n|---|---|---|\n| \"Documents, tokens, and components say different things, so agents can't tell which is correct\" | **Single source of truth principle + lint enforcement** — tokens are in one place (`app/globals.css`), this document references names only without duplicating values, `no-restricted-syntax` mechanically blocks hardcoding | `.claude/rules/design.md` \"Specs are enforced via lint\", Carbon citation |\n\n| \"Agents only take what the prompt explicitly specifies, filling the rest (spacing, typography, color ramps) by guesswork\" | **Conditional rule auto-loading** — opening `src/**/*.tsx` or `app/**/*.css` automatically loads `.claude/rules/design.md` into the session even if the prompt doesn't request it | `CLAUDE.md` rule loading table, `tests/contract/rules-path-scope.contract.test.ts` |\n\n| \"Document drift should be treated as a monitored failure mode\" | **Contract tests monitor relationships (aliases, parity), not just values** | `topology-ink-contrast.contract.test.ts` (aliases), `node-kind-shape-parity.contract.test.ts` (§\"Node specs\") |\n\n\n(2026-08-01 survey: [Design Tokens Community Group Standard Stabilization](https://www.w3.org/community/design-tokens/2025/10/28/design-tokens-specification-reaches-first-stable-version/) · [\"Your Design System Is Not Ready for AI Agents\"](https://www.intodesignsystems.com/blog/design-system-not-ready-for-ai-agents) · [DESIGN.md format](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md).)\n\n### Newly filled in\n\n- **The canvas has no DOM — the only window agents \"see\" is `window.__atlasMap`** (`?e2e=1` gate, `ui/use-topology-loop.ts`). It outputs typed values for node coordinates, `draggable`, camera, selection, and cluster chip \"claims vs. actuals.\" 2026 industry discussions mostly bypass canvas/WebGL automation with **computer-use agents that view screen pixels**, but this repository uses an agent that accesses source directly, solving the same problem cheaper and more decisively via **typed hooks** without screenshot round-trips — direct remedy for the 2026-07-31 incident (cursor scanning misidentified background as nodes, \"not slow\" wrong answer 6 consecutive times). Gate: `tests/contract/map-testability.contract.test.ts`. This hook existed only in code comments, so it was effectively non-existent to this document's reader — this paragraph is its inclusion. Node **shape/radius/size specs** (above \"Node specs\" section) are not directly exposed by this hook — screen coordinates/interactivity are the hook's domain, while shape specs are derived from kind following static contracts §1–§4.\n- **Changed code references in node specs to symbol names** (entire section above + 1 existing line number reference in \"Fan\" section) — line numbers silently point to wrong places when code moves.\n\n### Deemed unnecessary (and why)\n\n- **W3C DTCG (Design Tokens Community Group) JSON export.** The first stable version came out in 2025.10, sponsored by over 24 organizations with a growing tool ecosystem — but the problem this standard solves is the **round-trip between Figma ↔ Style Dictionary ↔ code**. This repository has no such round-trip (no design tool source — prototypes are static HTML, `docs/prototypes/*.html`). Creating new DTCG JSON would mean values are written in **two places** (`app/globals.css`) — exactly the pattern this document repeatedly rejected. When consumers arise (e.g., actual Figma library adoption), add a script to **generate** from `globals.css` (manually maintained second source of truth is prohibited, build-time derivation is allowed — pattern like `docs-vault:build`).\n- **Component JSON manifests (Meta Astryx type).** This is an app-builder pattern for \"agents picking and assembling components from a component library.\" This product is a single application where humans+agents directly edit TSX in the same repository, so it needs \"rules to follow\" not a \"list of components to pick\" — that role is already handled by `.claude/rules/design.md` + lint + contract tests. Creating a manifest would create a fourth place saying the same thing differently from those three.\n- **Separate `DESIGN.md` (Google Labs format).** The problem this format solves (YAML tokens for machines + prose rationale for humans in one file) is already solved by this repository in other arrangements — tokens are in `app/globals.css` (CSS itself is a machine-parsable format), rationale is in this document (prose for humans). Adding a third file means three places to verify \"are tokens really these values?\" Since agents already read the repo directly, the benefit of separate manifests (reduced query costs) for remote agents doesn't apply here.\n- **Component-specific \"explicit anti-pattern\" metadata fields.** Industry cases (Spotify Encore type) are problems for **libraries** with dozens to hundreds of components. The \"anti-patterns\" in this repository already exist in one place — the \"Anti-AI Design Criteria\" section (below) + `forbidden.md`. Scattering them per component creates a new drift surface itself.\n\n## Design tokens\n\nDefined via Tailwind 4's CSS-based `@theme`. See `app/globals.css` for the actual implementation.\n\n### Scale fixed contract (2026-07-24, owner confirmed — \"fixed as is now\")\n\nAfter four consecutive prescriptions for the size series (zoom removal → field 36 → Pretendard → fundamental fix of twMerge misclassification → rail 20 unification), the owner fixed the current scale as standard. These are the only\nchroma exceptions to the neutrals + single-indigo charter; they explain\n*state*, never decoration. The single source of truth for the verdict is\n`isEvidenceOnlyConcept` (`entities/knowledge-graph`), and the display is\na set of `EvidenceOnlyBadge` (`shared/ui`).\n\n- **Badges are achromatic** — `--color-text-quaternary` text + `--color-border-soft`\n  border. The reason we don't use signal tones (amber) is scale: among 289 dogfood concepts, 193 are derived; using amber would cause dozens of badges to appear on one screen, directly violating the charter's \"more than three ambers is a defect.\" Hierarchy is communicated not by color but by **position** (collapsed lower layers) and quiet labels.\n- **Line height remains stable** — `text-label`(11px) + `leading-4`(16px) keeps it lower\n  than the body text on the same line (`text-body` 12.5px, line-height ~19px). See the *Dimensional regularity* section below for details.\n- **Hierarchy expansion motion** — `.insights-disclosure-in` = tab transition on the same surface, using **the same\n  keyframes and tokens** (`panelCrossfadeIn` + `--motion-fast` 120ms). New keyframe\n  0 · new duration 0. Since it only grows downward, the space for the row above remains unchanged (measured shift 0px).\n- **The bar uses the same layer for both** — since the counts come from the same calculation (`computeOntologyDependents`\n  = MCP `blast_radius`), having separate bars would draw the same 15 with different lengths in two lists, making the bar lie.\n- **Hiding is not hierarchy** — do not delete demoted rows. Scale is communicated by the toggle label\n  remaining as is (\"... view 193 items\"), and the developer's trace and \"create document\" promotion path remain.\n\n### Three ambers, three rules (the recurring audit false-positive)\n\nEvery colour audit re-opens this, because a grep for \"amber\" returns three\nunrelated families. They are governed by different rules, and a finding is only\na defect if it names the right one:\n\n| Family | Value | Rule |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| **Hub amber** | `--topology-v2-amber-hub` / `BRAND_MARK_AMBER` `#d4b478` | One hub ring + one Layer-0 container, plus two written exceptions (agent focus ring, `?recent=` spotlight). A third on screen is a defect. |\n| **Brand mark** | the same `#d4b478` in the nav-rail logo | Not an expansion — it is the product's mark, one instance per route, never data. Written down here so audits stop re-filing it. |\n| **Kind tone** | `capability` `rgba(211,159,73,.94)` (amber) · `element` `rgba(124,166,141,.94)` (eucalyptus) | A **data mark**. Allowed only where colour is the sole identity channel — the kind-census strip, map dots, tree chips. Composition bars whose segments are already identified by order + adjacent numerals use the app bar grammar (indigo primary + neutral + 1px seam) instead. Never a surface, rail, or callout. |\n| **Footprint trail** | `--color-footprint-trail` `#e8c47a` (2026-07-29, added) | Deliberately a DIFFERENT value from hub amber, not an extension of it — same family, split value, so \"center\" (hub) and \"walked\" (trail) never collapse into one meaning. Opt-in, default 0, `shadowBlur` capped 6px, single consumer (`shared/lib/footprint-glyph.ts`). Gate: `tests/contract/footprint-bloom-exception.contract.test.ts`. See `.claude/rules/design.md` \"amber has four branches\" for the full four-way rule. |\n\n**Bar colour is neutral + one indigo.** Indigo marks the primary series only —\nthe leading row in a one-value ranking (`DomainCompositionGrid`), the capability\nsegment in a two-value composition (`DomainCapacityBar`). The boundary between\ntwo segments is carried by a **1px seam** (a gap that lets the track colour\nshow through), not by hue: indigo against neutral measures 1.12:1, far under the\n3:1 graphic threshold, so the separator has to be colour-independent — the route\nWCAG 1.4.11 sanctions.\n\nThe earlier rule (\"bar colour follows the number of series\") granted every\ntwo-series bar a licence for two chromatic data marks. Measured cost on\n`/ko/projects` (1512 dark, 2026-07-26): 13 chromatic faces, 32,987px² of chroma,\nthe longest bar on the first-visit screen amber. Worse, the licensed pair failed\nits own premise — amber against eucalyptus composites to **1.14:1** on the\ntrack, so it never separated by luminance, only by hue, and that hue axis\n(orange↔green) is the one red-green colour deficiency (~8% of men) cannot\nresolve. Order (capability always left), the unit word, and the adjacent\nnumerals were already carrying identity three times over; the colour was\nduplicate ink.\n\nVerified live 2026-07-26 after the change (`/ko/projects`, 1512 dark): chromatic\nfaces 13 → **1** (the nav-rail brand mark), chroma area 32,987px² → 36px². The\ninsights configuration tab keeps 4 kind-tone faces, all inside the kind census card where\nthe unlabelled stack strip has no other channel. `/ko/project/[slug]` renders\nzero. None of these is `--color-status-success`; a green **status dot** would be,\nand that is a separate, sanctioned signal. Verdict 2026-07-26 (owner confirmed) —\nthe working file was in gitignored `.qa-scratch/` and is not in the repository. The measurement and rationale\nare copied into the \"bar coloring\" section of `.claude/rules/design.md`.\n\n### Borders\n\n- `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)` — subtle\n- `rgba(255,255,255,0.08)` — default\n- `rgba(255,255,255,0.12)` — strong\n\n### Typography\n\n- Primary: `Inter Variable` (OpenType `\"cv01\", \"ss03\"` applied globally)\n- Signature weight: `510` (Linear's signature)\n- Mono: `JetBrains Mono`\n\n#### Do not overlay Latin-only decorations on Korean (2026-07-26)\n\nThe owner read `What goes out`, `Sent records`, and `It's your choice to commit` with double spaces in the [AI Connection] panel. The i18n string contained only a single space — the gap was not between words but in the **space glyph**.\n\nThe cause is two Latin conventions being overlaid on Korean.\n\n| Decoration | What it does in Latin | What it does in Korean |\n|---|---|---|\n| `uppercase` + wide tracking eyebrow | Uppercase subheading structure | No uppercase. **Only letter-spacing** expands |\n| `font-mono` sentence | Signal that it's code/identifier | JetBrains Mono is a Latin subset, so Korean falls back, and **only spaces** remain as monospaced advances |\n\nRule:\n\n- **Do not apply `font-mono` to Korean sentence text.** If a line mixes paths/identifiers\n  with Korean, wrap **only the machine string** in a mono span\n  (`<span class=\"font-mono\">.ontology-atlas/llm-audit.jsonl</span> · commit choice …`).\n- The **Korean placeholder** for mono input fields should revert to body font — the value is a machine string, but\n  the prompt is not.\n- Do not use mono/uppercase/wide-tracking eyebrows for Korean sentence subheadings.\n  Provide hierarchy only through size and ink.\n- Keep Latin eyebrows themselves (they are normal signals in English labels/tabs/legends). The prohibition is on\n  **overlaying them on Korean**.\n\n**Bilingual surfaces condition decorations by locale (2026-07-26 entry check E-10).** If the same\ncomponent renders both ko and en, removing decorations entirely is over-treatment —\nthe eyebrow is a normal signal in en. `useLatinEyebrow(tracking)` in `src/shared/lib/latin-eyebrow.ts` is the single source for this verdict:\n\n```tsx\nconst eyebrow = useLatinEyebrow(\"tracking-[0.2em]\");\n<p className={`text-caption text-[color:var(--color-text-quaternary)] ${eyebrow}`}>\n```\n\n- ko → empty string (decoration 0). en → `font-mono uppercase tracking-…`.\n- **Machine strings are exceptions** — monospace is preserved for glyphs like gauge numbers, folder paths, and shortcuts where width matters. Only the adjacent **Korean words** change.\n- Unregistered locales are treated as non-Latin (it's costlier to apply incorrect decorations).\n- Components rendered outside the intl provider cannot use this hook — instead of hiding via fallback, place a provider mock in tests (`useLocale: () => \"ko\"`).\n\nMeasured evidence (1512×950 dark, full getComputedStyle): the first screen's 7 ko instances had tracking\n1.36~1.8px + mono fallback + uppercase overlaid on Korean → now 0 instances. en unchanged.\n\n#### Labels do not touch node outline lines (2026-07-26 entry check E-4)\n\nThe baseline for canvas labels comes from **one place**: `render/labels.ts#resolveLabelBaselineY`. `draw()` and the bbox build in `topology-frame-draw.ts` use the same function — if they diverge, the measured box and the actually painted text will be placed at different positions.\n\n- Label anchors use the **drawn** screen radius (including magnitudeScale · breathe · entrance ramp ·\n  selection's 1.12 growth). Using the nominal radius causes names of large/selected nodes to fall inside the shape.\n- Ensures minimum clearance (`LABEL_NODE_CLEARANCE` 3px) between the outline drawn **outside** the node disc (selection ring +6px) and the glyph. If only offsets are used, the glyph will pierce the ring as it grows upward from the baseline — this cannot be resolved at any zoom level (the font scales with it).\n- Ego member/hover node discs are passed to the label placer as **reserved**\n  (`NODE_DISC_LABEL_PRIORITY` = 1: selection/hover labels do not yield, only passive labels move aside). Reservations have an owner (`ownerId`) that exempts its own label.\n- The order of yielding is **flip first, suppress later** — if the bottom is blocked, try the space above the node once; only drop the label if that is also blocked (preventing \"nameless shape\" recurrence).\n\n### Map ink ladder — one depth axis, two others (2026-07-31)\n\nProduct of 45 rounds of map research + system stone verdict. **Structure is the contract, not values.**\n\n**Starting point**: All **eight** edge/node strokes on the map failed WCAG 1.4.11 (3:1) —\nthe brightest project stroke was 2.78:1, the darkest contains-l2 was 1.59:1.\nThe hierarchy stone's physical measurement captured the same issue from a different angle: contains line peak luminance 14.4\nvs background 13.3 is **effectively absent**, and the brightest thing on screen was not the connection line but\nthe summary chip (102.5). **The map's job is to show connections, yet connections were the blurriest.**\n\n**Depth axis (`--topology-v2-ink-depth-*`)** — single source of truth. Node strokes and\ncontainment edges are **drawing the same tree depth twice**, so they reference the same values:\n\n| Row | Token | Contrast | Alias |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| leaf | `--topology-v2-ink-depth-leaf` | 3.22:1 | `node-stroke-element` · `edge-contains-l2` |\n| mid | `--topology-v2-ink-depth-mid` | 3.42:1 | `node-stroke-capability` · `edge-contains` |\n| top | `--topology-v2-ink-depth-top` | 3.96:1 | `node-stroke-domain` · `edge-contains-l0` |\n\nInitially, I listed the two groups separately, and the third pair converged within a 0.02 contrast ratio **by chance**.\nThat’s luck, not a contract — if you fix one side, it drifts apart without any warning.\n*\"If a value is written in two places, the drift has already begun.\"* (Carbon).\n\n**Outside the axis:**\n\n- **`node-stroke-project`(4.63:1)** — One step on the depth axis. It has no corresponding containment\n  edge (since there is no parent above the project), so it holds its own value. This is the\n  brightest mark on this map.\n- **`edge-depends`(3.61:1)** — Not a hierarchy but a relationship **category**. It is distinguished by a separate channel (dashed line + indigo tint) rather than a step on the lightness ladder. Therefore, it does **not impose an upper bound between ladders** like *\"edges must be ≤ 80% of node strokes\"* — that rule assumes the two ladders compete, but containment edges share the same axis as nodes, while depends is on a completely different axis, so they are not comparable. The only constraints are:\n  **WCAG 3:1 or higher**, and **not exceeding the brightest mark (project)**.\n\n**Chrome is darker than content** — the cluster chip rest is at the **bottom step** of the lamp\n(`--topology-v2-cluster-chip-{border,ink}-rest`, 3.01/3.14:1). It is darker than any node but still respects the WCAG lower bound (it must not be unfindable as a control). **Not using indigo for rest is key** — indigo is this app’s single accent; if chrome used it constantly, it would compete with the user’s intended target. It wakes up to indigo on hover/focus.\n\n**Gate**: `tests/contract/topology-ink-contrast.contract.test.ts` enforces ① the 3:1\nlower bound, ② the order of the two ladders, ③ the **alias relationship itself** (not the value but the `var()` reference), ④\nthe out-of-axis rule for depends, ⑤ that chips are darker than any node, and ⑥ that gates do not degrade. Lint cannot catch this — it requires background color and WCAG formulas for judgment.\n\n⚠️ **Deprecated rule**: During research, I invented *\"edge contrast upper bound = node stroke × 0.8\"*\nbut later deprecated it. Since WCAG only provides lower bounds, this was an invention of this study; after unifying the axes, it became clear that **the premise was wrong** (two expressions share the same axis, so there is no reason to suppress one by 20%). To revive it, you must first demonstrate why the two ladders are in a competitive relationship.\n\n### Relief/Topology layout tokens\n\n> ⚠️ **Many token names in this section do not actually exist** (measured on 2026-08-15). After label rendering moved to the canvas, consumers disappeared, leaving only definitions and this document's spec descriptions. Same reason as `--pad-card`/`--pad-panel` (2026-07-26) — **unused tokens are misinformation, not specs.** Especially since this family presented sizes outside the type ramp like `-text-size: 10.5px` / `-svg-text-size: 9.5px` as if they were standards, which could justify ramp deviations for future developers. Use these tokens for click focus, camera movement,\npanel entry, drag settle, and focus confirmation before adding bespoke easing:\n\n- `--topology-motion-focus-duration`: short focus confirmation.\n- `--topology-motion-panel-duration`: panel/support chrome entry.\n- `--topology-motion-camera-duration`: camera pan/zoom continuity.\n- `--topology-motion-drag-settle-duration`: post-drag settle.\n- `--topology-motion-ease-standard`: default topology state transition.\n- `--topology-motion-ease-out`: landing/settle transition.\n\nNew motion must name what it explains: selection, camera relocation, drag\nmovement, path construction, composer blocking, or command feedback. Motion\nthat only makes the screen feel busy fails the design system.\n\n### Motion Syntax (usability motion family, Phase 3 2026-07-25)\n\nThe usability motion for \"verifying meaning\" in the map contextual editor and insights (`/ontology/insights`) is built only on the **single duration/easing family** below. Use only transform/opacity; glow, bounce-loop, and ambient loops are prohibited.\n3-step ramps are ≤240ms (above that, only **exception tokens with a name and reason** — currently 2:\n`--agent-panel-reflow-duration` 260ms panel reflow · `--overlay-spring-response`\n300ms overlay spring. Both have critical damping so their physics are correct; what was misaligned was not the code but this sentence).\n`prefers-reduced-motion` is immediately neutralized by the global rule in the `app/globals.css` base layer.\n\n- `--motion-fast: 120ms` — **Verification**. Confirming a state that has already occurred (hover/focus/color/\n  rotation/chip crossfade/tab content crossfade/picker origin scale).\n- `--motion-base: 180ms` — **Movement**. Surfaces changing position (popovers/panels/cards/\n  backdrops/docking entrance/exits). Matches Chrome's 180ms rhythm.\n- `--motion-settle: 240ms` — **Settling**. The signature that something is done (satellite repositioning (FLIP)·\n  commit convergence/completion linger).\n- `--motion-ease: cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1)` — The common easing for the three above.\n- `--topology-motion-camera/drag-settle: 420/720ms` — **Map canvas only**\n  continuity. Referencing this from a DOM surface is a defect.\n\n#### Choose by usage, not value — and don't use classes if it's the default (2026-07-27)\n\nThe ramp existed for a long time, but only one component referenced it. The cause was not taste but\n**plumbing**: over 500 `transition-*` utilities were running on Tailwind's `--default-transition-duration` (factory default 150ms) and the default curve, and among the 30 scattered `duration-<n>` literals in the code, 12 had manually re-typed that factory value — a number no one ever chose effectively became the app's default motion.\n\nSo we swapped the default duration/easing in `@theme` for ramp tokens. Result:\n\n- **Don't use duration classes if it's the default.** Unspecified transitions automatically\n  become `--motion-fast` + `--motion-ease`. Over 500 places that didn't change a single class\n  now ride the ramp.\n- **Conversely, specifying means \"this is not verification.\"** Where surfaces\n  appear or disappear, **specify `--motion-base` and write the reason next to it** — in this replacement, the help popover, \"Back to Top\" button, and 3 map internal entry buttons fell here (leaving them to default would cause flicker instead of fade).\n- **Elements receiving ramp duration go with the same family easing.** Swapping only duration\n  leaves half of the \"common easing for the three\" family definition unkept.\n- **Writing numbers directly is blocked by lint** (`no-restricted-syntax`, ratchet mirror).\n  Map-specific spots using `--topology-motion-*` remain as-is.\n\nEmpirical measurement (1512×950 dark, headless Chromium, rAF value-ramp sampling) — how this change altered the ramp's shape: Document tree row hover changed from `0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)` (first frame 2.5% · peak 4th · ramp width 108ms) to `0.12s\ncubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1)` (first frame 15.4% · peak 2nd · ramp width 92ms). The total displacement is the same, only the time distribution shifted forward — not near the pop threshold (70%), but improved toward the \"instant response\" (response visible in the first frame) discipline.\n\n#### Motion budget goes to the protagonist (2026-07-27)\n\nThe family above defines \"how much,\" this section defines \"for whom.\" It's a principle derived from empirical measurement: When clicking an INDEX row, the concept popover (the object the user summoned) reaches 88.8% of the luminance ramp in the first frame via hard cut, while the background map ego focus received 100ms easing — and the two stages were misaligned by 250ms, running separately. The motion budget was spent on the background, not the protagonist.\n\n1. **The protagonist gets it first.** When one input changes multiple surfaces, the transition belongs to the attention winner designated by the Design Guardian verdict. If the winner is a hard cut (first frame delta share >70%) and the background uses easing, that's a defect. Both being instant response (hard cut) is allowed — what's prohibited is inverted allocation, not restraint.\n2. **One input = one event.** Stages spawned by the same input start in the same frame.\n   If the start difference exceeds `--motion-fast`, humans perceive it as two separate events.\n   Stagger only when showing causality (cause first); intervals ≤ `--motion-fast`.\n3. **Verdicts via measurement.** Not screenshots, but frames — measure and compare the first frame share of the winner ROI and background ROI. This principle cannot be caught by lint (elements without transitions have no literals, so all value rules pass integrity checks).\n   So the gate is the Motion item in the Guardian verdict: a verdict that can't answer with the winner's transition token name is incomplete.\n\nPosition relative to existing disciplines: \"Exit via the path entered\" (direction symmetry) · \"Instant response\" (first frame\n33ms) · \"Interruptible\" · \"Not turning off but equivalent\" (reduced-motion) are rules **within a single surface**; these principles are rules for **allocation between surfaces**. Translated Apple HIG's purposeful motion and Tufte's ink budget (emphasis ink goes where information is greatest) into this app's syntax.\n\n#### What exhaustive measurement taught us (2026-07-28)\n\nBy remeasuring the full screen, we learned **three facts that supersede the principles above**. All three are of the type \"written correctly in rules but not actually enforced,\" so they are guarded by contract tests, not documentation.\n\n**① Exit plays forward under its own name.** Exit reversing the entrance keyframe via `reverse` **does not play where only classes change on the same element.** CSS animations do not restart if `animation-name` remains the same, even if duration/direction change; since the start time is unchanged, an already-finished animation interpreted upon meeting `reverse` + `both` jumps immediately to the \"post-end\" state, showing the **end state of reverse playback instantly**.\nNode popover close empirical: opacity `1 → 0` in **1 frame**, then only transform\n`1 → 0.9877 → 0.9829 → 0.9804` — **the already invisible element shrinks slowly.**\nLooks correct when read, and duration/easing are all tokens so value rules pass integrity checks.\nGate: `tests/contract/exit-motion-restart.contract.test.ts`.\n\n**② `!important` reverses layer order — write equivalents within the same layer.**\nThe global reduced-motion kill rule (`*`, specificity 0,0,0) lives inside `@layer base`.\nWriting equivalents **outside the layer** loses even with specificity (0,3,0):\nbetween important declarations, layer order is inverted, so the one inside the layer wins. When toast equivalents were written at the end of the file, the computed value remained `0.01ms` (verified empirically). **Even if a rule exists, wrong placement means it's as if it doesn't.**\n\n**③ Don't attach movement curves to opacity-only classes.** `.map-overlay-in`\nonly changes opacity but rode the movement expo curve (`--topology-motion-ease-out`), which hits 47% in the first frame (empirical 45.9%) — a large surface effectively turned on via hard cut. `.topology-chrome-in` is the other half of what we learned on 2026-07-27: \"brightness and movement must not share curves.\" Without a movement axis, what remains is brightness's curve, i.e., the app-wide ramp (`--motion-ease`). Ramp width intact, first frame share drops from 45.9% → 16.1%.\n\n**Frequency eats budget.** Surfaces triggered by hover/focus are encountered dozens of times a day, so objectively fast curves feel slow at that frequency. The answer is curve adjustment, not budget reduction: high-frequency surfaces use `0~--motion-fast`; movement/settling ramps belong to events happening a few times a day (mode switches/surface replacements/commit convergence). This discipline isn't enforced by md but by the shared selector array in `eslint.config.mjs` — hover/focus variants and movement/settling durations coexisting in the same className string are caught.\n\n**Swap takes two frames.** Where two surfaces alternate occupying the same spot (INDEX collapse ↔\nexpand, settings sheet open ↔ close), if only the arriving surface gets entrance syntax, the user's target object gets 0 frames while the background (mere result) gets 200ms — structurally violating verdict①. `src/shared/lib/use-presence.ts`'s `usePanelPresence` /\n`useSurfaceSwap` capture the frames they emit; the departing side is immediately neutralized via `inert` +\n`pointer-events-none`. Exit windows share a single `EXIT_WINDOW_MS` — varying per surface recreates the defect.\n\n**Crossfade must wrap reflow.** If only content fades but container height changes in 1 frame, text bleeds and boxes jump (insights tab empirical: height 878.5 → 605px, full document 246px jump). `useSwapHeight` measures the height **just before** replacement in the handler (if measured in effect, it's already the new layout so transitions always go from self to self), transitions to the empirically measured new height in one step, then returns to `auto`.\nHeight is a jittering axis so don't apply it for reduced-motion users.\n\n**WCAG 2.2 §2.3.3 exceptions are real exceptions.** The standard explicitly excludes **user-initiated** movement (scroll/pan/pinch). While the canvas camera's reduced-motion snap cut wheel/pinch/pan, for reduced-motion users this meant the **entire viewport instantly jumped in one frame** — worse than the intended easing and removing even clues to \"where did I go.\" Snap applies only to **app-initiated movement** (ego dive/fit/auto-align).\n\nCanonical utility classes (globals.css `@layer base`):\n\n- `MeaningEditorPanel` uses the shared `Surface`'s\n  `--motion-base` entrance/exits from the same origin as the selection inspector. No new easing or panel tokens created.\n- Canvas preview is an overlay outside the force graph. Draft uses dashed directional edge,\n  confirm converges dashes to solid via `MOTION.settle`, cancel disappears via `MOTION.fast`. Reduced motion draws final state instantly without position movement.\n- `.insights-tab-crossfade` — insights tab transition content crossfade\n  (`panelCrossfadeIn` reuse + `--motion-fast`). Hero number count-up uses JS\n  hook (`useCountUp`, immediate final value if `prefers-reduced-motion`), bar fill uses width\n  0→target transition (`--motion-settle`, 30ms stagger).\n- `.ai-row-disclosure` / `.ai-row-disclosure-body` / `.ai-row-swap` —\n  **List row expansion** (next section).\n\n#### List row expansion — exit via the path entered (2026-07-26)\n\nThe canonical contract for the surface where an inline card opens upon row click ([AI Connection] vendor list).\n\n- **One surface, two states.** Drawing different rows per state (replacement) leaves nothing to transition.\n  The header band (`--control-row-h`) is always the same DOM; only the detail area below\n  grows in height. Thus, the folded row **becomes** the expanded row rather than changing into something else,\n  a fact conveyed through motion.\n- **Open/close/content swap share the same transition.** With only one class, there is no room for\n  different curves per direction. If it simply vanishes without folding, \"Cancel\" reads as\n  \"something went wrong\" rather than \"cancelled\" — because the screen lacks clues to distinguish\n  whether the disappearance was intentional or a bug.\n- **Height transitions in px.** `height: auto` does not interpolate,\n  and `grid-template-rows: 0fr↔1fr` only handles open/close, failing to support **content swap** (input form →\n  registered action). When the consumer continuously writes actual content height via ResizeObserver,\n  open/close/swap/reflow converge into a single mechanism.\n- **Siblings yielding space signifies \"these three are siblings.\"** If the expanded row's height\n  grows continuously, the pushing down of subsequent rows is also continuous. Since the parent dialog's height\n  follows the same curve, expansion reads as \"growth\" rather than \"jitter.\"\n- **duration**: Height `--motion-base` (180ms), content opacity/2px `--motion-fast`\n  (120ms). Content is one step faster — on open, space appears first then text enters;\n  on close, text clears first so the empty box doesn't appear to close.\n- **JS does not replicate ms.** The exit unmount timer reads `--motion-base` via\n  `getComputedStyle` (cached once at module level).\n- **`prefers-reduced-motion` provides an equivalent rather than disabling it.** By overriding the global rule\n  (`transition-duration: 0.01ms !important`) only on this surface,\n  we remove shaking axes (height·translate) but keep non-shaking ones (opacity 120ms). This is because motion in this interaction is **evidence of causality** — a completely static screen\n  cannot distinguish whether something disappeared because I clicked \"Cancel\" or because the app broke. The override rule must appear **later in source order** than the global block to win (if the order is reversed, it silently fails).\n- **Accessibility**: It remains in the DOM during folding (≈180ms), so the detail area becomes\n  `inert` immediately upon closing — invisible input fields do not remain in tab order/screen reader scope. We do not pay accessibility costs for exit motion.\n- **Undo happens on that frame.** \"Cancel\", header toggle, and Esc converge into a **single function**, avoiding confirmation dialogs (confirmation is excessive for discarding an unentered state). Even with entered content, it discards quietly — losing it is just a matter of pasting again, and this card's confirmation budget is already spent by the [Delete] 2-step confirmation.\n\n\n### The reduced-motion equivalent is a list, and tests enforce that list (2026-07-26)\n\nThe above contract (\"providing an equivalent rather than disabling\") existed **only in documentation** for a while. The only selector actually enforcing it was `.ai-row-disclosure`; other surfaces were hard-cut by the global rule (`animation-duration: 0.01ms !important`). Frame measurement: Settings sheet 150ms easing → **98.9% of total delta in 1 frame**, Insights tab transition 150ms → 1 frame. Writing specs only in documentation does not ensure compliance.\n\nNow, **the surface requiring an equivalent is a list**, and `tests/contract/reduced-motion-equivalent.contract.test.ts` blocks deviations between that list and globals.css. Rule set:\n\n1. **The global kill rule remains.** It is a safety net for un-audited motion (infinite heartbeat `.agent-pending-dot`, decorative flow `.studio-strut-flow`). Stopping is correct there, and the fact of progression is already stated by the adjacent text.\n2. **Crossfade types reclaim time** — `.insights-tab-crossfade` ·\n   `.insights-disclosure-in` · `.ai-row-swap` · `.agent-panel-stage-swap` ·\n   `.overlay-fade-only` · `.app-settings-scrim-in` · `.map-overlay-in` ·\n   `.overlay-spring-scrim`. Since they are opacity-only, we only restore the duration token.\n3. **Appearances with transforms change only the keyframe name** —\n   `.app-settings-panel-in` · `.topology-chrome-in` / `-out` ·\n   `.rail-status-dot-in` switch to `animation-name: panelCrossfadeIn` (opacity-only) and retain their own duration token. **New keyframes 0 · New duration 0.**\n4. **The override block must appear later in source order than the global block.** If it appears first, it silently fails.\n5. **No literal ms rewrites.** Equivalents reclaim time only via tokens (the gate checks this).\n\nMeasured result (Settings sheet open, reduced-motion): 1-frame 98.9% hard-cut →\n`1.217 → 1.664 → 1.731 (peak at frame 3) → 1.591 → 1.217 → 0.961 → 0.913 → 0.155`\n= True easing of ~150ms for the first frame's 25.9%, with only the scale axis removed.\n\n### Tokenization Contract For Relief/Topology\n\nRelief/Topology is not allowed to rely on \"looks better\" CSS. A visual value is\nvalid only when it is a named workbench decision, an ontology-reading decision,\nor a verified interaction decision.\n\nUse named `--topology-*` tokens or add a documented token before changing:\n\n- panel width, reserved map space, padding, radius, border, surface, shadow, and\n  z-order intent;\n- relation label width, selected relation card density, chip rhythm, footer\n  height, disclosure thresholds, and proof row layout;\n- dim/scrim treatment for a blocking composer, modal, destructive confirm, or\n  write surface;\n- camera, focus, panel, drag, path, composer, and reduced-motion durations or\n  easing;\n- MCP/CLI handoff markers that prove the selected fact, evidence, quality, and\n  next action stay visible.\n\nRelation-label handoff state is aggregated on the skeleton-cards root with\n`data-relation-label-handoff-contract=\"label-level-mcp-cli-fallback\"`. Every map\nlabel hit target must expose its gate, primary MCP action, CLI fallback command,\nfact route, quality, and evidence; when a map label is selected, the root also\nmirrors the selected label's handoff state so installed-app WebView evidence can\nprove the label is an actionable ontology fact, not just a decorative badge.\n\nRelation-label geometry is also a frame-level contract. The skeleton-cards root\nmust expose `data-relation-label-geometry-contract=\"frame-positioned-hit-targets\"`\nwith after-render expected/ready/pending counts, so a visible scan label is\nproved to have real viewport-clamped hit-target geometry before the user opens a\nrelation card.\n\nEach new topology token needs:\n\n- **product reason**: the user problem it reduces, such as overlap, unclear\n  current action, unreadable relation evidence, or untrustworthy handoff;\n- **state/layer**: map, support panel, focus/path, transient, blocking\n  composer, or utility chrome;\n- **responsive fallback**: compact, 14-inch fullscreen, 1920x1080, and\n  2560x1440 behavior;\n- **WebView/test marker**: deterministic evidence that the token is active and\n  the relevant overlap/transient count remains acceptable.\n\nTreat W3C/DTCG-style design tokens as the principle: design decisions should be\nportable, named, inspectable, and testable across tools. This repo does not\ncopy third-party component skins, palettes, layouts, screenshots, assets, or\nanimation signatures.\n\n### Touch & tablet responsive contract (2026-07-23, Responsive Audit Round)\n\nWidth breakpoints alone cannot express \"tablet = touch\" — a 1024px display could be a fine-pointer laptop or a coarse-pointer 12.9\" iPad. Thus, the touch axis is a **separate contract**:\n\n- **`--touch-target-min: 44px`** (`:root`) + **`@media (pointer: coarse)`**\n  block serve as the single source. In coarse mode, `--app-nav-rail-tile-height` (32→44) ·\n  `--topology-chrome-control-height` (clamp 32–36→44) ·\n  `--topology-shortcut-sheet-close-size` are promoted to 44px. Fine-pointer retains density. No dark/single/color changes — only height/Hit area.\n- **Bottom tab bar reservation** — For `<lg` where BottomTabBar exists, surfaces anchored to the bottom or having scroll ends must subtract/pad `--topology-mobile-bottom-tab-reserve`\n  (56px + safe-area). Application points: expanded INDEX (`--topology-index-bottom-inset`) · bottom-right gauge\n  (`--topology-relation-legend-bottom-inset`, bottom-specific separate token) · datasheet max-height (`--topology-v2-panel-bottom-reserve` single knob) · content page main `max-lg` bottom padding. **\"Blocked by tab bar behind it is a defect\"** — when creating new bottom-anchored surfaces, contract from this reservation.\n- **`<md` expanded INDEX = full-bleed sheet** — `--topology-index-width` switches to `calc(100vw - 2 * var(--topology-index-inset))` at `<md`. Narrow screens use \"one main view at a time\": expand for sheet (map is context), collapse for full map. The boundary shares md (768) with GlobalSearch's sheet↔floating split — sheet-like surfaces share this boundary.\n- **Honest degradation** — Do not force desktop workbench (macOS app window) surfaces (e.g., Builder 3-pane) into tablet widths. The Builder canvas gate is lg (1024)+; below that, tree editing + topology fallback is correct.\n\n### Shell body slot — No-compression contract (2026-07-27)\n\n**Scroll containers do not compress their children.** The shell (`AppShell`) owns viewport height, and the body slot scrolls; that slot is a flex column. Page roots use `min-h-full` to fill the slot, and this **explicit min-height overrides the flex item's automatic minimum size (= content height)**. Thus, when content exceeds viewport height, flex shrinks the page box to viewport height, causing content to overflow visibly — scrolling works, but **the bottom reservation declared by the page is trapped at the shrunk box bottom**.\n\nMeasured (at defect time): Download's last line sat exactly on the viewport bottom (0px margin),\nand at 768px, the project detail's last line went **17px behind** the bottom tab bar (project list had 9px margin). The touch contract's \"blocked by tab bar is a defect\" reappeared in this form.\n\nThe prescription is **the shell declares it once** — direct children of the body slot are not compressed.\nForcing pages to remember `shrink-0` actually failed: after fixing one screen, the same defect persisted across four sibling routes (project list · project detail · insights · download). The structure pages must remember disappears on the next screen.\n\n- Growing (`grow`) remains unchanged, so vertical centering of short content is **unaffected** (measured: top/bottom margins of centered box 415/415px, identical before/after prescription · screenshot bytes identical).\n- The gate has two layers — `src/app/providers/AppShell.test.tsx` (prescription in place) + `tests/e2e/scroll-end-gap.spec.ts` (measures scroll end margin/tab bar occlusion via **actual layout**). jsdom does not perform layout, so it cannot see pixels.\n\n### History destination tokens (`--git-*`, Workbench redesign 2026-07-27)\n\n`/git` (history) is a destination where **form splits into state**. Since dimensions, not code, support this split, all values are tokens.\n\n| Token | Value | What it defines |\n|---|---|---|\n| `--git-setup-measure` | 520px | Single task column width before connection (no web/folder, before recording starts) |\n| `--git-setup-action-height` | 36px (coarse 44px) | Primary/secondary action row height |\n| `--git-evidence-min` | 600px | Minimum evidence column width. 11px mono 80 columns ≈ 528 + gutter + padding |\n| `--git-evidence-stack-max` | 460px | Upper bound for vertically stacked evidence (scrolls within) |\n| `--git-row-h` | 26px (coarse 44px) | Change row height — content cannot dictate this as it's a repeating set |\n| `--git-step-h` | 44px | Step row height (summary + name, two lines) |\n| `--git-row-stagger` | 14ms | List appearance stagger interval. Max 8 rows → total delay ≤112ms |\n| `--git-single-measure` | 920px | Single column width when no evidence column is present |\n\n**Three contracts matter more than values.**\n\n1. **Column existence promises content existence.** The evidence column renders only when there are changed lines to show or past steps. Old code unconditionally declared 2 columns, leaving the right side with just one line while a vertical divider stretched to the screen edge (1512×950 measured: right valid ink 1 row / empty height 1,010px). **The answer for empty columns is not to fill them, but not to create them.**\n2. **Work area height is `min(content, remaining space)`.** Flex child default (`0 1 auto`) + `min-h-0` expresses this. Using `flex-1` creates a 500px empty gap with no one filling it in short lists. Columns scroll inside only when overflowing.\n3. **The 2-column gate is `xl` (1280)** — enabling 2 columns at `lg` (1024) consumes 600px for the evidence column, crushing the list to 430px and truncating concept names. **Truncated lists are not decision material** (just as truncated diffs are not evidence). 1024–1279 stacks vertically.\n\n### App-embedded terminal dock tokens — Removed (2026-07-26)\n\nThe `--terminal-*` · `--agent-terminal-*` token group and `.agent-terminal-dock` surface were removed along with the bottom terminal dock. The rationale is in the reversal record section of `docs/AGENT-GRAPH-WORKFLOW.md` — the dock was a proper subset of the user's own terminal, and the sole advantage cited, \"the map reacts when the agent fixes it,\" was already provided by the vault (user-chosen markdown folder) watcher regardless of location.\n\n**Do not revive it.** If we must recreate cell typo·ANSI palette·grip width tokens here, it means the dock has returned, and that decision must be reversed first. Values are available in git history if needed.\n\n## Category differentiation strategy\n\nDifferentiate by **border style**, not color — the only color (indigo) is reserved for hub nodes:\n\n| Category           | Marker                                    |\n| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |\n| In progress        | Indigo underline                          |\n| Planned            | Dashed border                             |\n| Hub (IAM/Reactor)  | Indigo background and border (only color) |\n\n## Product Surface Hierarchy\n\nOperational pages should expose intent before visual flourish:\n\n1. **Primary task** — what the user can do on this screen now.\n2. **Graph evidence** — node count, relation count, warnings, health, or query\n   packet readiness.\n3. **Next graph action** — Workshop for a frontmatter-backed write, Insights\n   for maintenance, or Topology for spatial/path inspection.\n\nAvoid making large explanatory panels the first thing users read. Prefer compact\naction and handoff strips that name a concrete destination (`Check in map`,\n`Edit relation`, `Concept doc`, `Copy next action`) and why it is useful. The retired\n`Browse / Write / Query` cards, tree/ego hub, ERD Builder rails, and query\ncockpit are not current chrome and must not be revived by documentation or\ndesign guards.\n\nTopology is the browse and decision surface. Its INDEX panel may project the\nproject → domain → capability → element hierarchy, but the canvas and\ndatasheet keep typed relations, evidence, and impact visible. Selecting a row\nor node must preserve one canonical graph handle across map focus, detail,\nWorkshop deep-link, and source-document handoff. `/ontology` is only a\ncompatibility redirect to `/topology?index=expanded`; do not design a second\nontology hub behind it.\n\nWorkshop is the write surface. The center card plus fixed compass bearings\nexplain the current node and allowed relation directions; empty line-art\nsockets invite one relation at a time. A writable vault lands real\nfrontmatter, while a read-only vault produces an MCP packet. Completion is the\ncenter-card border and plain progress caption, not game reward, glow, loot, or\na hidden draft canvas. `/ontology/edit` is only a compatibility redirect to\nthis surface.\n\nInsights is a maintenance board, not a generic analytics dashboard. Its exact\nfive questions are **Do next / Composition / Connections / Boundaries /\nFreshness**. `?tab=` restores the selected question, `TabBar` exposes one\nselected tab, and only the matching `tabpanel` is visible. The first viewport\nshould answer the selected question with real graph data; the bottom handoff\nrow copies the matching MCP/CLI action without making raw query syntax the\nvisual winner. A fixed three-tab dashboard, reader-persona lanes, or a large\nquery cockpit is retired structure.\n\nSource/setup surfaces should expose the vault execution contract before setup\nactions. Use compact `Files` / `Graph` / `Agent` cells to show that local\nmarkdown remains the source of truth, frontmatter compiles into graph/query\nsurfaces, and MCP agents read the same vault. Action cards can follow, but the\nfirst native-app entry must make the ontology workbench contract clearer than\nthe document-editor mechanics. The `Agent` cell should expose a copyable graph\nDB runtime gate, so Source Vault can prove the same read-first agent loop\nwithout sending the user to a deeper panel first. Its visible replay markers\nshould name `relation_name_parity` and `pattern_walk` / `project_map`, so the\nsource route reads as the start of graph verification rather than a document\nreader with an agent button.\nThe global entry label and page header for `/docs` should say `Source` /\n`Source Vault`, not `Docs`, because that route is the local markdown source and\nagent setup surface for the graph. First-viewport counts and vault badges should\nsay `source records` / `records`, not `docs`. Keep `document` language for\nindividual markdown files and evidence rows, but avoid making the route identity\nread like a documentation portal. Palette groups, search sections, empty-state\nprompts, and tree navigation labels should say `Source records` / `Source tree`\nwhen they name the surface rather than one specific markdown file.\n\n## Topology node focus & scale (ego popover)\n\nFull spec + cited references: [`TOPOLOGY-FOCUS-AND-SCALE.md`](./TOPOLOGY-FOCUS-AND-SCALE.md).\nThe graph view obeys the infovis mantra *overview first, zoom and filter, then\ndetails-on-demand* — not the inverse (everything-at-once + fullscreen-on-click).\n\n- **Click = ego focus + compact popover, not a fullscreen modal.** Clicking a\n  node keeps the node and its direct neighbors (its `ego` subgraph) at full\n  opacity and dims the rest through `topology-map-v2`'s `focus-state` world\n  derivation; the source graph is not mutated. A content-sized\n  `TopologyV2DetailPanel` anchors near the node and lists connected nodes as\n  incremental ego-walk targets. `FullDetailA1` remains an opt-in full-detail\n  drill, not the click default.\n- **Card count chips are topology marks.** `--topology-card-count-surface` /\n  `--topology-card-count-border` / `--topology-card-count-text` make each\n  visible skeleton card's count read as node scale, not incidental metadata.\n  Keep the chip compact and token-backed so card width remains stable while\n  important anchors expose why they matter on the map.\n- **Default view is an overview, not the full graph.** Show `project` + `domain`\n  + hub nodes at level 0; reveal a domain's members on demand (semantic zoom).\n  Never drop the full 2–3k-node hairball on the user uninvited.\n- **Plain language over graph jargon.** `Affected N` → \"Used by N\";\n  `Dependencies N` → \"Required items N\". No duplicated labels\n  (`Concept information` ×3).\n- **Scale path is evidence-gated.** The current canvas uses a deterministic\n  semantic skeleton, tier reveal, density-gate cluster chips, label collision\n  suppression, viewport pass-through edge demotion, and focus/realm filters\n  before drawing more detail. Do not claim a 10k-node capacity from the retired\n  Sigma/WebGL stack; publish a new upper bound only after production\n  canvas-2D measurements at the stated viewport and interaction.\n- **Canvas palette tokens.** The only current map-layer token source is\n  `src/widgets/topology-map-v2/tokens/read-topology-v2-tokens.ts`. Dark overview\n  edges stay quiet enough for dense vaults while containment, dependency,\n  dimmed, hovered, and selected relations remain distinct semantic layers.\n  There is no `topology-map-sigma` palette or WebGL reducer contract.\n\nThis serves the new \"topology\" row in the cited-lineage table above.\n\n## Anti-AI Design Criteria\n\nAnti-AI design does not mean colorless UI. It means every visual decision has a\njob that a local-first ontology workbench needs, and nothing is added just to\nlook generated, glossy, or broadly SaaS-like.\n\nApply these checks before shipping ontology surfaces:\n\n- **Color is a keyed data mark, not atmosphere.** Kind color may identify\n  `project` / `domain` / `capability` / `element` / `unknown`, but the surface\n  must also show a label, icon, size, position, or legend. This follows WCAG\n  2.2 SC 1.4.1 and Apple HIG color guidance: do not rely on color alone.\n- **Color area stays proportional to evidence value.** Graph marks can use\n  high-contrast fills because they are small data points; panels and cards use\n  neutral surfaces, compact swatches / markers, and low-alpha borders. Avoid\n  full-height colored rails inside detail cards; they read as decorative\n  generated-callout chrome before they explain the data.\n- **Qualitative, not theatrical.** Kind colors are nominal categories, so they\n  use a quiet qualitative palette in the ColorBrewer sense. Avoid neon yellow,\n  magenta, or over-saturated \"AI dashboard\" tones when label/icon/shape can do\n  the separation work.\n- **No generated-gloss signals.** Decorative gradients, glass blur, glow rings,\n  aurora backgrounds, oversized rounded cards, and scale-hover motion are\n  regressions unless a specific native-system state requires them.\n- **Craft is verified in small contracts.** The design drift guard must catch\n  forbidden patterns, focused tests must lock role labels and tone attributes,\n  and browser/native verification must prove the UI reads as a workbench rather\n  than a decorative demo.\n- **No floating-box soup.** A screen with several unrelated cards, popovers,\n  prompts, minimaps, HUD buttons, and inspectors visible at the same visual\n  weight is not \"rich\"; it is an attention failure. One surface owns the\n  current action, support surfaces stay visibly weaker, and blocking surfaces\n  dim or suppress the rest.\n- **No stacked transient UI.** Popovers, context menus, hover previews, and\n  selected cards may not cascade as unrelated layers. Opening a new transient\n  surface closes the previous unrelated one; opening a composer/modal demotes\n  or closes transient surfaces and blocks parent-map interaction.\n- **No tokenless positioning.** Panel width, radius, padding, shadow, elevation,\n  z-order intent, and topology motion must use named tokens or marker-backed\n  contracts. One-off `clamp(...)`, shadow, or easing values in JSX are treated\n  as design debt unless the same change adds a token and verifier.\n- **No modal without modality.** A write composer, destructive confirm, or\n  decision dialog must visibly separate itself from the map through a dim,\n  scrim, or blocked interaction state. If the background still appears equally\n  actionable, the modal/composer fails.\n- **No elevation noise.** More shadow does not mean more hierarchy. Elevation\n  must describe map/support/focus/transient/blocking layer order consistently\n  (dark theme only — light mode was retired 2026-07-19).\n\nReference anchors:\n\n- Apple HIG Color: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color\n- Apple HIG Modality: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/modality\n- Apple HIG Sheets: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets\n- Apple HIG Layout: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout\n- Fluent 2 Layout: https://fluent2.microsoft.design/layout\n- Fluent 2 Design Tokens: https://fluent2.microsoft.design/design-tokens\n- Material Design Dialogs: https://m2.material.io/components/dialogs\n- WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 / 1.4.11: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/\n- W3C Understanding SC 1.4.11: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast\n- ColorBrewer scheme types: https://colorbrewer2.org/learnmore/schemes_full.html\n- Linear, \"Why is quality so rare?\": https://linear.app/now/why-is-quality-so-rare\n\n## Absolute rules (Don'ts)\n\n> **This list is the single source of truth** (2026-08-05). The same list existed in three places, and **none of them matched**: `.claude/rules/forbidden.md` had 9 of the union's 15 items, `.claude/rules/design.md` had only 8, and each contained one item the other lacked. There was no gate to reconcile the three copies.\n>\n> Now **this is the only source of truth**, and other files do not copy it:\n>\n> - `.claude/rules/forbidden.md` — An **intended subset** that contains only «judgments to make before opening a file» because it is **resident** (rendered every turn). Writing items here that are not in this list will be blocked by the gate.\n> - `.claude/rules/design.md` — Does not hold a list but **points to** one (the way the `Node specs` section already works).\n>\n> The `dont:` HTML comments at the end of each item are **keys for machines to match pairs**, not sentences for humans to read. You may freely rewrite or translate the sentence, but leave the key unchanged — this avoids the trap where «improving the document's expression breaks the test» (`documentation.md`). Gate:\n> `tests/contract/design-donts-parity.contract.test.ts`.\n\n- ❌ Clicking a topology node opening a fullscreen/full-bleed detail modal — the\n  default is ego focus + a compact popover anchored to the node; full detail is\n  opt-in from inside that popover (see \"Topology node focus & scale\" above)\n  <!--dont:node-click-fullscreen-modal-->\n- ❌ Purple → pink gradients <!--dont:purple-pink-gradient-->\n- ❌ Glassmorphism (`backdrop-blur`) <!--dont:glassmorphism-->\n- ❌ Glow pulse / neon effects <!--dont:glow-pulse-neon-->\n- ❌ Glow-like `boxShadow: \\`0 0 ...\\`` rings on ontology operation surfaces\n  <!--dont:glow-boxshadow-ring-->\n- ❌ Animated gradient backgrounds / aurora <!--dont:animated-gradient-bg-->\n  - **One explicit exception (2026-08-18): Gateway current field** — Three low-luminance accent radial light sources floating very slowly in the background of the gateway (`/` gateway face · `/download`). It lives only on one surface in `src/views/download/ui/GatewayFx.tsx` (gateway FX sealed namespace) and is an exception only when all four conditions are met:\n    **Alpha cap** (light source 0.14 · grain 0.05 — locked by token) · **First 1s pause** (background does not interfere with headline appearance) · **Full stop for reduced-motion** (does not run the rAF loop itself) · **Accent tokens only** (reads `--color-indigo-brand` without refreshing hue — automatically follows accent transitions).\n    Two gates: `eslint.config.mjs`'s gateway-fx scope selector (locks consumers to `src/views/download/**`) +\n    `tests/contract/gateway-fx-exception.contract.test.ts` (single consumer · alpha cap · reduced-motion stop · documented listing). Expanding to other app screens like workbench or document room remains forbidden. Ledger: `docs/DECISIONS.md` (69).\n- ❌ Scale-based hover effects <!--dont:scale-hover-->\n- ❌ More than one color system <!--dont:multi-color-system-->\n- ❌ Floating-box soup: unrelated panels/popovers/HUD/minimap/cards at equal\n  visual weight <!--dont:floating-box-soup-->\n- ❌ Stacked popovers or popover-over-modal without closing/dimming the previous\n  surface <!--dont:stacked-popover-->\n- ❌ Blocking composer/modal without dim, scrim, or suppressed parent\n  interaction <!--dont:modal-without-dim-->\n- ❌ One-off topology `clamp(...)`, shadow, radius, z-order, easing, or duration\n  without a `--topology-*` token and verifier marker\n  <!--dont:oneoff-topology-value-->\n- ❌ Overlap tolerated because the surface \"mostly still works\"; overlap count\n  must be `0` for fixed/card surfaces in the tested state\n  <!--dont:overlap-tolerated-->\n- ❌ Decorative arrows trailing a label — `Open →`, `Details →`, or a trailing\n  `ArrowRight`/`ArrowUpRight` glyph after link/button text (see\n  \"Arrows carry information or they don't ship\" below)\n  <!--dont:decorative-trailing-arrow-->\n- ❌ Cards in one grid whose height is decided by how much text each happens to\n  contain (see \"Dimensional regularity\" below)\n  <!--dont:content-decided-card-height-->\n\n## Arrows carry information or they don't ship\n\nOwner verdict, 2026-07-26, on seeing `Open from map →`:\n\n> *\"I don't like arrows next to text like that? It feels AI-ish.\"*\n\nA trailing arrow after a link label adds no information. The label already says\nwhere you're going, and the control already looks like a control. What the arrow\nactually signals is *generated marketing chrome* — it's the visual tic of a\nlanding page that wants you to click something.
