On a workbench where the same\nlabel appears a dozen times, it becomes noise a dozen times over.\n\n**The rule is not \"no arrows.\"** It's that an arrow must be carrying something\nthe words aren't:\n\n| Allowed — the arrow *is* the data | Forbidden — the arrow is decoration |\n| --- | --- |\n| `{source} → {target}` — a path between two nodes | `Open Document →` |\n| `Old → Recent` — an ordering | `Details →` |\n| `Settings → Developer` — a menu path to follow | `View Details` |\n| `Click TOC → jump to location` — cause and effect | label + trailing `ArrowRight` icon |\n| Leading `↗` on a link that **leaves the app** (`target=\"_blank\"`, an external deeplink) — it warns before the click | Trailing `↗` on in-app navigation |\n| `ChevronRight`/`ChevronDown` as a disclosure state, or prev/next on a carousel | |\n\nThe test: **remove the arrow and read the label aloud. If nothing was lost, it\nwas decoration.**\n\n### The gate has to reach the markup, not just the strings\n\n`tests/contract/label-decoration.contract.test.ts` scans three things now, and\nthe third one was added because the first two were not enough:\n\n1. every `messages/*.json` string, for a trailing arrow;\n2. a bare `↗` in JSX, unless the element declares `data-external-link-marker`;\n3. **a lone arrow element that sits at the end of a label** — matched by what\n   follows it, not by which glyph it is.\n\n(3) exists because the rule shipped on 2026-07-26 exempted `→` wholesale, on the\ngrounds that every standalone `→` in this repo was an infix data arrow. One day\nlater the workshop's primary save button read `Confirm and Save <span>→</span>` —\nthe repo that wrote the rule broke it, under its own exemption. **A rule whose\nrange is too short fails exactly like no rule at all.**\n\nThe exemption is gone; the discrimination moved to position. An arrow element\nwhose next non-whitespace sibling is the parent's closing tag is trailing\n(decoration); anything else after it means the arrow sits between two things\n(data). Measured before enabling, as `.claude/rules/design.md` requires: 3\ntrailing (all the same save-button family) and 7 infix across `src` + `app`.\n\n## Dimensional regularity — when content length varies\n\nOwner verdict, 2026-07-26, on a card grid whose rows didn't line up:\n\n> *\"The box sizes don't match? It doesn't look clean, it looks crooked… I prefer neatness.\"*\n\nThis is the recurring failure mode of a data-driven UI: the layout is regular in\nthe code and irregular on screen, because each card's height is decided by how\nmany words its content happened to have. A grid only reads as a grid when the\neye can find a repeating rhythm; content-driven height destroys that rhythm\nwithout anyone having chosen it.\n\n**The principle: the container's dimensions are a design decision, not a\nbyproduct of its contents.** Concretely:\n\n- **Fix the anatomy, not just the box.** A card in a repeating set has the same\n  named slots in the same order — head / measure / list / foot. A slot that is\n  sometimes absent is worse than a slot that is sometimes empty, because absence\n  moves everything below it.\n- **Reserve the optional clause's space.** If a caption is sometimes\n  `2 elements` and sometimes `2 elements · 1 more competency`, the caption line still\n  occupies one line either way. Do not let an optional clause change the card's\n  height.\n- **Truncate list slots to a fixed count.** Show N items and a remainder\n  caption — never \"however many fit.\" N is a design decision made once.\n- **Equalize rows, not just columns.** CSS Grid stretches items within a row by\n  default, so cards in the same row already match; rows do not match each other.\n  When the set is meant to read as one field, make the row height uniform.\n- **Truncation is a layout tool, not a failure.** Long titles clamp; they do not\n  get to reflow the grid. Pair every clamp with the full value on hover/focus or\n  in the detail surface, so nothing is actually lost.\n\nThe cost is real and must be paid knowingly: reserved slots create visible empty\nspace in small vaults. Accept that cost only where the set is genuinely a\nrepeating field the eye scans. **A one-off card should size to its content** —\nregularity is for repetition.\n\n> There is no carve-out. Every Don't above holds **app-wide, including the\n> contextual editor and change-review surfaces**.\n\n## Contextual ontology writing; Studio surface retired 2026-08-21\n\n`/topology` is the vault's visual read/write workbench. A selected node's\ninspector swaps at the same anchor into a one-relation editor; creation and ACP\nwrites use the same typed pre-write review. `/ontology/studio` is a compatibility\nredirect and has no rail item, dedicated UI, or design-token namespace.\n\nThe removed Studio once carried a **game-energy exception** (a node as a hexagon\n\"item\" you socket meaning-\"gems\" into: focal glow, gold rarity, light rays,\nparticles, gradient frames). **That exception is retired.**\n\n**Why it was retired (fable verdict B + owner, 2026-07-24):** \"Make it addictive like a game\" was a *metaphor*, not a spec. Rendering loot-game aesthetics inside an\napp whose identity is Rams/Linear restraint read as \"restraint cosplaying a\ngame,\" not a finished game — and this surface is **decision material** (planners,\nexecs, developers, agents read it), where rarity glow *erodes trust*. Scoping\nthe energy to `--studio-*` tokens was itself an admission that it could never\nfully commit. The exception was a considered mistake; removing it makes the\nworkshop finally look like this app.\n\n**What replaced it (restrained, full charter):**\n\n- **One relation at a time.** Type, target, and rationale sit in the compact\n  contextual editor; there is no radial stage or second dock.\n- **The map is the preview.** A dashed arrow uses live endpoint geometry without\n  entering force/layout input. A target hidden by density gating is temporarily\n  rendered at its real coordinate with its label; its surrounding graph stays\n  folded. Relation text and the arrow shape keep colour from becoming the only\n  channel.\n- **Review before bytes.** `OntologyChangeReview` shows exact fields before\n  `createDoc`/`updateFrontmatter` or ACP `allow_once`. Semantic writes never show\n  `allow_always`.\n- **Motion uses the existing three-step ramp.** inspector/editor swap=`base`,\n  cancel=`fast`, confirmed dashed↔solid crossfade=`settle`; no bounce, glow, or\n  camera jump. Reduced motion snaps the canvas state and adds no settle delay.\n- **The editor owns enough map.** INDEX folds only while `workbench=edit` is\n  active and restores afterward; at 1024px the measured center map gap stays at\n  least 480px. Below `lg`, one centered sheet stays above the bottom-tab reserve.\n\nThe following bullets describe the retired Compass shape for historical design\ncomparison, not current implementation:\n\n- **Compass Stage.** The focal node is the center hero card; relation *types* are\n  nailed to fixed bearings — UP = Superordinate concept (is_a), DOWN = Subordinate item (contains), RIGHT = Required item (depends), LEFT = Related item (relates). Filled = solid indigo\n  strut + satellite card; missing = a **dashed line-art socket** (not a jewel)\n  you fill via an inline anchored picker.\n- **Recorded/open directions**, not completeness, read from the center card's\n  4-side border (dashed = open, solid = recorded) + a plain caption\n  (\"2 of 4 directions recorded\") + a top-left relation-map cue (mini compass). An empty\n  direction is not automatically missing meaning. No floating % ring, no levels,\n  no rarity.\n- **Color:** achromatic + single indigo, exactly like the rest of the app.\n  Indigo `recommended` and amber `expected` are allowed only with a candidate-\n  specific receipt containing rationale, evidence references, and a matching\n  safe-to-add relation preflight. The current graph projection supplies no such\n  receipt, so empty sockets are neutral. **No glow / gradient / gem / particle /\n  gold.**\n- **One calm frame prompt** + plain-language socket questions (\"What kind of thing is this node?\") — zero ontology jargon on the surface. A neutral socket says\n  that no recommendation evidence exists; it remains clickable. `is_a` keeps\n  same-kind candidates in Browse but does not rank topology/name proximity as a\n  semantic recommendation.\n- **Motion:** one interruptible ~200ms opacity/color confirm when a socket fills\n  (dashed → solid); `prefers-reduced-motion` → instant. No ambient motion.\n- **Enhance vs Create** are the same surface in different fill-states (no mode\n  tabs). Enhance = partially filled existing node (`?node=`); Create\n  (`?mode=create`) = all-empty draft card.\n\nThe `--studio-*` token block and every `.studio-*` motion class are **removed\nfrom `app/globals.css`**. is_a remains a real writable relation via the `broader`\n(SKOS) frontmatter key (derive → `is_a` edge; registered in mcp/cli schema +\nvalidator). Addictiveness comes from the **loop** (next action → immediate\nreflection → accumulating progress), not from bling — Duolingo/Oura/Linear make\n\"one more\" with zero glow. design-guardian now rejects glow/rarity/particle on\nthis surface too. Full history + KEEP/KILL/BUILD: session memory\n`ontology-studio-game-direction`.\n\n## Motion principles\n\n- Initial load: `opacity 0 → 1` + `translateY 8px → 0` (spring)\n- Hover: border opacity rises, connected edges brighten — no scale or glow\n- Drawer: right-side `x: 100% → 0` spring\n- Filter toggle: deselected categories fade to `opacity 0.15`\n- Background: fully static\n- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`\n\n## Page header — English caption + Korean h1\n\nThe header on each operations page (currently `/ontology/insights`) follows a **two-line pattern**. The user-facing Korean title is the primary heading, and the English category caption serves as a micro identifier that yields one step in the visual hierarchy.\n\n### Pattern\n\n```\n[English category caption — text-caption / mono / uppercase / tracking-caption / quaternary color]\n[Korean h1 — text-display / signature weight / primary color]\n[Subtitle — Korean / text-body-lg / secondary color (optional)]\n```\n\nExample: `/ontology` page\n\n```tsx\n<p className=\"font-mono text-caption uppercase tracking-[0.18em] text-[color:var(--color-text-quaternary)]\">\n  Ontology\n</p>\n<h1 className=\"text-display font-[var(--font-weight-signature)]\">\n  Ontology Tree\n</h1>\n<p className=\"text-body-lg text-[color:var(--color-text-secondary)]\">\n  Approved nodes and relationships …\n</p>\n```\n\n> This snippet was corrected to use ramp utilities on 2026-08-04. The previous example\n> showed `text-2xl`/`text-sm`/`text-[10px]` as-is, but while the code zeroed those values,\n> **the document was teaching off-ramp values to the next person**.\n\n### Intent\n\n- **English caption** — A category-area identifier for the page. The mono + uppercase + spacing combo enables fast visual recognition of \"where you are,\" but stays weaker than the main heading so the Korean h1 reads first.\n- **Korean h1** — The name users actually call it. Korean is the primary heading, so all body copy / descriptions / CTAs maintain a consistent Korean tone.\n- **Two-line separation** — Mixing English and Korean on a single line (e.g. \"Ontology\") is forbidden. Each line stays in a single language with a single tone.\n\n### Legitimate English caption examples\n\n- Page categories: `Ontology`, `Workspace`, `Manual node`, `Get started`.\n- System metadata: `ID Recommendation`, `Beta`, etc. — only intentional English identifiers. Sentence-style English is forbidden (translate to Korean).\n\n### Consistency rules\n\n- Caption font size stays in the `9px ~ 10px` range. Tracking ranges from `0.10em ~ 0.18em`.\n- Within a single page, keep caption tokens consistent (mono / uppercase / tracking / color). System tokens will eventually be unified under a CSS var like `--font-caption-mono`.\n- Use the English caption only once per page (top header). Don't repeat English category labels in the body — avoid duplicating the visual hierarchy.\n\n### Surfaces where this applies (current)\n\n`/ontology/insights` — follows this pattern. (`/ontology/edit`, the ERD builder,\nwas retired 2026-07-24 → it now redirects to `/ontology/studio`, the workshop (Compass Stage).)\n\nThe public surfaces `/`, `/topology`, `/docs`, `/projects`, `/project/[slug]` use the standalone Korean h1 pattern (without an English eyebrow caption) — these are the browse surfaces, not the operations surfaces.\n\n## Geometry & Type Codex (R5, 2026-07)\n\n> **Specify every box's size down to the pixel, identical everywhere.** This section is a **codebook** pinning text size, radius, and padding to token names. Value source:\n> `app/globals.css` `@theme` \"Geometry & Type Codex\" block. Off-ramp\n> literal `text-[Npx]` / `rounded-[Npx]` below are **forbidden** — if a new value is needed,\n> add it only via a PR creating a new token (do not sneak in inline arbitrary values).\n\n**Empirical basis (before substitution, 2026-07):** `text-[Npx]` hardcoding **29 size variants · 1,184 instances**,\narbitrary radius **18 variants**, card padding 4 variants. This dispersion was converged to the ramp below.\n\n### Type ramp — 7 steps\n\nTailwind v4 `--text-*` namespace creates `text-<step>` font-size utilities. Letter-spacing is managed **separately** via `--tracking-*` pairs —\nif auto-combined with `text-<step>`, ~1,000 elements' tracking would change at once,\nbraking the \"codification redesign\" principle. New code must pair them together (Apple optical principle: small steps get positive tracking for legibility, large steps get negative tracking for cohesion).\n\n| Row | Token (utility) | px | Tracking pair (utility) | Target |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| caption | `--text-caption` (`text-caption`) | 9.5 | `+0.04em` (`tracking-caption`) | micro-labels, legends, timestamps |\n| label | `--text-label` (`text-label`) | 11 | `+0.02em` (`tracking-label`) | chips, badges, secondary labels |\n| body | `--text-body` (`text-body`) | 12.5 | `+0.005em` (`tracking-body`) | default body text, list rows |\n| body-lg | `--text-body-lg` (`text-body-lg`) | 14 | `0` (`tracking-body-lg`) | emphasized body text, subtitles |\n| title | `--text-title` (`text-title`) | 16 | `-0.01em` (`tracking-title`) | panel/card titles |\n| display | `--text-display` (`text-display`) | 23 | `-0.022em` (`tracking-display`) | page headlines |\n| hero | `--text-hero` (`text-hero`) | 30 | (no tracking pair — only use explicit tracking when consumption is specified) | hero headline |\n| hero-lg | `--text-hero-lg` (`text-hero-lg`) | 34 | (no tracking pair — legacy `tracking-hero` retired to consumption 0 on 2026-08-18) | legacy gateway headline — the top-of-page text from when maps covered the full screen |\n| monument | `--text-monument` (`text-monument`) | clamp(40, 5.8cqw, 96) | `-0.018em` (`tracking-monument`) | **Gateway Monument Headline** (remade on 2026-08-18) — the sole slot where typography takes over as maps leave the first screen. Line-height pair is ratio `--leading-monument` (1.08); since it uses clamp, creating px pairs would require size-specific tokens (display-tight class). |\n\n**Closest-convergence rule** (on substitution): Snap each literal px to the nearest step\n(±1px absorbed by ramp). Exactly between steps (e.g. 15px) goes to the upper step; off-ramp values (≥1.5px deviation) remain only via \"explicit exceptions\" below.\n\n**Calling a non-existent step renders at root 16px** (recorded 2026-07-27). Since Tailwind\ncreates no class for undefined steps, names not in the ramp like `text-large` are **syntactically valid but apply no size**. This is invisible to any value checker — non-existent things leave no hardcoding literals either,\nfalling outside `type-ramp-coverage`'s view, and tsc/eslint do not check strings.\nTwo empirical cases existed: `text-callout` (found manually in #618), `text-large`\n(node name on workshop center card — the screen's protagonist was only 1.28x larger than satellite card names at 12.5px. Converged to `text-display` on 2026-07-27).\n\nThe gate is `tests/contract/type-ramp-step-defined.contract.test.ts`. **Why not ESLint**: The judgment requires the actual token list from `app/globals.css`, but `no-restricted-syntax` uses AST selectors and cannot reference other files.\nCopying step names into the rule would cause that copy to drift from the ramp, making the gate blind to its own gaps. So we build it as a contract test that reads the source to judge.\n\nIf a new step is truly needed, do all three in one PR: ① Ramp in `app/globals.css` ② Table in this doc ③ Registration in `src/shared/lib/cn.ts`.\n\n### Line-height ramp — 9 steps (2026-07-27)\n\nTailwind v4's `--leading-*` namespace creates `leading-<step>` utilities.\n**Line-height is not an independent ramp but a pair of size** — the repo's\nreal data says so: the trend for named utilities is already fixed px (`leading-4/5/6` = 16/20/24px,\n121 instances), and the scale-fixed contract has already codified one pair (Chrome label 11px + 16px line-height).\nThis aligns with the dimensional regularity charter — **line-height is the seed of line height**\nso it must be fixed in px so that the rhythm of repeated card sets does not depend on character count or language.\n\nThe values are on a 2px grid, and the three pairs (label 16 · body 20 · title 24) already have\nthe **same values** as the previously used\n`leading-4/5/6`. This is not a new specification but merely naming what is already the trend.\n\n| slot | token (util) | value | pair (font) | ratio | usage — when to choose this line-height |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| caption | `--leading-caption` (`leading-caption`) | 14px | caption 9.5 | 1.47 | micro-labels, transcripts, 9–10px secondary text |\n| label | `--leading-label` (`leading-label`) | 16px | label 11 | 1.45 | chips, badges, chrome labels, card descriptions. **The locked contract of 16px** |\n| body | `--leading-body` (`leading-body`) | 20px | body 12.5 | 1.60 | default body text, list rows, panel paragraphs, TOC rows |\n| body-lg | `--leading-body-lg` (`leading-body-lg`) | 22px | body-lg 14 | 1.57 | emphasized body text, subtitles |\n| title | `--leading-title` (`leading-title`) | 24px | title 16 | 1.50 | panel/card titles |\n| display | `--leading-display` (`leading-display`) | 28px | display 23 | 1.22 | page headlines (wrappable) |\n| hero | `--leading-hero` (`leading-hero`) | 34px | hero 30 | 1.13 | hero headlines (wrappable) |\n| hero-lg | `--leading-hero-lg` (`leading-hero-lg`) | 38px | hero-lg 34 | 1.12 | gateway headlines (max 2 lines) |\n| display-tight | `--leading-display-tight` (`leading-display-tight`) | 1.06 | free | — | **Slots read as a single block** — hero/section titles, card names, large numbers. **Max 2 lines** |\n| prose | `--leading-prose` (`leading-prose`) | 1.7 | free | — | **User-written text** — markdown viewer/editor, detailed body, pre. Upper bound for long reading widths |\n\n**One-line verdict**: If the app's UI text, use the **pair** of that size; if user-written text, use\n**prose**; if names/numbers, use **display-tight**.\n\n**Reason for only 2 free steps being out of bounds**: These two are steps that overlay sizes outside the ramp (`clamp()` hero,\nnested sizes inside markdown), so fixing them in px would require tokens for each size. The ratio is the intent (cohesion/relaxation) here.\n\n**Boundary of display-tight**: Using it on text or sentences stacking 3+ lines (descriptions/body) is a defect — Korean characters have top-line final consonants and bottom-line initial consonants that touch. Up to 2 lines is allowed (the download hero uses `<br />` for 2 lines in real usage).\n\n**Korean sets the upper limit of values.** Korean fills the character box tighter than Latin, so the same\nline-height looks denser. Thus, shared ramp values are set to **the spacing Korean requires**, and Latin follows that spacing (Latin is generous with wide line-heights, but Korean is not generous with narrow ones). **No locale branching** — apps mix two languages in one paragraph (Korean vault data within an en UI), so branching would disrupt the line height of the same paragraph.\n\n**Must register with tailwind-merge.** If you don't register the step in `LEADING_RAMP_STEPS` of `cn.ts`, classes won't be dropped, but **conflict merging won't occur** — both survive in `cn('leading-body', cond && 'leading-prose')` and CSS source order decides the winner. It's quieter than size ramp drop accidents, so you can't find the cause even by looking at the screen. Gate: `cn.test.ts`.\n\n**Companion auto-binding — enabled (B2, 2026-07-27).** Defined `--text-<step>--line-height` for all 7 steps in Tailwind v4, so one `text-<step>` carries line-height. This binding is necessary to close the spec — if you only define pairs, **places without line-height classes** remain outside the spec and render with inherited 1.5, and hardcoding checks/ratchets can't see *missing\nclasses* (a blind spot similar to unregistered steps quietly rendering at root 16px). 927 instances were in that state.\n\nRadius measured before/after with the same conditions (1512×950 dark · ko/en · 8 screens) before enabling:\n\n| character | count | line-height |\n|---|---|---|\n| 9.5px caption | 94 | 14.25 → **14** (−0.25) |\n| 11px label | 186 | 16.5 → **16** (−0.5) |\n| 12.5px body | 70 | 18.75 → **20** (+1.25) |\n| 14px body-lg | 30 | 21 → **22** (+1.0) |\n| 23px display | 8 | 34.5 → **28** (−6.5) |\n\nOf 746 elements, 388 changed, and of those, **380 had |Δ| ≤ 1.25px** — mostly one-line\nchips/labels so pixels don't even move. **Only 8 places had box height changes ≥ 2px**, all page headlines (`/projects` · `/ontology/insights` · `/docs` empty state ·\n`/git`). That 34.5px was a product of inherited 1.5 that no one ever chose, and line height is returned to design decision per the dimensional regularity charter. The 186 labels dropping to\n16px is **the value already codified in the locked contract**, so binding doesn't violate the contract but converges 186 places to the value the contract states.\n\n**Since font-size doesn't change at all, line breaks cannot theoretically increase.** Zero places where repeated card set uniform height broke (line-height is determined only by size, so one set moves together). Same 8 places + 1 two-line label (42 → 44px) even at 1024·768.\n\n**Explicit `leading-*` wins over companion** — the explicit classes laid down by B1 in 74 places act as shields. But within `cn()`, **order matters**: tailwind-merge assumes \"size also determines line-height,\" so subsequent `text-<step>` absorbs preceding `leading-*`. Before binding, this assumption was false, and absorbed places quietly fell to inherited 1.5; after binding, it became true. Recommended notation: size first · line-height second. Gate:\n`cn.test.ts`.\n\n**`--leading-hero` creates no pixels today — still kept.** Both 2 call sites of `text-hero` in the repo already have explicit leading attached (`leading-tight` · `leading-display-tight`, both with \"single-line cohesion\" intent written in code). Kept for future: if hero is used without leading later, it will receive **34px** instead of inherited 45px. Removing it would create exceptions where only the top two ramp steps lack pairs; no exceptions is the value of the spec. Don't delete as *\"zero usage so dead token\"* —\n`--pad-panel` precedent (unused tokens are misinformation) differs. That was a value no one used, but this is a value **carried by** the `text-hero` utility.\n\n**`--leading-hero-lg`(38px) has the same status** (new 2026-07-29). The only consumer today, `/download` headline, has explicit `md:leading-hero-lg`, but `--text-hero-lg--line-height` binding is needed to close the ramp top without exceptions.\n\n**Why is hero-lg 34px.** On a surface where maps cover the full screen, a 30px headline competes with background weight. At 34px, the ratio with lead (`text-body` 12.5) becomes **2.72**, falling within the reference hero band (2.5–3.0). Line-height 38px continues the trend of ratios tightening toward the ramp top (1.217 → 1.133 → **1.118**). (Tracking pair `tracking-hero` was re-retired with 0 consumers in the gateway remake on 2026-08-18.)\nPromotion trigger was **the second consumer**: `DesktopVaultWelcome` was already bypassing the ramp with `md:text-[34px]` + eslint-disable.\n\n#### Conditional size trap — new failure mode created by companion binding\n\nAfter binding, **switching only font size conditionally misaligns the pair.** Arbitrary sizes (`text-[Npx]` · `text-[length:…]` · clamp) have no companion, so the original step's line-height remains at that breakpoint too.\n\nFull measurement found 2 instances, actual misalignment 1:\n\n| slot | verdict |\n|---|---|\n| `/git` headline — `text-title` + `sm:text-[length:var(--text-display)]` | ⚠️ **Mismatch.** 23px font with title pair 24px line-height (1.04) — exceeds repo max. Corrected to `sm:text-display` |\n| desktop welcome hero — `text-hero` + `leading-tight` + `md:text-hero-lg` | Safe. **Explicit leading covers both sizes**. (2026-07-29: legacy `md:text-[34px]` + eslint-disable removed as 34px became a ramp step — the moment consumption becomes two places is when to promote the value to a name) |\n\n**How to judge**: If an element has both a ramp size step and conditional arbitrary size,\ncheck if explicit `leading-*` exists. If not, it's a defect. Two ways to fix —\n① Use ramp utilities for conditional sizes too (pairs follow) or ② Attach explicit line-height to directly set both sizes.\n\n**Don't bypass ramp tokens with arbitrary length.**\n`text-[length:var(--text-display)]` looks the same size as `text-display` but **loses the line-height pair**. Arbitrary references for ramp **outside** size tokens (rail labels · Chrome titles etc. dedicated\ntokens) are justified — there is no ramp to bypass.\n\nThe gate has two layers: bypass references are caught by **lint** (`arbitrarySizeSelectors`), and mismatched generic types are caught by **contract tests** (`tests/contract/type-ramp-leading-pair.contract.test.ts`) — the latter requires the entire class of a single element for judgment, which cannot fit into a single AST selector when split by `cn()` arguments.\n\n### Content Icon Ramp — 3 Steps (System Established 2026-08-04)\n\nThe size vocabulary for **content icon glyphs** (lucide) sitting next to body text or labels. The canonical values are `--icon-*` in `app/globals.css`, and the JS mirror for prop channels is `ICON_SIZE` in `src/shared/ui/icon-size.ts` (structured identically to MOTION mirrors — lucide's `size={N}` numeric prop cannot read `var()`).\n\n| Section | Token / Mirror | px | Adjacent Type | Purpose |\n|---|---|---:|---|---|\n| sm | `--icon-sm` / `ICON_SIZE.sm` | 12 | `text-label`(11) · `text-body`(12.5) | **Default.** Glyphs in rows, chips, and buttons (most frequent actual measurement: 77 locations) |\n| md | `--icon-md` / `ICON_SIZE.md` | 14 | `text-body-lg`(14) | Emphasis body text and subtitles |\n| lg | `--icon-lg` / `ICON_SIZE.lg` | 16 | `text-title`(16) | Icon next to title · Standalone icon |\n\n**Why this ramp was created.** The 2026-08-04 real-world test (the first attempt to build a new screen from scratch using this system) empirically revealed holes: content icons were split across **167 call sites** using **9 distinct px values** (10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 + 24 unspecified), with two surfaces mixing 4 values within the same file (Document Palette: 10/11/12/14; Dependency Picker: 10/11/12/13) — this was drift, not role differentiation. Since consumption channels used **JSX numeric props** (`size={N}`) rather than className, the values fell outside lint's scope (the same bug that fractured framer durations). The tester noted while copying sibling components: *\"Nothing told me it had a different value.\"*\n\n**Steps were chosen based on observed frequency + type pairing.** New value 0 — all are dominant values in today's screens, so adding them moves zero pixels. The source of the type-pairing principle is Carbon (verified 2026-08-04, [Icons usage](https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/icons/usage/)): *\"16px and 20px icons are optimized to feel balanced when paired with 14px and 16px IBM Plex\"* — icon steps stand not as independent scales but **paired with type sizes**, and *\"Be sure icon size is consistent throughout your product.\"* The lower bound source is Fluent 2 (verified, [Iconography](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/iconography)): *\"Smaller icons can give information or reinforce an idea, but should not be used for interaction\"* (12px is the lower bound for informational use). Material 3 · Apple HIG (SF Symbols) · Polaris · Primer have body text intended only for JS rendering, making source verification impossible — per precedent #0 in \"Rules for Expanding the System\" (M3/Spectrum 2026-08-03), no sentences citing these four as grounds are included.\n\n**Scope — content icons only.** Chrome and rail icons remain owned by their respective surface contracts: `--topology-chrome-icon-size` (12) · `--chrome-icon` (16) · `--app-nav-rail-icon-size` (20, logo only 26 — fixed scale contract). Overlapping values represent the same answer for the same type pair, but Chrome density decisions must move independently, so they are not bundled.\n\n**The gate is a ratchet, not lint** (`tests/contract/icon-size-ramp.contract.test.ts`): ① CSS ↔ JS mirror consistency ② Per-file ledger for sizes outside the ramp (`size={N}` prop + `size-N`/`h-N w-N` classes) — **new files start at 0 on day one**, existing debt of 64 cases/17 files can only decrease ③ Ratchet for unspecified (default 24px render): 3 cases/2 files ④ Composite probe + dead-code prevention denominator. The reason it's not lint: replacing the 64-case debt implies ±1–2px render changes, requiring design judgment at each site (the founding judgment of the ratchet), and an icon-specific exception block would replace ramp selectors for those files due to flat config multi-block pitfalls.\n\n**Debt repayment is a design pass with before→after tables per site.** Whether 10·11 (44 sites) target sm (12) — and whether micro steps (10 or 11) are separately needed — is judged after screen measurement (queued alongside mono command tag tracking confirmation). Until then, this ramp guarantees only one thing: **newly used icons do not expand the set from 9 to 10.**\n\n#### 2026-08-05 — This ramp had **zero consumers**, and the gate missed 73%\n\nThe above paragraphs were correct but unaware of two things. Upon review in the audit:\n\n1. **The production consumers of `ICON_SIZE` and `--icon-*` were exactly 0.** 216 sites had hardcoded numeric `12`/`14`/`16` values, which happened to match by chance. Defining ramp tokens without anyone referencing them makes them not a spec but **incorrect information** (the same judgment used when this document removed two margin tokens). Now, **313 sites reference `ICON_SIZE`** — moving the value moves the screen.\n2. **The ratchet's scanner only looked at `'lucide-react'` (single quotes).** Of the 99 lucide imports in this repo, **72 use double quotes** — meaning the gate did not exist for **73% of icons**. The empirical debt behind the ledger entry \"64 cases\" is actually **230 cases**. The reason the denominator assertion (`total ≥ 120`) didn't catch this is that counting just the 27 single-quote files exceeds 120 — **not being an empty set is not the same as inspecting the universal set.**\n\n**Paid / Remaining.** I paid the 127 sites where ramp steps were determined without judgment (9·10·11 → sm, 17·18 → lg). The remaining **103 sites are all 13px and 15px**, and since these fall exactly in the middle of two steps (13 → 12|14, 15 → 14|16), \"nearest neighbor\" provides no answer. The ramp's tiebreaker is «paired type», but that type is **completely absent for 59 sites** (icon-only buttons). Since Code Mode cannot generate the value, these are passed to the next pass with per-site tables.\n\n**Source scanning alone does not yield \"0\".** One actual defect in this round was caught in the browser — `BottomTabBar`'s nav icons were **rendering at 17px for 4 instances**, yet source scanning missed them entirely. Icons rendered via runtime variables (`const Icon = item.icon; <Icon size={17} />`) are out of scope because the opening tag name is not in the lucide import set. The adjacent \"Get App\" icon was 16px, so **siblings were misaligned within the same bar**. Hence, we include `svg` empirical measurement every round.\n\n**Two things correctly out of scope** — verified repeatedly during audit, so noted here:\nThe `data-kind-glyph` type markers (11px, etc.) are **typed data marks** owned by the \"Node Spec\" section, and Chrome/rail icons are owned by the surface contract in the paragraph above. Neither is a content icon.\n\n### Radius Ramp — 5 Steps (General Surface)\n\nTailwind v4 `--radius-*` namespace generates `rounded-<step>`.\n\n| Unit | Token (Utility) | px | Target |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| micro | `--radius-micro` (`rounded-micro`) | 4 | Micro badge, command tag, kbd — one layer below the chip |\n| chip | `--radius-chip` (`rounded-chip`) | 6 | Chip, badge, small button |\n| card | `--radius-card` (`rounded-card`) | 9 | Card · Input · Medium Surface |\n| panel | `--radius-panel` (`rounded-panel`) | 12 | Panel, Modal, Large Surface |\n\n| sheet | `--radius-sheet` (`rounded-sheet`) | 18 | Floating sheet/palette — a large temporary surface that floats above the screen and obscures what's below |\n\n**`micro` was added in the 2026-08-03 system establishment.** While the ramp had 3 steps, a 4px radius existed at **96 sites** on screens (59 Tailwind default `rounded-sm` + 37 un-suffixed `rounded`) — micro badges, command tags, kbd level, i.e., one layer below chips (6px) that actually exists but lacked a name in the ramp, leaking into the default. The 96 repeated instances are not explicit exceptions but a missing step. After adding it, all were mechanically replaced with `rounded-micro`, so pixel movement is 0; thereafter, `rounded-sm` and un-suffixed `rounded` are blocked by eslint selectors, and all named Tailwind default steps are blocked by per-family ratchets (`tests/contract/named-offramp-utility-ratchet.contract.test.ts`). The Chrome ladder's \"keycap 4px\" uses the same value — Chrome-side convergence (aliasing) is pending.\n\n**All 16 instances of `rounded-2xl` (16px) were downgraded to `panel` (12px) on 2026-08-04.** Unlike with `micro`, this was a judgment involving pixel movement, requiring site-by-site review; the answer came not from documentation but from the **radius census of the built screen**: within one row of the project drawer (width 399px), **six types** (20 / 18 / 16 / 12 / 9 / 6) coexisted, and only the `completeness`/`freshness` pair was already `rounded-panel`, meaning **siblings on the same line were misaligned**. Downgrading 16 to 12 leaves two steps — **sheet step** and **content step** (12). (The first draft of this paragraph listed drawer hero 20 as an explicit exception for the sheet step, but a full overlay judgment on the same day **reversed it** — the hero is inflow content scrolling within the drawer, lacking sheet eligibility, and was downgraded to panel. See the `sheet` entry below.) The previous 16/18/20 performed three roles while differing by only 2px from each other, failing to create hierarchy. It wasn't `card` (9) because these boxes are **slot containers** with widths of 365–399px, and the two sibling choices already occupying that slot + `TopologyEmptyState`'s override (`rounded-[var(--radius-panel)]`) yield the same answer. Icon tiles (44px) require separate judgment, but the conclusion is the same — this app's tile ratio is 36px/9px = 4.0, so the pair for 44px is 11px, and the nearest ramp step is 12.\nRegistration partners: `app/globals.css` + `src/shared/lib/cn.ts` `RADIUS_RAMP_STEPS` (tailwind-merge radius group — if unregistered, `rounded-chip` followed by `rounded-micro` will not merge, leaving both alive with CSS source order determining the winner).\n\n**`sheet` (18px) was added in the 2026-08-04 system establishment.** As the drawer judgment converged content steps to 12, the same bug surfaced one layer up — at 1512px empirical measurement, **overlay radii spanned six values** (12 · 9 · 22 · 16 · 18 · 20, plus mobile 28 in source), and among them, 16/18/20 differed by only 2px from each other, failing to create hierarchy. Sources were also fractured: 2 component-specific tokens (`--topology-shortcut-sheet-radius` 22 · `--topology-search-sheet-radius` 16, deprecated) + 4 eslint-disables (one literally \"pending registration\") + 1 directional-suffix lint blind spot (`rounded-t-[28px]`). **Five values were performing one job — floating sheets/palettes.** The reason for value 18: it is the current mode frequency and continues the ramp's common ratio (4→6→9→12→18, ≈1.5×). Scope rule — **only large transient surfaces that float and obscure below** (shortcut/search/agent connection sheets, quick action/gesture hints, mobile bottom sheet tops) qualify as sheet. Anchor popovers · menus use card/panel; small confirmation dialogs use panel; **inflow content is prohibited from using sheet regardless of size** (craft entry card 16 → panel, drawer hero 20 → panel are those judgments). The border partner for the sheet step is `--color-divider` (0.08) — the previous `--color-overlay-3` (0.10) instance was also converged. Gate: eslint radius selector (extended to include directional suffixes) + `RADIUS_RAMP_STEPS` sync contract (`cn.test.ts`).\n\n> **Relationship with Chrome radius ladder.** The `--chrome-radius` > (10px) · `--chrome-radius-inner` (7px) · keycap (4px) ladder in the \"Chrome Syntax\" section below is a **separate system encapsulated in components** (ChromeTile / ChromeChip / status chip specific). The `rounded-chip/card/panel` in this codex governs **general JSX surfaces** outside that scope. Since Chrome surfaces use components rather than inline `rounded-[Npx]`, the two systems do not conflict — Chrome boxes follow the Chrome ladder, everything else follows this ramp.\n\n### Page Column — Single `--page-max`\n\n| Target | Token | px |\n|---|---|---|\n| Page Container | `--page-max` | 1600 |\n\n`--page-max` is the page width that leaves a 160px gutter on both sides based on a 1920px viewport.\n\n**`--page-col-utility`(960px) has been retired** (Design Council Verdict ③, 2026-07-29).\nThe specification itself — \"narrow the screen one more time from the inside for a single judgment view\" — was not wrong, but **it produced the exact opposite result in its sole consumer.** The `/download` page is a surface that **attaches to the left** of the download panel, but centering only the footer with this token created two alignment references within the same page — measured (1920): panel x=160 · footer x=480. No element aligned with another.\n\nTwo lessons learned:\n\n- **The central column must not mix with left-aligned surfaces.** If a page contains both an `mx-auto` column and a left-fixed column, their x-coordinates diverge as a function of viewport width.\n- **Unused tokens are misinformation, not specifications.** The moment consumption drops to zero, remove it (same treatment as `--pad-card`/`--pad-panel`).\n\n\n#### Alignment Origin — `--gateway-origin` (2026-07-29 night, Gateway Surface)\n\n| Target | Token | Value |\n\n|---|---|---|\n| Gateway alignment origin | `--gateway-origin` | `max(--gateway-gutter, (100vw − --gateway-page-max) / 2)` (revised 2026-08-19: replaces the former `--page-max` with a gateway-specific ceiling) |\n| Gateway gutter (origin floor) | `--gateway-gutter` | 200, unitless (the 40→64→120→200 lineage lives in the dedicated `app/globals.css` block) |\n| Gateway content-column ceiling | `--gateway-page-max` | `1920px` (2026-08-19 wide-width revision, round 2) — the single ceiling read by `PAGE_COLUMN` and the alignment origin across gateway surfaces (gateway face, documentation face, and GNB). In the owner's 2560 measurement, each side margin was 480px and 37.5% of the screen was empty canvas; among four options, the owner chose “widen only the gateway”: [320][1920][320] at 2560. **Invariant: `--gateway-page-max` ≥ `--page-max` (1600).** While this value remains at least 1600, origin and column calculations are identical to the previous formula for vw ≤ 2000, so 1440–1920 rendering does not move by one pixel. Other surfaces (document vault, projects, insights) keep `--page-max`. Reading measures do not follow the wider column: the hero lead keeps `max-w-[40rem]` (measured 34 characters per line), and document prose keeps `--measure-prose` (70ch). Only the monumental proportional headline, instrument strip, rules, and GNB use the full column. Gates: `tests/contract/gateway-column-width.contract.test.ts` + `tests/e2e/download-gateway-grid.spec.ts` |\n| Gateway plate width | `--gateway-plate-width` | 880, unitless. The 2026-08-18 remake moved 520→880: the plate now sits in the installation section's flow instead of floating over the map, leaving only one content-width ceiling |\n| Gateway section rhythm | `--gateway-section-gap` | 160px (2026-08-18) — one section is punctuation for one thought |\n| Gateway stage width | `--gateway-stage-max` | `clamp(48rem, 40vw, 80rem)` (2026-08-19 wide-width revision) — the shared stage ceiling for demo and agent scenes. The 48rem floor is the owner-approved value (ledger (83)), and 40vw×1920 = 48rem, so **the previous 768px remains unchanged at 1920 and below**. The 40vw slope is the largest proportional coefficient allowed by the 1440–1920 no-regression constraint; the 80rem ceiling is the final regular step that does not upscale the 1512px source clip at 1x density. Gates: `tests/contract/gateway-stage-width.contract.test.ts` + `tests/e2e/download-gateway-grid.spec.ts` |\n| Gateway FX alpha ceiling | `--gateway-fx-blob-alpha` / `--gateway-fx-grain-alpha` / `--gateway-fx-dust-alpha` | 0.14 / 0.05 / 0.28 — ceiling for the charter exception (gateway current field). Gate: `tests/contract/gateway-fx-exception.contract.test.ts` |\n\n**[Retired 2026-08-18] Plate-gap token (gateway plate-gap) and camera reservation width derivation**\n(`computeGatewaySafeInset` = origin + plate width + gap → `--topology-v2-safe-inset-left`).\nThe map moved down to the background behind the plate as its own cutout (evidence), eliminating the premise of overlap — non-overlap is measured directly via rect in `tests/e2e/download-gateway-grid.spec.ts`.\nThe descriptions below regarding \"camera reservation width\" are records from that era.\n\n**Aligning only the left still causes visual bias.** Even after Verdict ③ placed these six elements at the same x, the column stops at `--page-max`, causing all remaining width to accumulate on the right — measured 1920: left 64 · right 256 (ratio 4.0), 2560: left 96 · right 864 (ratio 9.0). These six elements were **one set** even then. While adhering to alignment principles, symmetry can break; thus, they are specified and measured separately.\n\n**Do not fix with `mx-auto`.** Not because centering is bad, but **because it creates two origins** — the wrapper centers itself based on the viewport, while camera reservation insets are fixed values, causing a 96px offset at 1920 and 416px at 2560. Elevating the origin to a single token means both the six elements and the camera consume **the same value**, making this thought structurally impossible.\nSymmetry comes from having origins on both left and right padding, with the column filling the remaining width exactly.\n\n**It is the only gateway token registered via `@property <length>`.** Registration ensures computed values solidify into used lengths like `160px`, enabling: ① CSS to recalculate automatically when the viewport changes, and ② JS to read the same value via `parseFloat` and derive camera reservation width (`origin + plate width + gap`). The three atomic values manually set by humans are **not registered** — registration would cause silent drift where natural inputs like `30rem` silently revert to initial-value without error. Only derived values are registered.\n\n**⚠️ If the origin becomes a function of viewport, JS derivation must subscribe to resize.** CSS follows for free, but camera reservation width does not — setting it once on mount means the plate moves to the new origin while the camera continues using the old value. Updates require full invalidation or `refreshIndexDependentTokens` (replacing only that token).\n\nGateway: `tests/e2e/download-gateway-grid.spec.ts` — 8-column × (six elements x identical · `clientWidth − band.right === origin` · GNB right edge · reservation width = origin + plate width + gap) + resize round-trip. The reference for symmetry is `clientWidth`, not `innerWidth` (`100vw` includes the scrollbar, while `getBoundingClientRect` does not).\n\n### Padding — Do Not Use Ramps (Updated 2026-07-26)\n\n| Target | Token | px |\n|---|---|---|\n| Inside Card | `--card-pad` | 16 |\n\n| Inside Panel | `--topology-v2-panel-pad` | 14 |\n\n\n**A separate two-step ramp named `--pad-card`/`--pad-panel` once existed,\nbut was removed.** The documentation pointed to dead values:\n\n- An exhaustive census found **zero code uses** of either token. Cards had\n  always used `--card-pad`, and panels used `--topology-v2-panel-pad`.\n- `--pad-card` (16) duplicated `--card-pad` (16): two names for one concept.\n- `--pad-panel` (12) **differed** from the value panels actually used (14).\n  A new panel built from that table would have missed existing panels by 2px.\n\nThe lesson applies to specifications generally: **an unused token is\nmisinformation, not a specification.** Creating a ramp includes proving that\nits consumers actually reference it.\n\nThe gap steps follow the **4/8 principle** — `gap-*` / `space-*` use only steps of 1 (4px), 2 (8px), 3 (12px)...\nThe remaining 27 arbitrary px paddings were fully classified; excluding 3, 11, and 18px, they are all **optical corrections** used only once or twice. Snapping them to a ramp would actually break alignment —\ntherefore, no lint rules apply to padding.\n\n### Panel Width · Measurement Width — No Lamp (2026-08-04 System Stone)\n\nWidths have **no shared unit; that is the specification.** All widths in this repository are **derived values**\n— calculated from content constraints or geometry, not chosen from a scale:\n\n| Token | Value | Derivation Basis |\n|---|---|---|\n| `--git-setup-measure` | 520px | Single-task column (reuse of prose measured width) |\n\n| `--git-evidence-min` | 600px | 11px mono 80 columns ≈ 528 + gutter + padding |\n\n| `--git-single-measure` | 920px | Single column when evidence column is absent |\n\n| `--settings-content-measure` | 658px | Sheet 880 − border 2 − LNB 180 − p-5 40 (contract test verifies derivation) |\n\n| `--agent-panel-width` | `clamp(320px, 26vw, 420px)` | Viewport function |\n\n| `--topology-v2-panel-width` | `min(352px, calc(100vw − 28px))` | Viewport function |\n\n| `--docs-list-width` | 280px | Document list rail |\n\n\nFixed-unit ramps **cannot conceptually express** these — `clamp()`/`min()` are\nnot scales (same logic as listing `chrome-token` in the control ratchet). Snapping 658\nto a \"640 unit\" breaks derivation, so it won't follow when sheet geometry changes.\nThe industry agrees (source verified 2026-08-04, [Carbon 2x Grid](https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/2x-grid/overview/)):\n*\"Boxes are sized by applying a sizing scale based on either fixed mini units\nor fluid column widths\"* — width is **derived** from grid/content, not ramp steps.\n\n**When you need a width for a new surface — this path requires no convening or approval:**\n\n1. First find a same-nature measured width in the table above (e.g., reuse `--git-setup-measure` for prose).\n2. If none exists, **create a surface-specific token** in that surface's token block with a derivation comment. ⚠️ This is **neither** a \"system\" convening target nor an approval target —\n   the `design.md` convening trigger and `pnpm decisions:check` sensor only look at **ramp\n   tokens** (`scripts/lib/design-spec-census.mjs` `RAMP_TOKEN_PATTERN`,\n   explicitly excluding surface-specific tokens). The 2026-08-04 practical test observed that *\"the gate made `w-96` cheaper than a single ramp line\"*, but that cost model was **factually\n   incorrect** — the surface token path has always been free; the real hole was that no one knew,\n   which is why this section exists.\n3. One-off `max-w-*` values hold the same status as optical corrections — do not enforce them like padding.\n\n**To create a width «ramp»**, that is when ramp listing requires \"system\" convening + approval. Falsification\nobservation: if three or more surface width tokens of the same value repeat **without derivation** (evidence of scale demand), this decision is reconsidered.\n\n### Box Specifications Table\n\nEach box references only the tokens below. Do not reimplement inline px/radius outside the table.\n\n| Box | Height | Radius | Padding | Typography Unit |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Chrome Tile (ChromeTile) | `--chrome-tile-size` 36px | `--chrome-radius` 10px | `--chrome-inset` alignment | Icon 16px |\n\n| Status Chip (`CHROME_STATUS_CHIP_CLASS`) | 44px (same as tile) | `--chrome-radius` 10px | `px-3.5` | body / label |\n\n| Panel (INDEX · Datasheet) | Content | `--topology-v2-panel-radius` 12px (= `rounded-panel`) | `--topology-v2-panel-pad` | title header · body row |\n| Popover (ego popover) | Content | `rounded-panel` | `--card-pad` | title + body/label |\n| **Section Box** (Panel) | Content | `rounded-panel` | **`--card-pad`** | title + body |\n| **Item Box** (Card) | Content | `rounded-card` | Density determines inset (no enforcement) | title + body |\n| Badge · Chip (General) | Content | **`badgeClass({ shape })` generates** — `micro`(micro·px-1.5 py-0.5·caption) · `tag`(chip·px-1.5·label) · `pill`(full·px-2 py-0.5·caption). Do not copy values here | Same as above | Same as above |\n| Input (input/search) | Content | `rounded-card` | `px-3 py-2` | body |\n| Button (General) | Content | `rounded-chip`~`card` | `px-3 py-1.5` | body |\n\n**Why the badge row is a delegation** (2026-08-15): Previously, this line prescribed `rounded-chip · px-2 py-0.5 · label`, but an audit revealed **zero exact matches in production** — 67 badges were split across 30 geometric shapes and 60 colors, and no one was consulting the table. Instead of restating values in the docs, we delegate to `badgeClass`, and hand-written geometry is managed by `static-badge-adoption-ratchet`. **Color and letter-spacing are intentionally not covered by value layers** — with 60 color combinations and a maximum cluster size of 2, any chosen value would result in zero consumers (convergence happens via per-location design judgment in the next round).\n\n**Use panel for sections, card for items** (2026-08-15 \"System\" session). Boxes placed directly on page/sheet/drawer bottoms to **create zones** use `rounded-panel` (12px) + `p-[var(--card-pad)]`. Boxes already nested within cards/panels or serving as **items in a repeated list** use `rounded-card` (9px), with inset determined by content density.\n\nThe concentric relationship of outer 12 > inner 9 aligns with Material 3 shape scale and Apple HIG's \"nested surfaces have smaller radii\" guideline. Empirical evidence: within a single file, there are instances where the outer layer is panel/16px and the inner is card (`ConstructionReviewPanel` lines 104 ↔ 158), and all card family samples are items/nested boxes. Padding distribution also differs — the panel family has a majority of 16px (46%), while the card family follows a density-driven long tail, so **card inset is not enforced**.\n\n⚠️ **Previously, this table stated \"Card (General) = `rounded-card` + `--card-pad`\", but its real-world usage was zero.** The living spec is `rounded-panel` + 16px (token 13 + manual 12 = 25 locations). Using the table to build would have led to misinformation contradicting reality, akin to the removed `--pad-panel`. `--topology-v2-panel-pad` (14px) applies to only 4 consumers, all within map detail panels, making it a **map-local token**, not a general panel spec.\n\n### Explicit Exceptions (Outside the Lamp, Only Documented Ones)\n\nSurfaces that can be redesigned via lamp snap remain only as `// eslint-disable-next-line\nno-restricted-syntax -- <reason>`. Current listings:\n\n- **Hairline radius 1~4px** — progress/capacity meter tracks/fills for heights 2~14px (`full-detail-a1-reach-panel`, `TopologyIndexTreeRow`, `FreshnessTab`, reach step chips). Raising to chip (6px) makes them read like pills, preserving intent.\n- **Overlay sheet radius 18~28px** — floating cards/sheets (`SearchPalette` 22px, `GestureHint`/`PublicQuickActions` 18px, `ProjectDrawer` 20px, `detail-card` 28px signature). Adding the paired caption (14px) would grow both lines by 6px, pushing the action strip below the metric line and breaking the chrome scale contract. Since only one location in the app needs this value, we do not widen the lamp — tokens used once are misinformation, not specs. **Reason for extracting as a separate constant**: disable comments are line-level; attaching them to class strings would silence `text-[Npx]` fans on the same line (empirical: lint total dropped from 143 → 142).\n\n### Lint Blockade\n\n`eslint.config.mjs`'s `no-restricted-syntax` blocks new arbitrary classes like `text-[Npx]`, `rounded-[Npx]`, and `leading-[N]`.\n\n**Named line-height utilities (`leading-4/5/6/relaxed/snug` etc., 199 cases) are not caught by the rule.** The 199 warnings drown out the baseline of 143, and the dominant values (16/20/24px) are **identical to lamp pairs**, so they aren't violations either. After arbitrary usage hits zero, only `relaxed`/`snug` families will be re-measured as ratchet candidates.\n\n- **Migration complete directories = error** — `src/views/{ontology-insights,\n  project-selector,ontology-edit,docs-vault}` · `src/shared/ui` · `src/widgets`\n  (excluding R6).\n- **Incomplete (in-progress) = warn** — `src/widgets/topology-map-v2` ·\n  `src/widgets/hero-header` · `src/views/home`. One destination = one tile (e.g., view all, vault, builder). If `href` is provided, it acts as a link; otherwise, it's a button.\n- **Chip (ChromeChip)** — 44px tall label button. Icon (14px) + text + optional `kbd` cap. Used for controls where the label is part of the meaning, such as auto-alignment, search, and workspaces.\n- **Pill (Brand pill)** — Same surface as a chip (10px radius) but contains a pip (brand mark) + two lines of text (title + census). A composite surface. `HeroCollapsed`.\n- **Panel (INDEX · Compressed datasheet)** — 12px radius, one level larger than the three above, with its own internal header/body/footer rhythm.\n\n### Box Specifications (Geometry Ladder) — \"Applied Uniformly Everywhere\" Contract\n\n**All surfaces** in the top chrome row (brand pills, status chips, utility lane) share the same geometry tokens.
