The only enforcement mechanism that actually works here is lint (as stated in the \"Specs are enforced via lint\" section of this document), but components cannot be enforced by lint, whereas «whether this className originated from this function» can be.\n\n⚠️ **Moving existing controls is normalization, not refactoring — pixels will change.** The combined distribution of height, `px`, `py`, and type across 143 chips yields **50 unique combinations**, and even the top 3 account for only 23%. Thus, today's sizes are arbitrary values, not a ladder; the 3-tier ladder represents «the specification we must reach» rather than «today's summary». Therefore, mass migration is a task for the **design gate** (the \"system\"), and what is enforced today is singular: **new controls must not expand the 50 types into 51** (`tests/contract/control-adoption-ratchet.contract.test.ts`). The baseline only decreases — starting at 417, it is now 148).\n\n### Form Fields — `fieldClass()` · `fieldLabel()` (Design Council, 2026-08-06)\n\n**Pressing and receiving values are different parts.** The eight shapes of `controlClass()` emerged from a full census of **419** production `<button>` elements, while fields belong to a **different population** (63 forms). Hence, the ninth shape is not a variant but a **second cva** — for detailed rationale and rejected alternatives: `docs/DECISIONS.md` 2026-08-06.\n\n#### `fieldClass({ frame, size, multiline })`\n\n| Axis | Options | What differs |\n|---|---|---|\n| `frame` | `boxed` · `bare` | **Who provides the box** |\n| `size` | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` | Height — **1:1** with `--control-h-*` |\n| `multiline` | `false` · `true` | Hard `h-*` vs `min-h-*` |\n\n| `size` | Height | Token | Radius | Inset | Type |\n|---|---:|---|---|---|---|\n| `xs` | 28 | (same as `sm`) | `micro` 4 | `px-2` | `text-body` 12.5 |\n| `sm` | 28 | `--control-h-sm` | `chip` 6 | `px-2` | `text-body` 12.5 |\n| `md` | 32 | `--control-h-md` | `chip` 6 | `px-2.5` | `text-body-lg` 14 |\n| `lg` | 40 | `--control-h-lg` | `chip` 6 | `px-3` | `text-body-lg` 14 |\n\n**`xs` is not a height tier** — it is a tier that lowers only the radius, using the same syntax as chips' `xs`.\n\n**The reason types pair with sizes is because the screen dictated it.** Initially, we used only `text-body` (12.5), but reviewing `/project/new` revealed that **the values users input are roughly the same magnitude as the labels the app uses (11px)**. In forms, what must be most readable is the value entered by the user. The tight spacing of 12.5 exists because putting 14px text into a 28px box eliminates vertical breathing room.\n\n##### `boxed` vs `bare` — Why they cannot be merged\n\nThe \"Hierarchy\" column opened the reality and split forms into three:\n\n| Dialect | Function | **Winning choice** | `frame` |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **Record** | Value persists to disk | **Input** | `boxed` |\n| **Query** | Reaches existing data fastest | **Result** — not input | `bare` |\n| **Stage** | Renders text for cards in situ | 23px name | **Out of spec** |\n\nMaking records transparent causes forms to disappear; making queries heavy causes **input to overpower results**.\n\n`bare` **does not provide any dimensions, borders, radius, horizontal insets, or touch bottom** — the parent already provides the box; providing it again here would **push inward from within that box**.\n\n**List Stage (workshop name 23px · subtitle 9.5px) out of spec.** Its size is not a form type but the **type of card being created**, meaning its size carries information (Mackinlay expressiveness). The moment it enters a box, that information is erased. We document it here so **the next person does not have to rediscover it**.\n\n#### `fieldLabel({ row })`\n\nLabels split into three branches, but **only two have specifications**:\n\n| Branch | Spec | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Name text** | `text-label`(11) · `secondary` | Name must be larger than its footnote |\n| **Entire row is clickable** (`row: true`) | Touch floor + `min-h-6`(24) + row layout | Clicking the label toggles → **label is the target** (WCAG 2.5.8) |\n| **Layout-only wrapper** (`block` · `flex flex-col`) | **None** | Adding type/color competes with the inner name text and spec |\n\n**The reason ink is `secondary` is empirical measurement.** The label on `/project/new` was 9.5px · quaternary, while **the footnote directly below it was 11px** — the field's name was one step smaller than its own footnote, causing users to read the 14px placeholder before the label. This is the **same issue** as caught in the 2026-08-02 settings sheet (promoting dimensions from subordinate positions to primary roles).\n\n#### New Token 0 · Gate\n\nAll reuse existing lamps. Enforcement is not lint but the **full contract of cva output**:\n\n| Gate | What it locks |\n|---|---|\n| `tests/contract/field-class.contract.test.ts` | Exhaustive 16 combinations · **unit↔token 1:1** (reading px from CSS for comparison) · `bare` does not create a box · type↔size pairing · no width creation |\n| `tests/contract/checkbox-target-size.contract.test.ts` | Checkbox target 24 (its own size ∨ label floor) |\n| `tests/contract/control-adoption-ratchet.contract.test.ts` | Hand-written forms do not grow (form debt) |\n| `tests/contract/touch-floor-layer.contract.test.ts` | `boxed` gets coarse floor, `bare` does not |\n\n⚠️ **Do not use \"is it in the vocabulary\" as a check.** If you measure height by \"is it in the height vocabulary,\"**a flaw where a single-line `md` is set to `h-9`(36) passes green**(empirical). It must be unit↔token 1:1.\n\n⚠️ **Do not measure type with `toContain('text-body')`.** `text-body-lg` includes it as a substring, so it remains green even immediately after changing the rule (empirical).\n\n### Control Height Ladder (Owner confirmed 2026-08-03)\n\n**Control heights outside this table are deviations.** Without this section, 30 and 34 were born — while building the control value layer, `--control-h-*` was not found, and the sum of padding+line-height+border was called a lamp, producing chips 24/30/34 · fields 20/22/30. **30 · 34 · 22 · 20 are values not present anywhere in this app's height vocabulary**.\n\n| px | Token / Unit | Who stands here | Why this value |\n|---:|---|---|---|\n| **24** | (No token — spec constant) | `chip`/`pill`/`icon` `sm`, `segment` `sm`·`md`, **all sizes of `link` (`min-h-6`, 2026-08-04)** | **WCAG 2.5.8 (AA, Target Size Minimum) 24×24** — the floor of the ladder. Below this is a spec violation, not \"small unit\" |\n| **28** | `--control-h-sm` | `row` `sm`, `icon` `md` (`h-7 w-7`) | Single-line list row and 28px square icon |\n| **32** | `--control-h-md` | `chip`/`pill` `md`·`lg`, `segment` `lg`, `card` `sm`, `icon` `lg`, `--app-nav-rail-tile-height` | **The app's default control height.** The value layer stands on this value via `min-h-8` |\n| **36** | `--chrome-tile-size` | Chrome field/tile, **document header tile**, `row` `md`, `card` `md` | Workbench chrome dimensions nailed by the \"scale fixed contract\" |\n| **40** | `--control-h-lg` | Select, large form controls, `card` `lg` | Box for entering text |\n| **44** | `--touch-target-min` | `row` `lg`, `--control-row-h`, `pointer: coarse` promotion (token override + `.touch-hit-expand`) | Touch value from Apple HIG / Material / WCAG **2.5.5(AAA)** — **coarse single source**. The fine front of `link` was reset to 44 (`min-h-11`) on 2026-08-04, then back to 24 below (see \"link floor\" section) |\n\n**34 disappeared from this table on 2026-08-03.** It was listed as a single-line \"chrome lock,\" but that listing **only recorded it, not justified it**. Tracing the basis leads to a single comment in `DocsHeaderTile` — *\"`ChromeTile` fixes `--chrome-tile-size`(**44px**) and does not match header density (34px).\"* The chrome tile was **lowered to 36px on 2026-07-23** (owner: \"obviously too big\"), and on that day the only basis for 34 vanished, yet no one re-derived 34. Only two values and two coarse promotion rules remained for the same role (square icon tile). Now there is only one: `--chrome-tile-size`. Source: `docs/DECISIONS.md` 2026-08-03 \"Tile dimensions are one\".\n\n### link floor 24 · Prose link contract (2026-08-04)\n\n**The `link` floor is 24 (`min-h-6`), not 44.** The previous value layer cited WCAG 2.5.8 (AA, 24×24) but included the value 44 (`min-h-11`) from 2.5.5 (AAA)/HIG. This incorrect floor created an `inline` escape hatch, allowing five misconfigurations (16–18px hit areas) to survive without triggering any static checks. The three parts of the redefinition:\n\n- **Fine pointer = 24.** The value layer `link` base carries `min-h-6`. Gate:\n  `tests/contract/control-class.contract.test.ts` \"link floor is 24\" +\n  `tests/e2e/touch-target-contract.spec.ts` fine-pointer audit (24×24 ∨ inline\n  exemption ∨ 24px spacing exception — exactly as per WCAG 2.5.8).\n- **Coarse pointer = 44 — two prescriptions, neighbor spacing determines which**\n  (revised 2026-08-05). 44 comes only from `--touch-target-min` (single source for coarse).\n\n  | Prescription | Where | Why this one |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | **Actual height** — `.atlas-touch-floor` (`min-height`) | Value layer `chip`, `row`, `pill` | As the control grows, it **pushes neighbors away**, preventing overlap |\n  | **Hit expansion** — `.touch-hit-expand` (coarse-only pseudo-element, 0 layout shift) | Value layer `icon`, hand-drawn controls | A square surface contract; `min-h` alone cannot shape this area |\n\n  **Hit expansion attachment requires ≥12px neighbor target clearance** — blindly attaching to dense rows causes the `::after` of a later DOM element to steal the tab of the preceding one. This is exactly why we use actual height for the value layer: among 38 cases under 44px, **21 had <12px spacing with neighbors** (EN/KO toggle 1px · tab pair 2px). The cost is density (~50px vertical space in the mobile `/docs` header), documented in the ledger (2026-08-05).\n\n  ⚠️ **The floor rule lives outside cascade layers.** If placed inside `@layer base`,\n  `min-h-8` from `@layer utilities` wins — **layer order dictates specificity**,\n  so stacking classes cannot override it. We experienced this: the rule was in the\n  build, but the screen remained 32px. Gate:\n  `tests/contract/touch-floor-layer.contract.test.ts`.\n- **The `inline` axis is deleted.** \"Is it inside a sentence?\" cannot be determined statically (sibling text origin, used display, reflow all open outside the tag), so runtime handles it.\n\n**Prose links are not controls.** Links within markdown body flow (Document Viewer 5 ·\nGateway Reader 1) have siblings that are text, and the line box is owned by the parent `--leading-prose` — none of the eight value layer shapes can theoretically occupy this space (inline-flex kills wrapping at 320px — measured rect 1 vs. control 2). The target is\nthe single set **`.prose-link`** in `app/globals.css`: it owns only underline geometry (offset 2px) and default decoration color; it does not impose ① display, ② line-height/font-size, or ③ focus (preserving UA defaults). Gate: `tests/contract/prose-link.contract.test.ts`. In the control ledger,\n`prose` is listed as a claim (`control-adoption-ratchet`).\n\n### Which shapes does this ladder apply to? (2026-08-03 — scope explicit)\n\nThe previous sentence (*\"Heights outside this table are deviations\"*) omitted the scope, leaving\n**areas where deviation or compliance cannot be determined**: NavRail items render at **62px** across all routes (measured 1440×900), but that 62 is not a unified value — it is the **sum** of `py-1.5` (12) + tile 32 + `gap-1` (4) + label line box 14. This is not in this table, nor is it a defect — it was a gap caused by the rule not stating its scope.\n\n| Category | What the ladder captures | Example |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Single-line horizontal controls** — content is one line, height defines the axis | **The outer height itself.** All variants must explicitly declare `min-h-*`, and that value must be in this table | `chip` · `pill` · `segment` · `row` · `card` |\n| **Square icon controls** | **The side length itself.** `h-*` or size tokens must be in this table | `icon` · `ChromeTile` · `DocsHeaderTile` |\n| **Vertically stacked controls** — e.g., icon above, label below, two+ lines | **The inner square tile, not the outer height.** The outside is the sum of content, so the ladder does not define it | `tile` · NavRail item (`--app-nav-rail-tile-height` = 32 = `--control-h-md`) |\n| **Inline text links** | Exempt. Applying `min-h` pushes the line box up (measured 21.3 → 44) | `link` (inline). Non-inline `link` is 44 |\n\n**In short**: The ladder captures «height of single-line boxes» and «side of squares». For vertically\nstacked items, it captures **the tile inside**, not the outer sum — trying to do so would let label character count dictate specs, causing the ladder to violate its own rule 1 (*\"padding must not define height\"*).\n**Scope — this table applies to «single-line horizontal» controls (2026-08-03 system log).**\nApplicable targets are only single-line shapes (`chip`·`pill`·`segment`·`row`·`card`) and squares\n(`icon`). **Vertical 2-axis surfaces are not in this table** — `tile` shapes, and controls stacked like NavRail items (icon above, label below) have their height defined by content and chrome geometry tokens (`--app-nav-rail-tile-*`). A NavRail item rendering at 62px is not a ladder deviation but **out of scope** (sum of tile 32px + label + spacing). As the rule audit noted, the phrase \"outside this table is deviation\" was undeterminable without specifying which shapes it applied to — this paragraph is that scope declaration. Underline tabs (`tab-bar`) are also out of scope as they are baseline-aligned surfaces, not boxes; however, the note that their height (measured 29px) is outside the lexicon remains unresolved (see \"Next\" below).\n\n**`xs` (micro tier) is not a height step (2026-08-03).** The value layer's `size: 'xs'`\nkeeps the 24 floor (`min-h-6`) and only lowers **inset, type, and radius** to the micro tier (chip: `px-1.5 py-0.5`/caption/`rounded-micro`. Outside chips, it is an alias for `sm` — no consumers invent values). The reason for not creating a step below 24 is the first line of the table above: below WCAG 2.5.8 floor is not a \"small step\" but non-compliance. Evidence is the three-round continuous record in the ratchet ledger: \"no step below sm\" (full sweep 14 · 9 files).\n\n**Three disciplines:**\n\n1. **Height is defined by the ladder; padding is determined within it.** Reversing this (letting padding define height) quietly births values not in the lexicon — that is how 30/34/22/20 were created.\n2. **Hard `h-*` is forbidden; use `min-h-*`.** Hard heights clip wrapped controls, hiding content. `min-h` establishes single lines on the ladder and allows overflow to grow.\n3. **If you need a height not here, fix this table — do not add axes.** This is what Rules 0 (check if it exists first) and 1 (components over axes) of \"Rules for extending the system\" require here. The `fixedHeight` axis from 2026-08-03 did exactly the opposite.\n\n**Secondary correction (2026-08-03, system log · remaining half of #884)**: The previous restoration stopped at chip/pill — a secondary sweep found segment/sm **22px** (floor non-compliance, 0 consumers) · row/lg **42px** (outside lexicon, 0 consumers) · card/sm **30px** (outside lexicon, 15 locations) · card/md **34px** (accidental occupation by Document Viewer header chrome lock step, 5 locations). Thus, discipline 1 was encoded as a value:\n**All single-line horizontal shapes (chip·pill·segment·row·card) must explicitly declare a `min-h-*` floor.** Combinations where the floor equals natural height have 0px shift; only the four above were raised to 24/44/32/36 (chip/pill `md`=`lg`=32 remains unchanged — owner confirmation that `lg` grows text/inset, not height, is valid). `tile` is a vertical 2-axis surface where content defines height; `link` is non-inline 44 / inline exempt — neither is in this table's scope.\n\n**Gate**: `tests/contract/control-class.contract.test.ts` asserts ① `chip`/`pill` `md`·`lg` emit `min-h-8` and `sm` does not ② the pixel value of `min-h-8` **matches** the parsed value of `--control-h-md` in `app/globals.css` (if the ladder token moves, the lamp turns red immediately) ③ the `fixedHeight` axis does not reappear ④ **all single-line horizontal shapes (5×3)+squares (3) explicitly declare height and that value is within the height lexicon — `--control-h-*`·`--chrome-tile-size`·`--touch-target-min` parsed values + WCAG floor 24**\n⑤ arbitrary `min-h-[...]` cannot bypass the lexicon — five assertions.\n\n**Scope gate**: To ensure the above table does not remain only in words, `tests/contract/control-height-ladder-scope.contract.test.ts`\ncaptures two categories **outside** the value layer — ① default values of all tile size tokens in `app/globals.css` (`--*-tile-size` / `--*-tile-height`) are within the height lexicon (`max()`/`calc(× scale)` forms extract base px for determination) ② inner tiles of vertically stacked controls stand on the ladder (`--app-nav-rail-tile-height` = `--control-h-md`). Without ①, no gate fired when 34 was born.\n\n### Rules for extending the system (2026-08-03 owner directive)\n\n`/design-build` is **how to use** the system. This section is **how to extend** it —\nwe paid a real price for not doing so.\n\n> **Attempted verification but access failed (2026-08-03)**: Material 3 (`m3.material.io`) and\n> Spectrum (`spectrum.adobe.com`) render their body content via JS, so the original text\n> doesn't download properly\n> (for M3, the entire transmitted text is just *\"This website requires JavaScript.\"* — 69 chars). **Do not use these two as references** — I leave this note here to prevent the next person from repeating the same verification or, worse, filling gaps with search summaries. I also verified that Fluent 2's token documentation **lacks a section on \"When to create new tokens.\"**\n\n#### Rule 0 — **Look for existing values before creating new ones**\n\n**This rule is first because we didn't follow it on 2026-08-03.**\n\nThis app already had a single source of truth for control heights —\n`--control-h-{sm,md,lg}` = **28 / 32 / 40px** (`app/globals.css`, established in\n\"Design Overhaul #13\" on 2026-07-25, consumed by 7 files). But while building the control value layers,\nwe failed to find it and instead **invented new values of 24 / 30 / 34** as a byproduct of padding + line-height.\n**30 and 34 are values that do not exist in this app's height vocabulary (24·28·32·36·40·44).**\n\nThen it got worse. When the new values clashed with the contract (32px), **instead of fixing the value, we added an exception axis\n(`fixedHeight`).** System stone verdict: *\"That axis is a **symptom** that the value is wrong,\nnot a necessary axis — fix the value and the axis dies.\"*\n\nThe result appeared on screen: we reduced chip sizes from 50 types to 3, but **there were\n8–9 types of control heights on a single screen**. Even if Rules 1–6 were followed, this one violation caused it.\n\n**Procedure** — If you feel you need new dimensions, colors, or spacing, stop right there and:\n\n1. Find the token for that role in `app/globals.css` (`--control-h-*` ·\n   `--chrome-*` · `--text-*` · `--leading-*` · `--radius-*` · `--motion-*`).\n2. Read this document's **「Control Height Ladder」** and ramp sections.\n3. Run `git log --oneline -- app/globals.css | head -20` to see why those values\n   were set — there is usually a reason, and that reason is likely still valid.\n4. If they still don't exist, **only then** proceed to Rule 4 (count how many are blocked).\n\n> **Values created without looking are not part of the system; they are a second system.**\n\n**Industry publication** — [Carbon Contribution Review](https://carbondesignsystem.com/contributing/product-development-lifecycle/) actually has this question as a review item:\n\n> *\"Does it replicate anything in the system already, or is there truly a gap?\"*\n> *\"If the proposal does replicate an existing asset, is there evidence to show that\n> the proposed solution is better?\"*\n\n[W3C Design Tokens Draft](https://www.designtokens.org/tr/drafts/format/) defines the purpose itself\nas a single source of truth — *\"Maintaining a 'single source of truth' for design tokens\"* ·\n*\"Eliminating repetition of values in token files.\"*\n\nThe second quote is the exact reflection of our thinking: **if you must recreate something that already exists, you must provide evidence that the new version is better.** We invented 24/30/34 while having `--control-h-*`, without providing that\nevidence.\n\n#### Rule 1 — Look at slots before adding axes\n\n**The basis of this clause is arithmetic, and the tool called slots exists in the industry.** To avoid mixing them in speech, their sources are listed separately.\n\n**Our rationale (math)**: With 3 axes, there are 8 combinations; with 4 axes, 16. **Axes multiply, components add.** We added axes one by one from `active` → `inline` → `fixedHeight`, and the results appeared on screen — reducing chip sizes from 50 types to 3 types, yet **the control height has 8–9 types** on a single screen.\n\n**Industry tool**: [tailwind-variants slots](https://www.tailwind-variants.org/docs/slots)\ndefines them as *\"Slots allows you to separate a component into multiple parts.\"*\n⚠️ **That document does not call slots 'the solution to variant explosion'** — it introduces them merely as a part separation\nfeature. Using them as an alternative to axis explosion is **our judgment**, and the basis is the arithmetic above. (Original text verification on 2026-08-03. Initially I wrote \"the document explicitly states\" based only on search summaries, but that sentence was not in the original text — always verify quotes by opening the original source.)\n\n⚠️ **No industry publication basis.** No text in Carbon · Fluent · Polaris · W3C discusses \"variant axis\ncombination explosion vs. part decomposition\" (verified against original texts on 2026-08-03). This clause stands on **our arithmetic and measurements alone**. tailwind-variants is cited for tool usage, not as an industry principle basis;\nthe moment you erase that distinction, this clause gains fabricated authority.\n\nJudgment: When a new variant is needed, first ask \"**which part** of this control changes?\"\nIf only the shell changes, use an axis; if text/icon/badge changes, use **parts**.\n\n#### Rule 2 — Do not create two tags with the same appearance\n\n**Our basis**: If buttons and links look the same, one must inevitably become outdated. Measurement — this\nrepository had byte-identical `<button>`/`<Link>` twins with no guardrails.\n\n**Industry publication — why twins arise**: Because semantics diverge from purpose.\n[Carbon Button usage](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/button/usage/):\n*\"Do not use buttons as navigational elements. Instead, use links when the desired\naction is to take the user to a new page.\"*\n[Polaris Button](https://polaris-react.shopify.com/components/actions/button):\n*\"Buttons are used primarily for actions… Links are used primarily for navigation.\"*\n\n**And the industry's answer is also 'one component, replace only the underlying element'** — same Polaris document:\n*\"If navigation is required for the button component, use the `url` prop.\"* Our\n`asChild` escape hatch follows the same structure; Polaris releases it as a **first-class API**.\n\n**Industry tool**: [Radix's `asChild`](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/guides/composition)\nis *\"When `asChild` is set to `true`, Radix will not render a default DOM element,\ninstead cloning the part's child and passing it the props and behavior required to\nmake it functional.\"*\n\n⚠️ **However, Radix itself does not recommend this common path.** From the same document:\n*\"In the majority of cases you shouldn't need to modify the element type as Radix\nhas been designed to provide the most appropriate defaults.\"* And there are three conditions —\nyour child must **spread all props** (`If your component doesn't support those\nprops, it will break.`), **accept a ref** (`If your component doesn't accept a\nref, then it will break.`), and *\"it is your responsibility to ensure it remains\naccessible and functional.\"*\n\n**So our rule is this**: It is an **escape hatch** used only where duplicates would arise, not a default\npattern. When using it, pin those three conditions as contract tests. If you can't bear that burden,\ndon't create the duplicate — **eliminate one side**. That is the title of this clause.\n\n```tsx\n<RowButton asChild><Link href=\"…\">Open Document</Link></RowButton>\n```\n\n#### Rule 3 — To change the spec, invoke the \"system\"\n\nThe list of triggers and rationale is in the section of the same name in `.claude/rules/design.md`. The gist in one line:\n**A spec defined by oneself is not a spec, but a preference.**\n\n**Gate (added 2026-08-03)**: `pnpm decisions:check` requires records in `docs/DECISIONS.md` for changes that actually move the spec. Before that, this rule was a **rule only on paper** — of the five commits widening the value layer lamp, only one had a record entry.\nJudgments are made by **census**, not file name (increase/decrease of axis·option·default·lamp token values; excluding class strings and comments) — applying retroactively to the last 300 commits leaves 16 out of 79 that touched trigger files. Details: `scripts/lib/design-spec-census.mjs`,\ncontract: `tests/contract/design-spec-ledger.contract.test.ts`.\n\n#### Rule 4 — When adding new values, first count \"how many are blocked\"\n\nThe axes and shapes of this system all **came from a full census** (chip 128 · link-type 85 · row 39 · icon\n36 · pill 32 · card 18 · standard button 1). None were added by guesswork.\n\nWhen proposing new shapes, tones, or axes, **count the number of controls left outside the system because of it**\nand present that as evidence. If you can't count it, it's still a preference, not a spec.\n\n**Industry publication** — [Carbon contribution review](https://carbondesignsystem.com/contributing/product-development-lifecycle/) requires demand evidence as an adoption condition: *\"Proposals need to show that the component or\npattern would be useful to many teams and unique to the system.\"* Our \"counting blocked controls\" is a **measurement translated to single-repository scale** for that requirement — not copying the procedure, but measuring the same principle in our unit. The counting method is\nthe detector in `tests/contract/control-adoption-ratchet.contract.test.ts`.\n\n#### Rule 5 — When writing a spec in docs, include the gate in the same PR\n\n**Industry publications only half support this.** \"The system produces its own enforcement tools\" is\ncommon — [Polaris publishes stylelint config as an official tool](https://polaris-react.shopify.com/tools/stylelint-polaris):\n*\"A configuration of Stylelint rules that promote adoption of the Polaris design\nsystem in consuming apps.\"*\n\n⚠️ However, **\"binding in the same PR\" and \"pre-enforcement census measurement\" are absent from any publication.** Those\ntwo are supported only by our practical evidence — the noise incident where lint jumped 144 → 548, and three instances\nwhere the gate's own flaws were revealed (hardcoded lamp list · unexcluded folded `<details>` · penalties for shared\nconstants).\n\nThis is consistent with the existing discipline of this repository. But **count violations before enabling** (`/gate-probe`).\nAnd once the gate is added, **include a flaw to prove it turns red** — all gates in this system have been probed this way,\nand during that process, three flaws in the gates themselves were revealed (hardcoded lamp list · unexcluded folded `<details>` · penalties for shared constants).\n\n#### Rule 6 — Changing libraries is a last resort\n\n⚠️ **No industry publication basis.** None of the six publishers state when to replace a consumer's styling library\n(it's not their subject). This clause stands on `forbidden.md`'s dependency discipline and our figure of **244 usage sites**. Thus, rebuttal is easy — without external authority, it's a dispute over numbers alone.\n\nA replacement like `cva` → `tailwind-variants` provides slots, `extend`, and responsive variants. However,\n`forbidden.md` requires a **reason in the PR body** for new dependencies, and this system already has 244 using it. To propose a replacement, you must provide **evidence that slots cannot be done with `cva`** — \"it's more convenient\" is not a reason.\n\n### There are two layers — values and behavior\n\n`controlClass()` does **not replace** components. The industry standard is clearly components\n(Carbon · Fluent · Material · Polaris · shadcn), and this repository also produces components.\nThe distinction is **what is separated**:\n\n| Layer | Form | Carries | Why |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Value | `controlClass()` | Appearance · Size · Color · Disabled | A string is sufficient; contract tests prevent the lamp from emitting out-of-contract values. |\n| Action | `Chip`/`IconButton`/`RowButton` | Default `type=\"button\"`, mandatory accessible name, button semantics | **Strings cannot fundamentally represent me** |\n\nSpecifically, three things strings cannot do: ① Inside a form, the default for `<button>` is `submit`, so\na single chip could submit the form ② Icon controls have no readable text, requiring an accessible name,\nwhich is an attribute ③ List rows are wide, tempting one to make them `div+onClick`, but then keyboard navigation fails. `IconButton`'s `label` is a **required prop**, so the type blocks it at the moment of use — lint and contract tests tell you \"you missed it\" later, but types block it right there.\n\nHeight was not put in the lamp. Of 143 chips, only 38 (30%) have an explicit height; putting it in would change\nthe key for the remaining 70% at the moment of transition. Squares (`icon`) are the exception —\nthere, height is shape.\n\n### Disabled State — One Value (2026-08-06)\n\nThe visual treatment for unclickable controls is **the single set `CONTROL_DISABLED_CLASS` in `control-class.ts`**: blurred `disabled:opacity-55`, cursor `not-allowed`, removed shadow, and disabled hover. These four form one set — taking only the blur leaves a half-state where the control appears disabled but hover still works. `controlClass()`/`fieldClass()` already load this as base; hand controls combine this constant (they do not copy the value).\n\n- **Why 55**: The value from the 2026-08-03 layer decision (owner feedback: «pressing recent changes yields no response»), verified on `/project/new` where both filled indigo and outline buttons read as «present» and «not clickable». The nine places split across 60, 50, and 45 were unified to 55 on 2026-08-06 — WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled components from contrast requirements, but this exemption does not permit «any value».\n- **Elements that cannot receive `disabled:` variants** (inactive representations of `<Link>`/`<span>`) use `opacity-55` directly at the same level — currently one place (`TopologyV2ContextMenu`), outside lint.\n- **Gate**: `eslint.config.mjs` `disabledAffordanceSelectors` (global ban on values other than 55, zero exempt files) + `tests/contract/disabled-affordance.contract.test.ts` (does the constant handle all four treatments? · do values not diverge per path? · is the value layer consistent with lint allowed values?).\n\n\n### Select / Listbox (#4)\n\n- **Trigger** — 40px (`--control-h-lg`, `size=\"md\"` is 32px `--control-h-md`), `--color-overlay-1` surface, chevron, `role=\"combobox\"` + `aria-haspopup=\"listbox\"` + `aria-expanded` + `aria-activedescendant`.\n- **Popover listbox** — `--color-elevated` surface, `role=\"listbox\"`, each option `role=\"option\"` + `aria-selected`; active/hover options use indigo highlight (`--color-indigo-a16`), selected option uses indigo check.\n- **Keyboard** — ↑↓ cycling · Enter/Space confirmation · Esc close (+ return focus to trigger) · Home/End · Typeahead (600ms buffer). Closes on outside click.\n- **List is a portal** (2026-08-02 installed app regression). `createPortal(document.body)` + trigger rect anchor + collision avoidance (if space below cannot fill 264px and space above is larger, flip upwards; `max-height` is trimmed to actual available space). Since `position: fixed`, it re-anchors on scroll (capture)·resize while open.\n  **Why**: Old `position: absolute` was clipped by ancestor `overflow: hidden` — in the AI connection model cell, the runner provided 7 items but only 1 remained on screen (39px out of 264px, 14.8% visible); `aria-activedescendant` correctly traversed all 7. **The world keyboard users hear and the world they see diverged** (Nielsen ① System Status Visibility), passing through all role·aria markers. The clipping ancestor (`.ai-row-disclosure`) has `overflow: hidden` for height purposes only, so it cannot be removed.\n- **Motion** — Entry `select-pop` (`--motion-fast`), exit `select-unpop` (`calc(var(--motion-fast) * 0.67)` — exiting is faster than entering, same syntax as `settingsPanelOut`·`overlayFadeOut`). Only opacity + `scaleY`; `transform-origin` follows the opening direction. Chevron's `transition-transform` also uses **the same 80ms** — if two elements spawned by one input use different timings, they are read as two events (old state: list disappeared in 1 frame + chevron eased over 120ms).\n  Exit window uses the shared gate `usePanelPresence`; that frame immediately removes from accessibility tree via `aria-hidden` + `inert`. The equivalent for `prefers-reduced-motion` is `panelCrossfadeIn`/`overlayFadeOut` (remove only the shaking axis, keep timing).\n- **API** — `{ value, onChange, options: [{value,label,description?}], placeholder, ariaLabel, size?, disabled? }`. Tokens only.\n- **Gate** — `src/shared/ui/select.test.tsx` (portal·clipper escape·exit frame a11y) · `src/shared/ui/select-growth.test.ts` (upper bound arithmetic) · `tests/contract/reduced-motion-equivalent.contract.test.ts` (`select-listbox`) · `tests/contract/exit-motion-restart.contract.test.ts` · installed app `--verify-ai-settings` (list clipping·hit test·upper bound verification).\n\n\n#### List Growth and Upper Bound (`select-growth.ts`, 2026-08-02)\n\nThe old upper bound was a single literal `max-h-[264px]`, and that value **answered nothing**: how many items are fully visible? · when does scrolling start? · what happens if it opens at the bottom of the screen? All three were wrong. The upper bound is **two values, and the smaller one wins.**\n\n| Upper Bound | Value | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| Row upper bound `LISTBOX_MAX_ROWS` | **8 rows** | ① Measured runner had model **7 items** — if common cases scroll, «more available» becomes a lie ② 8 rows with mixed description lines ≈ 320px, which is less than half the settings sheet (672px) where this list appears. Growing beyond that turns it from a «selection control» into a «covering surface», requiring search rather than a larger dropdown |\n| Space upper bound | Remaining viewport relative to anchor | Using row upper bound directly on bottom-triggered triggers causes the window to go off-screen |\n\nThree rules:\n\n1. **Row height is measured, not assumed.** Rows with «embedding-only» descriptions are two lines and thus taller. Multiplying line count by fixed height causes half-rows near the upper bound. `ResizeObserver` follows late-loading web fonts.\n2. **The upper bound when nothing is constrained is not «measured content height».** Doing so means the box scrolls its own content the moment a row grows 1px due to subpixels or late fonts — verified in practice (all 7 items visible but `scrollHeight > clientHeight` so affordance falsely enabled). If unconstrained, the upper bound is **remaining space**.\n3. **Affordance only appears when actually clipped by the upper bound.** `listboxTopIsHidden` / `listboxBottomIsHidden` — same judgment as composer's `composerTopIsHidden`, syntax intentionally matched (if two surfaces solve the same problem differently, the next person won't know which to copy). If upper bound is not reached, there is no scrollbar at all due to `overflow: hidden`.\n\n### Settings Sheet Row Measurement Width (`--settings-content-measure`, 2026-08-02)\n\n| Token | Value | What it defines |\n|---|---|---|\n| `--settings-content-measure` | 658px | Maximum row width on **any face** of the settings sheet |\n\nThe sheet is fixed at 880×672, but row widths differed per face: root (LNB 2-tier) was `880 − 2 borders − 180 LNB − 40 right gap p-5 = 658px`; AI drill-in was `880 − 2 − 32 p-4 = 846px`. **As the drill-in detached from LNB, that 180px was consumed by content.** The increased 188px (+28.6%) carries 0 information, but `justify-between` rows spread ends further as width increases, making the gap between «Anthropic ‥‥‥ [Key Register]» entirely empty space (owner flagged twice).\n\n**Constrain the row, not the sheet.** Sheet size is owner-confirmed fixed value (2026-07-29); reducing it breaks root LNB 2-tier and «Expand» section together. And merely reducing width does not prevent recurrence — widening the sheet next time brings the same bug back.\n\nThe value is not preference but **the exact derived value from the root face**; if derivation drifts, `tests/contract/settings-sheet-content-measure.contract.test.ts` catches it (token must follow regardless of changes to sheet width·LNB width·padding).\n\n**Prose is narrower than this** — reuse `--git-setup-measure` (520px). Measurement widths for reading and manipulating differ; do not create new tokens with the same value.\n\n### EmptyState (#16)\n\n- **Slots** — `icon` (line-art glyph, muted rounded rect) · `skeleton` (true = default muted 3-line bar, or custom ReactNode) · `title` (single-line plain text) · `description` (next action guidance) · `action` (selection button).\n- **Tone/Alignment** — `tone` dashed (inside lists/cards, signals «filling spot») | solid, `align` left (default) | center (entire page body empty situation).\n- Empty charts/lists show **filling form (skeleton)** first instead of «long whitespace» — applied to current insight «most needed items» / «hub» empty areas.\n\n### Control Height Tokens (#13)\n\n```\n--control-h-sm: 28px;\n--control-h-md: 32px;   /* Select size=\"md\", dense form controls */\n--control-h-lg: 40px;   /* Select default trigger */\n--control-row-h: calc(var(--control-h-md) + 12px);  /* = 44px, list row containing controls */\n```\n\n- **`--control-row-h` (2026-07-26)** — List row height where buttons/controls sit. Must not equal control height: owner feedback («key register button looks too cramped») stemmed from [AI Connection] vendor row height 32px = button height, leaving 0 vertical margin above/below the button. Three rows touched each other with only a 1px divider between, making the three buttons read as one block. Write as an **expression** so rows grow when controls grow. Resulting 44px matches `--touch-target-min` in value and rationale — fingers and eyes read boundaries via padding around controls.\n  In expanded lists, **expanded card headers must also use this token** to maintain rhythm and name column alignment with other rows (dimensional regularity).\n- Chrome fill/tiles continue using separate lock token `--chrome-tile-size` (36px) — this control scale is for interactive controls **outside** the chrome system (canonical Select, form inputs, etc.). The old `--dialog-w-lg: 720` was removed because it was a ghost with zero consumers and zero definitions — unused tokens are not specifications, they are misinformation. If a new level is needed, convening the \"System\" team comes first.\n- Single source of truth for centered modal/composer width; primary consumer is `Dialog`\n  (`src/shared/ui/dialog.tsx`). It stays read-only: every page and target mtime must be checked before\nhuman approval, and Atlas still never patches or finalizes meaning automatically.\n\n```\ninput (humans + AI agents)     parse           store              output\n        │                       │                │                │\n        ▼                       ▼                ▼                ▼\n  .md in vault  →          frontmatter   →  user disk      →  Topology (/, /topology) map + INDEX\n  (frontmatter)                              (vault)           Topology contextual write + review\n  + AI agent (MCP)                                            Docs workspace (/docs)\n                                                              Insights (/ontology/insights) maintenance board\n                                                              compatibility redirects (/ontology, /ontology/edit, /ontology/studio)\n```\n\n### Web and app do not promise the same screens (2026-07-27)\n\nDecided in `docs/DECISIONS.md`; the enforceable version is\n`.claude/rules/surfaces.md`. It is one codebase and one build — the app loads\nthe same static export in a WebView — so this is a capability table, not a\nfeature-parity backlog. **Desktop capabilities ship without a web equivalent,\non purpose.** What the web owes instead is an honest degradation: why it cannot\nwork here, and where it can.\n\n| Capability | Web (Chromium) | Desktop app (macOS · Windows x64 beta) | Why they differ |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Open the map with no install | ✅ | ✅ | the web's first job — gateway |\n| Open your own markdown folder | ✅ File System Access API | ✅ absolute path | Firefox and non-FSA browsers degrade to a notice + download link |\n| Read / edit / create nodes in that folder | ✅ | ✅ | same parser, same schema, same files |\n| Remember the folder between visits | ❌ pick it again | ✅ | web keeps an FSA handle in its own IndexedDB; a convenience cache, not the source of truth |\n| Work offline | ❌ | ✅ | |\n| Git history and snapshots | ❌ degraded card + `ontology-atlas snapshot` | ✅ | a browser has no right to run git on your machine |\n| API keys / in-app **agent** chat | ❌ **and will not be built** | ✅ native credential store | keys in browser storage leak to a single XSS, and vendors name the direct-call header `…-dangerous-direct-browser-access` |\n| Write agent config (`.mcp.json`) into the vault | ⚠️ folder writes work, but there is no absolute path to record | ✅ | MCP registration needs a real path |\n| In-app updates | ❌ | ✅ | |\n\n**Windows today**: an unsigned x64 beta carries the same local folder and MCP\nsurface as the desktop app. `/download` states the SmartScreen unknown-publisher\nand managed-PC risk before the executable CTA. Chrome or Edge remains the\ninstall-free fallback when that warning or an organization policy is a blocker;\nthe web still does not offer BYOK or MCP registration.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Mode branching (data source)\n\n`useDataSourceMode()` resolves to one of two modes (R10b: cloud / auth surface permanently removed):\n\n| Mode | Condition | Behavior |\n|---|---|---|\n| **local** | a vault folder is active — picked in the installed app, or in an FSA-capable browser | vault manifest is the source of truth |\n| **static** | no active vault | build-time dogfood manifest (this project's own ontology) |\n\n**Effect**: when a user opens a vault folder in the installed app, `/`, `/topology`, `/projects`, `/project/[slug]`, `/ontology`, and `/ontology/insights` all switch to vault data instantly. Mutations (create / edit / connect) are mode-aware: local → show an exact change review, then write to vault `.md`; static → ask for a writable folder instead of presenting a dead editor.\n\n**Bootstrap from existing docs (2026-07-20, Slice 1)**: opening a folder that\nalready has markdown but no `kind:` frontmatter used to strand the user on a\n\"0 concepts\" map with misdirected copy. Now the topology empty state\nacknowledges the found documents (\"Found N documents\") and offers **Create map from my docs** — a blocking dialog that proposes candidates from the already\nscanned manifest (root README → project title · 1-depth folders → domains ·\neach doc → element with `domain:`), and on confirm writes ONLY frontmatter to\nthe accepted docs (bodies untouched) plus one new `project.md`. Pure candidate\nderivation: `src/features/docs-vault-local/lib/bootstrap-candidates.ts` — the\nbrowser equivalent of CLI `bootstrap` / MCP `analyze_repo_structure`, so all\nthree ingress paths converge on the same shape. Plain-language copy: the\ndialog never says \"ontology\" (map-building framing for non-experts).\n\n**Meaning & time surfaces (2026-07-21 execution run, PRs #425–#449)**:\n- **Edge popover** — edges are first-class clickable objects on the map: a\n  click within 7px opens a popover with a plain-language sentence (\"A leans\n  on B\"), the formal type, both endpoints (click = focus), the declaring\n  `.md` (with its change-date label), an optional **why** line\n  (`relation_notes`), and an edit-relation deep link.\n- **Relation rationale (why)** — `relation_notes: {ref: one-line-why}` in\n  frontmatter; MCP `add_relation` takes `why` and writes relation + note in\n  ONE frontmatter write; `rename_concept` rewrites note keys (collision:\n  existing new-key note wins).\n- **Agent connect sheet** — INDEX footer agent status opens a sheet:\n  heartbeat-file connection state, Claude Code/.mcp.json + Codex + generic\n  registration snippets (desktop autofills the path), config-file writer on\n  desktop, and an agent-brief preview that speaks the user's own domain\n  names. **Scope segment** — *this folder* (the app writes `.mcp.json` /\n  `.codex/config.toml` / `.cursor/mcp.json` / `.agents/mcp_config.json`\n  inside the vault, so a `git diff` shows it) or *this whole computer*\n  (the app writes nothing outside the vault; it hands you a ready command\n  or settings block with the absolute vault path already filled in, and\n  says plainly that a home-folder change will not appear in `git diff`).\n  Claude Code's global path is a `claude mcp add --scope user` command\n  because `~/.claude.json` is a file Claude Code rewrites at runtime.\n  Default is *this folder*; your pick is remembered.\n- **Hierarchy ink ladder** — containment edges carry depth (L0 project\n  spine → L2 leaf) as width×value (never hue); pass-through edges (both\n  endpoints off-screen) get demoted ink; `depends` bows are\n  direction-consistent perpendicular offsets (mutual pairs separate).\n- **Magnitude & type scale** — domain/capability radii encode descendant\n  count (log-compressed); labels/engraved numerals scale sub-linearly with\n  zoom (widthCache keys include quantized font size).\n- **First-map reveal** — after \"Create map from my docs\", nodes assemble out\n  of the project position and spring-settle into place (reduced-motion\n  arrives instantly).\n- **Idle frame gate** — the canvas stops physics+paint after 1.2s of true\n  idle (rAF stays alive; any state change resumes next frame).\n- **Canonical census** — every surface that says \"N concepts\" uses one\n  derivation (`computeCanonicalCensus`). Topology, Docs, Workshop, Insights,\n  and Projects read the same file-backed scope; a surface-specific subset is\n  labeled as a subset rather than silently presenting it as the vault total.\n- **Docs library on the web** — the local-vault gate is capability-based\n  (File System Access), not runtime-based: the same browser session that\n  writes via Workshop or the document editor can read/edit in the docs\n  library.\n- **Relation vocabulary** — one dictionary (formal/plain × 7 types × ko/en)\n  feeds the map legend, Insights, Workshop, and datasheet (contract-tested);\n  the \"?\" sheet footer defines domain/capability/element in plain language.\n\n**Single source of truth (R8)**: `LocalVaultProvider` mounts once in `app/[locale]/layout.tsx`. Its many `useLocalVault()` consumers (`RootEntryPage` / `AppNavRail` / `HomePage` / `DocsVaultPage` / `useDataSourceMode` / `useProjects` / `useProjectMutations` / `useVaultOntology` and the persistent app shell) share one state instance, one IDB rehydrate, one filesystem walk.\n\n**Desktop first-run (2026-07-18)**: in the installed app (Tauri — detected via\n`isDesktopShell()`, `src/shared/lib/desktop-shell.ts`), `/` with no vault\nrenders an Obsidian-style **FirstRunPage** (`src/views/first-run/`): four\nmachined cards — **just start** (2026-07-23, Tauri runtime only — no folder\npicker at all: creates `~/Documents/Ontology Atlas/<name>` on real disk\nautomatically, numbering `-2`/`-3` on a name clash, connects it, then reuses\nthe same `scaffoldOntology()` seed as \"create new vault\", and the success\ntoast names the exact path — real disk, not OPFS, so an AI agent/MCP can\nstill read it; hidden when the real Tauri invoke bridge is absent, e.g. a dev\n`?shell=desktop` browser override) / open vault folder / create new vault\n(existing `scaffoldOntology()` when the picked folder is empty — 5 markdown\nseeds + agent configs + the agent guide pair + 3 procedure skills) / browse the\nbuilt-in demo vault — plus a local-first trust line. No download CTA inside the\ninstalled app.\n\n**Vault-carried agent skills (2026-08-17)**: every scaffolded vault — CLI `init`\nand the in-app/web starter alike — ships `.claude/skills/atlas-{review,grow,absorb}/SKILL.md`.\nThe app launches the coding agent with the vault as its working folder, so these\nappear directly in the composer's `/` menu tagged `(project)`; measured on a\nfreshly initialized vault, they take the first three slots of the 50 commands an\napp session offers. They encode order and stopping conditions the tool list\nalone cannot: review reads `validate_vault` + `health` and writes nothing, grow\nfilters `growth_plan` candidates against evidence before proposing, absorb checks\nfor duplicates before extracting. All three refuse to write until a person picks.\nByte-parity between the CLI templates and the web starter constants is gated by\n`tests/contract/starter-templates.contract.test.ts`.\n\n**Web root-first-open (2026-07-18, superseded 2026-07-30)**: on hosted web, `/` no longer showed a\nmarketing landing page at all — with no vault selected it renders `HomePage`\n(the same topology hub `/topology` uses) drawing this project's own dogfood\nsample, read-only, plus a **first-run starter module** integrated into the\nINDEX panel itself (no floating card/dock — `FirstRunStarterModule`,\n`src/features/first-run-starter/`): census meters (concepts/relations/\ndomains, real data — if screen language is Korean, labels are also concepts/relations/domains) +\n\"open my markdown folder\" + \"create a new vault\" + \"just looking around\"\ndismiss (sessionStorage — reappears next session, not on reload).\n2026-07-24 first-use flow refinement: the two buttons to open a folder do not\nimmediately open the OS file picker but instead open a **pre-informative sheet** (`VaultOpenGuideSheet`,\n`src/features/docs-vault-local/`) first — three lines to ease concerns (any markdown folder is fine / Atlas opens it locally and does not upload it to an Atlas backend; a connected coding agent is a separate provider boundary / if empty, starter docs are created automatically) and a branch to choose an existing folder or start fresh with an empty one. The card also includes a \"2-minute tour\" button and a \"Show plain language\" toggle (bringing the 'normal' mode from the gear menu into the card).\nImmediately after opening an empty vault, instead of text suggesting there's nothing more to do, a **start checklist** (`VaultStartChecklist`, `src/widgets/topology-controls/`) appears — per owner instruction (2026-07-24 2nd round), it's a **3-step process to attach AI agent first**: connect AI agent (determine actual connection via heartbeat file) → hand over first analysis (copy instructions to paste into the agent) → create directly (optional, project type preset writer).\nThe incorrect guidance branch recommending macOS installation on the web has been removed. On first visit, the folder guide sheet opens automatically first (once only, with a skip option); if the user opens a folder directly in this session, the AI agent connection sheet follows automatically once. A brand-pill `SAMPLE` badge and a bottom-right map readout (\"N project · N domains ·\nSpine view · zoom in to reveal elements\") stay visible for the whole static\nsession regardless of whether the starter module was dismissed. The former\n`LandingPage` and its hero/value-chain/evidence-instrument content moved to\n`/download` (see below) — a returning user whose vault handle restores from\nIndexedDB goes straight to their own workspace, no starter surfaces at all.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Routes\n\n> The route inventory itself is `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — this section describes what\n> each surface *does for a user*, not how many there are. A count here rots on the next\n> route and nothing gates it (it said 12 while listing 15, 2026-07-31).\n\n### `/` — Smart entry\n\n- **Hosted web, no vault** → the **gateway face** — headline, download, and \"open it in the browser\" — the same view `/download` renders (2026-07-30 — reversed the previous decision to open the map directly from the root). Judged by `isGatewaySurface()`.\n- **Desktop app, no restored vault** → `FirstRunPage` (just start / open / create / browse demo), not the hosted intro\n- **Recent desktop vaults** → the picker stores recently opened Tauri vault paths, can reopen them without another Finder selection, and can remove stale paths from the list\n- **Vault loaded (web or desktop)** → `HomePage` — the topology hub for that vault (map + INDEX concept panel + node datasheet), the same component `/topology` renders (B3 decision [\"Don't keep a separate hub; the map takes its place\"] — the old tree/ego hub, `OntologyViewPage`, is retired; `/ontology` now redirects here with INDEX expanded). Restoring a previously-opened vault handle from IndexedDB goes straight here — no starter surfaces, no re-clicking through first-run every visit\n- **Switch vault mid-session**: the topology settings gear (⚙, top-right utility rail) has a \"switch vault\" row → `/docs/?intent=local`, alongside the `/docs` vault pill's own \"swap\" control\n\n### `/download` — the install decision (remade 2026-07-27)\n\n**This screen's job, in one sentence**: *a first-time visitor chooses their\nplatform, understands its trust state, and gets the matching installer without\nhunting for it.* Everything on the page earns its place against\nthat sentence; the remake removed what could not (a second landing hero, a\nKorean-only changelog excerpt, 12 same-weight boxes, and the signing copy that\nhad become false).\n\n- **Decision first, at full column width**: eyebrow → headline → one-paragraph lead → the macOS decision card. The card is the widest thing above the fold because it is the most important; it used to sit inside a half-width column under a taller figure.\n- **One filled indigo button per release state, and it is the one that works.** Generated GitHub Release facts select the CTA: published assets show their real platform/architecture download and size; an unavailable asset gets honest pending copy instead of a dead release button. The releases link stays at lower weight.\n- **Architecture help is on the page, not assumed**: \"Apple menu → About This Mac; if *Chip* begins with Apple M, it's Apple Silicon\". Naming both architectures and stopping there left the majority of visitors — who do not know which Mac they own — stuck in front of two buttons.\n- **One release-state source**: everything the page may claim about a build comes from `src/views/download/model/macos-release.generated.ts`, written by `pnpm download:release-facts` out of the real GitHub Release. Published macOS → per-architecture DMGs; published Windows → the x64 NSIS installer; both carry real byte size, filename, direct URL, and copyable SHA-256. Unpublished → plain pending copy instead of placeholder facts. There is no state where the page shows a size or checksum that does not exist.\n- **Trust is four facts with their proofs, not a paragraph**: Developer ID signing (`codesign verified`) · Apple notarization + stapling (`stapler validate passes`) · a published SHA-256 per file with the verify command built from the current version's real DMG name · and *what Atlas does not do* — no Atlas account or backend; the vault remains disk-backed and Atlas itself does not upload it. A connected coding agent may send prompts and the context or MCP results it reads to its own provider. Signing is stated as a property of the release path and drift-guarded by `release-facts.test.ts` against the real `desktop:release-artifact` chain (`desktop:sign` → `desktop:notarize` → `desktop:verify-release-dmg --require-signed --require-notarized`), so the claim cannot outlive the pipeline that backs it.\n- **After-install path in three steps** — drag to Applications and launch · point it at a markdown folder · connect your AI assistant (tool and command counts derived from `mcp/src/index.js` and `cli/src/lib/cli-commands.mjs`, both drift-guarded) — plus the fact that makes this page a one-time visit: the installed app updates itself with one button (#726).\n- **Windows x64 beta**: a published unsigned NSIS installer appears in its own platform section inside the same decision plate. The static warning precedes the outline CTA and names SmartScreen's unknown-publisher warning and managed-PC blocking. Native Windows CI requires dependency audits, Microsoft Defender scan, silent install, app launch, and the installed MCP sidecar smoke; it does not claim to have verified the Windows 11 SmartScreen UI.\n- **Evidence figure**: the dogfood instrument (project hex + domain chips + hub capability circle, real `docs/ontology` census — `src/views/download/model/dogfood-census.generated.ts`, built by `scripts/build-docs-vault.mjs`) now sits beside step 02, the one place it is an answer rather than decoration, with its scope caption (\"counts this repo's own vault, not yours\").\n- **Secondary CTA**: \"Go to GitHub\" → GitHub repo, as a visible medium outline button rather than a small source footnote.\n- **Motion**: none on entrance (first painted frame is identical to the settled frame across every node in `#main`). The budget goes to the attention winner alone — the filled CTA eases on `--motion-base` + `--motion-ease` with a 6.1% first-frame share — and `prefers-reduced-motion` lands it instantly. The previous page inverted this: a staggered fade ran on background cards while the winner hard-cut.\n- **Live deploy verification**: `pnpm desktop:verify-hosted` checks the deployed `wlsdks.github.io/ontology-atlas` root/download pages after the Pages workflow deploys; on a published release it also runs `pnpm desktop:verify-download` for that tag. It asserts only **server-rendered** text: a loaded-vault map hydrates client-side, so its in-app CTAs never reach the static HTML — expecting them is what kept this gate failing on every Pages deploy while the site itself was fine (5/5 runs red, 2026-07-26~27). Expected download copy is read from `messages/ko.json` instead of duplicated in the checker, so the contract is \"the page renders its own copy\" and cannot drift: title, source-code CTA, both platform headings, the Windows beta trust state, the hosted-site scope note, a stable GitHub Releases href, and no `/releases/latest` dependency.\n- **Privacy note**: the installed app and vault data use local disk as the source of truth; `/docs`'s own local-source *browsing* tab stays desktop-only (unrelated to opening your primary vault from `/`)\n- **Footer**: license · GitHub · stack chips · `LocaleSwitch`\n\n### `/` (with a loaded vault) and `/topology` — canvas-2D topology hub\n\n`/topology` renders `HomePage`; `/` renders it after a vault is loaded (R3 keep-both decision: `/` = home/back-link target, `/topology` = explicit deep-link namespace). Without a vault, `/` follows the gateway/desktop first-run branches above.\n\n#### Analysis modes + workflow entry points\n- **Overview (default)** — the canvas-2D Topology map with deterministic\n  project/domain/hub structure and bounded ForceAtlas2 settling: the read-first\n  decision surface.\n- Focus/path/health are **not separate canvases**:\n  - **Focus** — enters via node click on the map (selection state); `mode=focus` deep links preserved\n  - **Path** — enters via shift-click of 2 nodes or `mode=path` deep links\n  - **Health** — enters via the maintenance queue count chip on the view rail; `mode=health` deep links preserved\n\n#### Canvas (`topology-map-v2` — custom canvas-2D engine + Graphology ForceAtlas2 physics)\n- **Click node** → right-side panel opens (`ProjectDrawer` for project nodes, the 352px node datasheet for domain/capability/element nodes — see \"Node datasheet\" below)\n- **Drag node** → reposition (releases back to physics)\n- **Double-click node** → \"local graph\" mode (2-hop neighbors only, breadcrumb: `Local · Root · slugA · slugB`, click to backtrack, Esc to exit)\n- **Right-click node** → context menu (Focus / Local graph / Copy detail URL)\n- **Shift-click 2 nodes** → highlight shortest path\n- **Dense-group cluster chips** → a parent with more than 12 direct children (e.g. a domain with 108 capabilities) folds its whole subtree into a single `+N` chip instead of spilling hundreds of overlapping nodes/labels. Click the chip to expand just that parent (nodes fan out as a bounded phyllotaxis disk); click the `−` chip to collapse again. Expanded parents live in the URL (`?open=slug1,slug2`) so a shared link or an AI agent reproduces the same expansion. Nested dense children get their own chips once their parent is expanded.\n- **Expand all** → the top action opens every containment parent in one step and\n  fits every rendered node inside the map. It is a temporary overview, not a\n  saved default; pressing it again collapses the batch. A route arriving with\n  existing `?open=` parents also uses full-bounds fitting on its first frame so\n  already-open nodes do not begin off screen.\n- **How the chip looks and where children land is a setting** (Settings › Expand, 2026-08-01 — ported from the `.qa-scratch/proto-expand.html` measurement prototype). Five values: the open control (`floating pill` · **`bar above`, default** · `shoulder badge`), the child layout (`spiral disk`, default · `fan` · `ring` · `column`), and three numbers — how many open at once (4–24, default 24), how many names are attempted per parent (3–40, default 8), and how many parents stay open at once (1–6, default 3). The default control is the bar docked directly above the **selected** node: nothing shows until you select a node, and the folded count keeps living on the node body. Rationale and the observation that would reverse it: `docs/DECISIONS.md`.\n- **Expand realm** → focus a node (click) and an orbital **Expand realm** button appears just outside its ring (also offered as an action in the node datasheet, for container nodes). Activating it transforms the map into *that node's world*: only its containment subtree remains, re-laid-out with the node as a temporary root at the origin (children map to rings by **depth**, not kind), and everything outside unmounts behind a 1px indigo warding circle. Relations crossing the boundary fade to a stub at the ring. The transition is a 600ms choreography — outside nodes fling out along curved \"gravity\" trajectories, inside nodes FLIP to their new spots, the camera dollies in to fit the realm (`prefers-reduced-motion` snaps instantly). The active realm lives in the URL (`?realm=slug`) so a shared link or an AI agent reproduces the same world; a top-center **Realm: {title} ✕** chip and **Esc** (highest ladder priority) return to the full map. Click, `?open` density gating, selective ego, and top-K labels all still work inside a realm.\n- **Ontology block exchange** — feature to exchange concept bundles folder-by-folder. INDEX's\n  **Import Block** reads `.md` folders and, if present, `block-manifest.json`, showing **only what is coming in and what conflicts with existing files first**\n  (dry-run — running it tentatively without writing anything). Then only the files approved by the person are written via the vault's existing `createDoc` path. **Export this realm's source .mds as a block folder** on the realm expansion screen copies only the source files of the child nodes contained in that realm. The folder picker window uses\n  `showDirectoryPicker()` on the web, and Tauri's own picker following the same `FileSystemDirectoryHandle`\n  protocol on the installed app. Canceling that window is neither an error nor a write. For terminal-only use, run `ontology-atlas import <path...>`.\n- **Tab** → keyboard cycle to neighbor hub\n- **Empty state** (0–1 nodes) → `TopologyEmptyState` explains whether the\n  vault lacks projects or relations, then offers the applicable next actions:\n  bootstrap from found docs, create a node, open Topology INDEX, open Workshop,\n  or choose a vault.\n- **Filter active** → bottom-left \"filter · N / TOTAL\" badge\n\n#### `TopologyFitControl` (top-right, desktop-only)\n- Single **Fit Map** tile — fits the camera to the graph bounds. The top and vertical map controls on the left side of the panel are attached 12px from each side of the seam, totaling a 24px gap, moving in sync with the dock's timing and curvature.\n- From the first frame of opening the panel, the header, empty conversation prompt, current folder recommendations, and input box are all visible in their final positions. Expanding it when needed reveals both the original order and target nodes, with thought Markdown rendered as actual bold, code, and lists.\n- GFM tables in agent responses appear as real tables with headers, row dividers, and cell padding. The two slugs from `find_path` reveal the exact shortest path nodes and relationship lines. Only typed Atlas read tools in the same turn are used as input; response sentences or non-existent names are not used as basis for map movement. The streamed input completing the initial `tool_call` via `tool_call_update.rawInput` is also merged into the same tool row.\n- If there is no project source connected to the starter vault, \"Code Scan\" is not executed first. \"Connect Code Folder First\" navigates to the project data sheet, and only after re-reading the connection on the same screen does the source-evidence-first build prompt appear.\n- **First 3 words** (`buildFirstWords`) — When the conversation is empty, up to three sentences extracted from the actual state of this folder appear: ① The biggest gap in the currently viewed concept ② The concept first pointed out by the \"To-do\" list (the function used for judgment is the same `detectMeaningGaps`) ③ The ever-present \"Where is the strangest place on this map right now?\"\n- **Zero model calls to create these sentences** — These sentences are already drawn on screen *before* the user clicks [Send]. Therefore, sending a request to create them would be an unauthorized transmission, using the user's own API costs (BYOK) without permission. The code creating these sentences is pure and does not import any transmission code (`tests/contract/agent-first-words-local.contract.test.ts`).\n- **Clicking only fills the input box; it does not send** — Clicking places that sentence into the input box, selecting all text and focusing it. You can edit and send it or delete it. The button does not disappear even after clicking.\n- **Does not force-fill 3 items** — In an empty folder, only one appears (\"Let's organize what product we're making from scratch\"); if there is no concept being viewed, ① is omitted; in a folder with nothing to fix, only ③ remains. Regardless of sentence length, **the height of one button is always the same** (measured at 1512×950: 44px for both 1 and 3 items, input box position remains unchanged).\n- **\"You can ask things like this\" shown when no key or folder exists is also created by the same code** — The sentences are identical, differing only in appearance (a plain list instead of buttons). No clickable buttons are created for tasks that cannot be executed to completion.\n- **Next step** — Makes the model mention one empty spot next to it **within the very response** where it suggests fixing the document (the `NEXT:` line in the system prompt). This line becomes a single button. By filling the input box **without calling the LLM again**, it prevents the ongoing suggestion from doubling.\n- **Continues even if the conversation disconnects** — Starting a new conversation includes the **most recently applied changes** to this folder (git history up to 5 lines, max 120 characters per line) as context. Conversation content itself is not saved — changed content remains in frontmatter and git, becoming the context for the next conversation.\n- **Summary of this conversation** — The subtitle in the header changes to \"N concepts · M connections in this conversation\" (counting only those successfully saved). Only the text changes; the line's position and size remain the same.\n- **Same sentences even when coming from another screen** — The \"Ask by Voice\" button in node details and \"Agent by Voice\" in the `⋮` menu of insight list rows use **the same sentences created by the same code** as the buttons above. What the address (`?ask=missing-definition|missing-domain|missing-relations`) carries when coming from insights is **only the type of request**; the actual sentence is created by the arriving screen in its language. Since the address is the state, pressing back restores the same context, and closing the panel removes the request along with it.\n- **Non-overlapping** — While the panel is open, the info area of the selected node shifts inward by the panel's width (they are a pair meant to be read together). The timing and acceleration curve of this shift match exactly how the panel opens.\n- **14-inch top chrome also yields the same width** — If there is a selected node info area, the top map tools move to the remaining center of the map excluding that area. When the agent dock opens, central/right button labels collapse into icons by density so two absolute lanes do not overlap.\n- **Map camera also reads remaining width in the same clock** — On every frame where the agent dock's width changes, the current view among full/selected node/area/path/full lens follows the new available area, confirming target and speed together on the last frame. Thus, the camera does not start separately or bounce behind the dock, and manually panned/zoomed screens are not taken away. When closing node details, it does not incorrectly leave the exiting panel's width as the final overview safe zone.\n- **Work status and notifications do not open separate windows for the same fact** — The work status row opens only current agent/steps/target; the independent bell in the top-right toolbar opens only notifications and work receipts. Unread counts are overlapping badges within the bell, not increasing the square tile width. The notification panel uses `--topology-v2-panel-width` to secure a reading width up to 352px. The status row itself uses natural content width rather than short toolbar width, stopping only at 520px, so agent name and last work time are not cut off first.\n- **Start conversation directly from the agent destination** — The large \"Open Conversation with this Tool\" button of the prepared executor places the runtime id in the queue for the session only and navigates to `/topology`. The map consumes the queue once to open the dock only when executor detection ends and the same id is ready.\n- **Give meaning to top/bottom margins (2026-07-28)** — While keys are not yet connected, **top** means \"what can be asked,\" **bottom** means \"what is needed + buttons to do it,\" and **center** is where the conversation will appear (answers actually appear there upon sending). During conversation or when asking for consent, content grows from the bottom, bringing answers and clickable buttons closer. Measured at 1512×950: The two previously meaningless empty margins (top 361px · bottom 361px) were merged into one meaningful space, and during conversation, the margin reduced from 639 → 512px.\n- **Bottom leaves only one input box (2026-07-28)** — View instructions and send to terminal are not always visible; you press a single line below the input box to expand/collapse it (only one area expands at a time — no stacking multiple temporary screens). The guidance sentence \"AI in the terminal is better for tasks requiring code review\" also moved into this collapsible area. The height permanently occupied at the bottom reduced from 176 → 104px.\n- **Make the promise to ask before saving readable on the decision screen (2026-07-28)** — The sentence \"If a document needs fixing, show the changes first; confirmation is required for saving\" appears on **both** the screen deciding whether to entrust the API key and the consent sheet. Previously, this sentence was nowhere on screen until the suggestion card appeared.\n- **\"Unconfirmed words\" warning only applies to the final answer of that turn (2026-07-28)** — Intermediate speech by the model before calling tools (\"I'll read first\") is not a claim about vault content. Thus, the highest-level warning repeated three times per turn was reduced to once.\n- **Way back when failing (2026-07-28)** — Failure notifications are drawn with the same weight as the body (previously the least noticeable line on screen). A button is also attached that puts the just-sent message back into the input box — it only puts it there; it does not send it.\n\n#### Agent work visibility\n\n- The status line in the map utility lane does not expose raw transport names directly.\n  Audit `codex-mcp-client`/`codex-acp` are preserved in logs and displayed as `Codex` on screen,\n  Claude/Cursor/others are shown by each product/agent name.\n- **Only fresh valid heartbeats are live.** Live status shows planning/editing/verifying/blocked\n  as Planning/Editing/Verifying/Awaiting Approval. Three facts the app already knows drive the row actions: ① can this session write to the vault ② has an agent been observed in this folder (heartbeat) ③ does this concept own a document (`hasOwnDocument`). Read-only sample → 「Edit in Workshop」 becomes 「View in Workshop」 plus a copyable command, and the group order flips (hand-off work first, since hand-off is the only completion this session has).
