Thus, ACP is not a replacement for MCP servers but a path that sits on top of them. capabilities/reviewed-ontology-writing: \"ACP permission requests reuse the reviewed ontology writing contract: read tools continue, while write tools pause on the shared typed change review before allow_once or reject_once.\" }\nrelates: [capabilities/reviewed-ontology-writing]\n---\n\n## Definition\n\nThe ability to detect ACP (Agent Client Protocol) v1 coding-agent executors already installed on the device, directly launch only those with a verified app-owned permission gate (currently Claude Agent), and apply scoped permission review. No new Atlas API key or vendor integration is needed: it uses the subscription authentication already held by the launched tool.\n\n\n## Behaviour Contract\n\nTen things this capability actually does:\n\n1. **Detection.** The executor status of this device is divided into five categories: `ready`, `cli-missing`, `node-missing`, `uvx-missing`, and `binary-missing`. The reason for not collapsing the status into just \"installed/not installed\" is that the user's required actions differ for each state.\n2. **The list comes from a committed snapshot.** The ACP registry is fetched once at build time and saved to `src-tauri/src/acp-registry.json`; icons are also bundled into `public/acp-icons/`. The committed registry and icons require no runtime network lookup. Starting a selected coding agent is a separate boundary: that agent may communicate with its own provider.\n3. **Configuration isolation.** Sessions launched by the app use its own configuration directory within the app data folder (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`). Inheriting the user's global settings would mean the app cannot block anything for users who have set \"allow all\" in their terminal. Credentials are not copied but pointed to via symbolic links.\n4. **Permission judgment.** Atlas read tools inside the selected vault proceed automatically. Atlas write tools pause on the shared typed change review and continue only after `allow_once`; `reject_once` cancels them. Other requests are judged by scope: inside-vault paths may proceed, while outside or unresolved paths ask the user. The basis for path judgment is not the title string but the `toolCall.rawInput.file_path` (absolute path) from the original permission request. The vault root is verified and normalized by `acp_start` and bound to the native session rather than trusted from each screen request. If the session is missing or the root is invalid, the app asks. If the root path changes to an external symbolic link after session start, normalized-path mismatch rejects it so the boundary cannot shift during the session.\n5. **Working directory hygiene.** The working directory of a session must pass the same vault root judgment as the folder picker. Filesystem roots, the home directory itself, and OS/app directories are rejected.\n6. **Workflow safety state.** Modes provided by the adapter are categorized as verified, risky, or unverified. Verified modes are hidden by removing permission checks, while unverified modes are preserved in `AcpSessionChoices.unverifiedModeIds` to display \"unverified\" along with its meaning in the existing selector.\n7. **Process tree termination.** Children have their own process group; termination sends SIGTERM and waits up to 1 second before sending SIGKILL to terminate the entire group. Completion is determined by the survival of the original PGID, not the leader PID, so grandchildren that ignore TERM are not missed even if the leader is reaped first. If grandchildren launched by the adapter are not terminated together, processes will remain after the app is closed.\n\n8. **Map synchronization.** Compares the typed input of actually called Atlas `get_concept` and `find_path` in the current user turn against the current vault's slug table, then moves to the same HomePage node focus or exact shortest path lens. Natural language answers or non-existent slugs are not used as map movement grounds. The actual order in which the Claude adapter completes streamed input with status-less `tool_call_update.rawInput` after a pending `tool_call` is merged into the same tool action before determining intent.\n9. **Inset conversation surface.** Maintains the outer flex dock that actually yields map width, but displays the ACP/API-key conversation surface visible to the user within the top/bottom/right spacing ramp. It shares INDEX/node inspector's existing panel radius, border, surface, and shadow so it doesn't look like a black wall covering the window height without boundaries. The map control rail on the left of the panel is also pulled to 12px on the opposite side of the seam, limiting the gap between them to 24px, and moves with the same clock/curve as dock reflow.\n10. **First frame connection state.** Separates conversation scaffold from session booting; header, empty guidance, vault-derived suggestions, and composer are drawn from the first frame the dock opens. After the remaining 240ms landing of the camera live spring after width reflow, ACP start is allowed; in the meantime, only the spinner and `connecting` text of the same status badge change. For large panels, overlay fade is used without overlapping scale/translate chrome motion so that layout reflow becomes the primary action.\n\n## Boundaries\n- **The \"Agents\" destination (`/agents/`) and the conversation panel on the right of the home map are the current user surface.** Selecting a measured runtime for isolation gates opens `HomePage` which passes the current vault as working folder and MCP server to `AcpChatPanel`. \"Open chat with this tool\" at the destination puts the selected runtime id into a one-shot queue in sessionStorage, moves to the map, and is consumed only when HomePage confirms the same runtime's readiness. Paths that only send window events without subscribers in `/agents` are not used.\n\n  ⚠️ This line was *\"The 'Runtime' section of settings … is neither a separate path nor a new screen\"* until 2026-08-20. The archive (90) overturned it. Installation/connection is an operational task with progress status, not just picking values, so a blocking modal didn't fit the vessel. The same component (`AcpRuntimeSettings`) stands at both the destination and settings sheet; whether to draw an intro line is decided by the caller.\n- **Starter vault's project source comes first.** Without source binding, empty conversation recommendations open code folder connections from the project dataset instead of agent analysis, re-read sidecar transitions on the same screen, and only then provide the source-evidence-first build prompt.\n- **The session's vault MCP server maintains only one set.** Redundant injection is skipped only when a measured runtime already reads the same valid server from its vault config. That Codex self-read path is retained for external setup evidence, but it does not grant in-app chat eligibility.\n- **The app offers in-app chat only for a runtime with an app-owned permission gate, and today that is just `claude-acp`.** Others remain visible for detection and external connection setup. Codex `read-only` blocks direct file access, but an installed-app probe showed a self-registered Atlas MCP write could still run without a permission request, so Codex chat stays unavailable until the app owns that MCP checkpoint.\n- `isolated` reports Rust configuration isolation only. In-app eligibility additionally requires a proven ontology-write checkpoint and outside-folder gate; detection, external MCP setup, configuration isolation, and chat eligibility are distinct states. Unmeasured work modes in an eligible conversation remain explicitly unverified.\n- Permission verdict IPC receives only `sessionId` and request path. WebView has no argument to redeclare `vaultRoot` and change native session boundaries.\n- Browsers cannot launch processes. If `isAcpBridgeAvailable()` is false, the screen explains why it doesn't work and where it does.\n- Windows process tree ownership (Job Object) is outside this fragment. /**
 * **The app-owned write checkpoint.**
 *
 * ⚠️ Why this file exists (2026-08-24). The permission gate an agent shows is the
 * *agent's* gate, and it does not necessarily cover this server. Measured on the
 * installed `1.0.0-rc.10`: a Codex session running in `read-only` mode blocked
 * direct file writes, yet a self-registered Atlas `add_relation` changed the vault
 * with **no permission request and no review card**. Codex's `--ask-for-approval`
 * documents its scope plainly — it decides "when the model requires human approval
 * before executing **a command**" — so MCP tool calls were never in that scope. The
 * screen promised a gate the wire did not have, and Codex was removed from in-app
 * chat because of it (`docs/DECISIONS.md` 2026-08-24 (111)).
 *
 * That record also wrote down what would earn Codex its way back: *"an app-owned
 * MCP proxy or server capability token reliably pauses every Codex Atlas write."*
 * This is that checkpoint, and it lives where it belongs — **in the server that
 * performs the write**, not in a third party's config. A gate the vault owns holds
 * for every client that ever connects, not just the one that was measured.
 *
 * The mechanism is MCP elicitation (`elicitation/create`): before a write tool
 * touches disk, the server asks the connected client to put the question in front
 * of a person. `codex-acp` forwards `mcpServer/elicitation/request` into ACP
 * `session/request_permission`, which is the same permission card the app already
 * renders for Claude — so one server-side gate reaches both.
 *
 * **Fail closed.** If the gate is on and the client never declared the
 * `elicitation` capability, the write is refused rather than performed silently.
 * A checkpoint that waves traffic through when it cannot see is not a checkpoint;
 * that is precisely the failure this file was written to end.
 */

/** Same vocabulary as `OATLAS_READ_ONLY` so the two switches read alike. */
export function parseConsentEnv(value) {
  if (typeof value !== 'string') return false;
  return ['1', 'true', 'yes', 'on'].includes(value.trim().toLowerCase());
}

/**
 * A short, human-readable line naming what is about to change. It is the whole
 * question a person answers, so it must say the vault-visible effect — not the
 * tool's internal argument shape.
 */
export function describeWrite(toolName, args) {
  const a = args && typeof args === 'object' ? args : {};
  const slug = typeof a.slug === 'string' ? a.slug : null;
  const from = typeof a.from === 'string' ? a.from : null;
  const to = typeof a.to === 'string' ? a.to : null;
  const count = (key) => (Array.isArray(a[key]) ? a[key].length : null);

  switch (toolName) {
    case 'add_concept':
      return slug ? `Create concept ${slug}` : 'Create one concept';
    case 'add_concepts': {
      const n = count('concepts');
      return n === null ? 'Create concepts' : `Create ${n} concept(s)`;
    }
    case 'add_relation':
      return from && to ? `Link ${from} → ${to}` : 'Add one relation';
    case 'add_relations': {
      const n = count('relations');
      return n === null ? 'Add relations' : `Add ${n} relation(s)`;
    }
    case 'remove_relation':
      return from && to ? `Remove the link ${from} → ${to}` : 'Remove one relation';
    case 'replace_relation':
      return from && to ? `Replace the link ${from} → ${to}` : 'Replace one relation';
    case 'patch_concept':
      return slug ? `Edit concept ${slug}` : 'Edit one concept';
    case 'rename_concept':
      return from && to ? `Rename ${from} → ${to}` : 'Rename one concept';
    case 'reclassify_concept':
      return slug ? `Change the kind of ${slug}` : 'Change one concept kind';
    case 'merge_concepts':
      return from && to ? `Merge ${from} into ${to}` : 'Merge concepts';
    case 'delete_concept':
      return slug ? `Delete concept ${slug}` : 'Delete one concept';
    case 'absorb_document':
      return 'Absorb a document into typed nodes';
    case 'connect_project_source':
      return 'Connect a source folder to this vault';
    case 'disconnect_project_source':
      return 'Disconnect a source folder from this vault';
    case 'git_snapshot':
      return 'Commit the vault';
    case 'finalize_project_meaning':
      return 'Write the project meaning receipt';
    case 'index_project':
      return 'Write an index of the connected source';
    default:
      return `Run ${toolName}`;
  }
}

/**
 * A dry run asks for nothing: it reports a plan and leaves the disk alone, so
 * pausing it would train people to click through the very card that matters.
 * The flag name differs per tool, so both spellings are honoured.
 */
export function isDryRun(args) {
  if (!args || typeof args !== 'object') return false;
  return args.dryRun === true || args.dry_run === true;
}

export const CONSENT_DECLINED = 'consent-declined';
export const CONSENT_UNAVAILABLE = 'consent-unavailable';

/**
 * Ask the connected client to put this write in front of a person.
 *
 * `server` is the low-level SDK `Server`; `elicitInput` is its push-style
 * server→client request. Returns `{ allowed }` and, when refused, a `reason` the
 * caller turns into an error the agent can read and act on.
 */
export async function requestWriteConsent({ server, toolName, args, enabled }) {
  if (!enabled) return { allowed: true, asked: false };
  if (isDryRun(args)) return { allowed: true, asked: false };

  const capabilities =
    typeof server?.getClientCapabilities === 'function' ? server.getClientCapabilities() : undefined;
  if (!capabilities || !capabilities.elicitation) {
    return {
      allowed: false,
      asked: false,
      reason: CONSENT_UNAVAILABLE,
      message:
        `This vault requires a human decision before any write, and this client did not offer ` +
        `a way to ask (no "elicitation" capability was declared at initialize). No change was made. ` +
        `Use a client that can surface permission requests, or unset OATLAS_WRITE_CONSENT for a ` +
        `vault where the client owns the gate.`,
    };
  }

  const summary = describeWrite(toolName, args);
  let result;
  try {
    result = await server.elicitInput({
      mode: 'form',
      /*
       * ⚠️ **`confirm` is asked for, never required** (installed acceptance, 2026-08-24).
       *
       * It was `required: ['confirm']` at first, and that made the gate refuse **every** answer,
       * including yes. A form-capable client fills the boolean; an ACP bridge does not have one to
       * fill. `codex-acp` maps this request onto ACP `session/request_permission`, the app renders
       * its ordinary permission card, and pressing 「allow once」 comes back as `action: 'accept'`
       * with **no form content at all**. Codex reported it verbatim: *"the permission response was
       * invalid because it lacked the required `confirm` field"* — the write was refused, twice,
       * after a person had said yes.
       *
       * A checkpoint that cannot be passed is not a checkpoint, it is a wall, and a wall teaches
       * people to route around the gate. So the boolean stays as the **form** spelling of the
       * question, and `action` stays the answer.
       */
      message: `${summary}. Apply this change to the vault?`,
      requestedSchema: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          confirm: {
            type: 'boolean',
            title: 'Apply this change',
            description: `${toolName} — ${summary}`,
          },
        },
      },
    });
  } catch (error) {
    // A transport error, a timeout, or a client that advertised the capability
    // and then refused the method all land here. None of them is a yes.
    return {
      allowed: false,
      asked: true,
      reason: CONSENT_UNAVAILABLE,
      message:
        `Asking for permission failed (${error?.message ?? 'unknown error'}). No change was made.`,
    };
  }

  /*
   * **`action` is the answer; the boolean only overrides it.**
   *
   * `accept` is the MCP elicitation spelling of "the person said yes" — `decline` and `cancel` are
   * the other two, and neither reaches here as an approval. A client that *did* render the form and
   * whose user unticked the box sends `accept` with `confirm: false`; that is a no, and it wins.
   * Absence is not a no — see the schema comment above for what absence actually measured as.
   */
  const answered = result?.content?.confirm;
  const accepted = result?.action === 'accept' && answered !== false;
  if (accepted) return { allowed: true, asked: true };

  return {
    allowed: false,
    asked: true,
    reason: CONSENT_DECLINED,
    message: `The change was not approved (${result?.action ?? 'no answer'}). No change was made: ${summary}.`,
  };
}

/**
 * **What "always allow" actually allows** — exactly as the adapter declared it.
 *
 * ## Why (2026-08-17)
 *
 * The permission card's third button **asserted** *"allow the entire folder containing the path above
 * for this whole conversation"*. But the adapter, not us, decides that scope. The adapter states it
 * through `_meta.permission.changes[].targets[]`, and measured, that value was **a tool, not a folder**:
 *
 * ```
 * { type: 'tool', toolName: 'mcp__atlas-vault__add_concept' }
 * ```
 *
 * Writing "allow the folder" while actually allowing a tool leaves the user believing **they granted
 * a permission they never gave, or the reverse.** That is the screen lying at this product's most
 * expensive decision.
 *
 * ## The rule
 *
 * **State only what the adapter declared.** The folder is not computed from the path and written down
 * by us — that would be guessing at the adapter's rules, and a wrong guess makes the card lie. Given
 * nothing, it asserts nothing.
 *
 * Mixed types is also "unknown". Forcing something that cannot be stated honestly in one sentence into
 * one sentence makes that sentence wrong about one of the two.
 */

export type PermissionScope =
  | { kind: 'tool'; names: string[] }
  | { kind: 'directory'; names: string[] }
  | { kind: 'unknown'; names: [] };

const UNKNOWN: PermissionScope = { kind: 'unknown', names: [] };

function asRecord(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> {
  return value && typeof value === 'object' ? (value as Record<string, unknown>) : {};
}

/**
 * @param options The `options` array of `session/request_permission`, verbatim.
 *   **Only the `_meta` of the "always allow" option is read** — reading another option's would
 *   describe the scope of a button that was not pressed.
 */
export function permissionScope(options: readonly unknown[]): PermissionScope {
  if (!Array.isArray(options)) return UNKNOWN;
  const always = options.find((o) => asRecord(o).kind === 'allow_always');
  if (!always) return UNKNOWN;

  const changes = asRecord(asRecord(asRecord(always)._meta).permission).changes;
  if (!Array.isArray(changes)) return UNKNOWN;

  const tools: string[] = [];
  const directories: string[] = [];
  let sawUnknownType = false;

  for (const change of changes) {
    const targets = asRecord(change).targets;
    if (!Array.isArray(targets)) continue;
    for (const target of targets) {
      const t = asRecord(target);
      if (t.type === 'tool' && typeof t.toolName === 'string' && t.toolName.trim()) {
        tools.push(t.toolName);
      } else if (t.type === 'directory' && typeof t.path === 'string' && t.path.trim()) {
        directories.push(t.path);
      } else {
        // Silently discarding an unknown type lets something else be allowed alongside while the card
        // says "only this one tool".
        sawUnknownType = true;
      }
    }
  }

  if (sawUnknownType) return UNKNOWN;
  if (tools.length > 0 && directories.length > 0) return UNKNOWN;
  if (tools.length > 0) return { kind: 'tool', names: tools };
  if (directories.length > 0) return { kind: 'directory', names: directories };
  return UNKNOWN;
}

 * possible, and what is added here is the session-mode branch. This function must be the only path —
 * if the screen's sentence and the action actually taken diverge, the screen makes a promise it
 * cannot keep.

export function isGuardedRuntime(runtimeId: string, isolated: boolean): boolean {

}

 * to the runtime and keeps the server gate off, so nobody is asked twice. `false` — the

  return typeof runtimeId === 'string' && CONFIG_ISOLATED_RUNTIMES.has(runtimeId);

//! ACP harness — a layer to invoke coding agents already installed by the user within the app.
//!
//! This file's responsibility is **finding**: which executors are actually present on this
//! machine, and what absolute paths are needed to launch them. Protocol (JSON-RPC) parsing
//! does not happen here — the UI layer handles that.
//!
//! ## Why reconstruct PATH directly (measured 2026-08-16)
//!
//! Just because `which node` works in the terminal doesn't mean the **app** can find it.
//! Apps launched via Finder·Dock on macOS do not go through shell initialization files (`.zshrc`, etc.),
//! so the paths set by version managers are entirely missing. Actual measurement on this machine:
//!
//! ```text
//! node · npx · codex → /Users/<me>/.nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/bin/
//! claude            → /Users/<me>/.local/bin/
//! ```
//!
//! Both are outside the default PATH for GUI apps. So saying "not found" would be a lie,
//! and the user would see a screen stating the tool they just used in the terminal is unavailable.
//!
//! **We do not launch a shell to extract PATH.** Running a login shell executes the user's
//! entire shell configuration, meaning we wouldn't know what gets executed. Instead, we only search **known locations** — exactly what is searched is written in the code, and that list
//! is itself the inspection target.
//!
//! ## Why pin the npx version
//!
//! The adapters (`claude-agent-acp` · `codex-acp`) are separate programs from the CLI. To avoid asking the user
//! to run `npm i -g`, we have two options — either the app bundles its own Node runtime and adapter
//! (reference products take this path, costing 1.06GB), or we invoke `npx` with the existing Node.
//! We chose the latter but **pin the version**: if not pinned, the adapter might update one day,
//! causing the app to silently speak a different protocol.
//!
//! If already installed, use it as-is — npx is slow on first execution.

use std::ffi::{OsStr, OsString};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// One item from the committed ACP registry snapshot.
///
/// The canonical list is `src-tauri/src/acp-registry.json`, generated by
/// `scripts/build-acp-registry.mjs`. **Never fetched at runtime** —
/// hitting a CDN every time the app starts is communication the user never asked for, and
/// the list would be empty on a flight.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct RegistryAgent {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub website: Option<String>,
    pub license: Option<String>,
    /// Whether we have **actually verified** it. A marker to prevent
    /// claiming the UI has done something it hasn't.
    pub verified: bool,
    /// The executable name of the real CLI wrapped by that adapter. `None` if unknown —
    /// guessing and filling in would fabricate reasons for UI absence.
    pub cli: Option<String>,
    /// Path to the bundled icon (`/acp-icons/<id>.svg`). Downloaded at build time so the app
    /// does not need to fetch images.
    pub icon: Option<String>,
    /// The vendor's brand color (`#RRGGBB`). Registry icons are all monochrome, so
    /// colors are added separately by the build script. Only **human-verified pairs** have values;
    /// if missing, the UI draws in grayscale — wrong brand color is worse than grayscale.
    #[serde(default, rename = "brandInk")]
    pub brand_ink: Option<String>,
    pub launch: RegistryLaunch,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub(crate) enum RegistryLaunch {
    /// `npx -y <package> <args…>`
    Npx {
        package: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        args: Vec<String>,
    },
    /// `uvx <package> <args…>`
    Uvx {
        package: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        args: Vec<String>,
    },
    /// An executable already installed by the user.
    ///
    /// ⚠️ **This comment used to say "the app never fetches it"** — conditionally changed on 2026-08-20
    /// (owner (88)). Installation only happens when all four conditions are met:
    /// the user clicks · we show what will be executed first · it installs only in an app-specific location · the version is pinned. The conditions and rationale are in `.claude/rules/forbidden.md`
    /// under the "Installing agent tools on behalf of the user" section.
    ///
    /// This branch (`Binary`) itself is unrelated to that — this is for **launching what is already in PATH**.
    Binary {
        command: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        args: Vec<String>,
    },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Deserialize)]
struct RegistrySnapshot {
    agents: Vec<RegistryAgent>,
}

/// The snapshot baked into the build. If the file is corrupted, **the build (not runtime)** must fail,
/// so we parse it only once here; if parsing fails, we leave an empty list — an empty list means
/// the UI says "nothing found" rather than launching something invalid.
fn registry() -> &'static [RegistryAgent] {
    static REGISTRY: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<RegistryAgent>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| {
        serde_json::from_str::<RegistrySnapshot>(include_str!("acp-registry.json"))
            .map(|s| s.agents)
            .unwrap_or_default()
    })
}

pub(crate) fn registry_agent(id: &str) -> Option<&'static RegistryAgent> {
    registry().iter().find(|a| a.id == id)
}

/// How to isolate settings — **only executors we have actually verified** are here.
///
/// Isolation requires knowing different environment variables and credential files per executor; filling
/// them in by guesswork causes login to silently break. So this table grows from
/// actual measurement, not the registry.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct IsolationSpec {
    pub id: &'static str,
    /// The environment variable that decides where this executor reads its configuration from.
    pub config_env: &'static str,
    /// The credential file name inside that config directory. To avoid breaking login upon isolation,
    /// we **link** this file to the user's original (do not copy).
    pub credentials_file: &'static str,
    /// The user's original config directory (relative to home).
    pub user_config_dir: &'static str,
}

pub(crate) const ISOLATION: &[IsolationSpec] = &[
    IsolationSpec {
        id: "claude-acp",
        config_env: "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR",
        credentials_file: ".credentials.json",
        user_config_dir: ".claude",
    },
    IsolationSpec {
        id: "codex-acp",
        config_env: "CODEX_HOME",
        credentials_file: "auth.json",
        user_config_dir: ".codex",
    },
];

// default mode at `agent` (codex's mode names — read-only/agent/agent-full-access — are completely
// different from claude's) and it wrote files **outside** the working folder with **0** permission
// requests. The second (installed acceptance, 2026-08-24): `read-only` blocked direct files but a
// self-registered Atlas `add_relation` changed the vault with no permission request at all.
//
// Neither hole is closed by a session mode, and that is the point — a mode is a request the adapter
// may override, which is exactly what was measured. Both are now closed by things this app owns:
// direct writes by the sandbox floor in `ISOLATED_CODEX_CONFIG` below, and Atlas MCP writes by the
// server-side checkpoint (`mcp/src/write-consent.mjs`, decision (113)).
//
// ⚠️ **Listing it here is not the same as offering in-app chat.** This entry only lets the app
// control the config directory. Whether the UI offers a conversation is decided separately in
// `runtime-gate.ts`, and decision (111) keeps that closed until an installed-app run proves reject
// and allow for both self-registered and injected writes.

/// Runtimes whose permission gate the app has **measured** — the only ones eligible for a
/// conversation inside the app.
///
/// ⚠️ **This is not the same list as `ISOLATION`, and keeping them apart is the whole lesson of
/// decision (111).** Isolation says the app can control a runtime's config directory. Eligibility
/// is the stronger claim that the resulting configuration actually stops a write until a person
/// answers. Codex is isolated and **not** eligible: its isolated `CODEX_HOME` was read (the `model`
/// value applied) while the approval policy was overridden, and an Atlas MCP write landed unasked.
///
/// A runtime joins this list only after an installed-app run shows reject-without-write **and**
/// allow-with-write, for both self-registered and injected Atlas MCP mutations.
///
/// ⚠️ **Codex earned its way back on 2026-08-24, and the run is what did it.** Decision (111)
/// named the price: *"an app-owned MCP proxy or server capability token reliably pauses every Codex
/// Atlas write."* The checkpoint now lives in the server that performs the write
/// (`mcp/src/write-consent.mjs`, decision (113)), so it holds for the vault's **own** registration
/// as much as for one the app injects — the hole that removed Codex in the first place.
///
/// Measured on the installed build against a disposable vault:
///
/// | answer | what the wire said | what the vault did |
/// |---|---|---|
/// | reject | `Error: The change was not approved (decline)` | unchanged, 10 files |
/// | allow  | `{"ok":true,"slug":"wire-probe","changed":true}` | the file appeared |
///
/// That run also caught the gate refusing **yes**: the elicitation required a `confirm` boolean an
/// ACP permission card has no way to send, so a person's approval came back as a decline. A
/// checkpoint that cannot be passed is a wall, and a wall teaches people to route around it.
pub(crate) const CHAT_ELIGIBLE: &[&str] = &["claude-acp", "codex-acp"];

/// Has this runtime's permission gate been measured to hold? See `CHAT_ELIGIBLE`.
pub(crate) fn chat_eligible(id: &str) -> bool {
    CHAT_ELIGIBLE.contains(&id)
}

fn isolation_for(id: &str) -> Option<&'static IsolationSpec> {
    ISOLATION.iter().find(|s| s.id == id)
}

/// The settings placed into sessions the app launches. **They do not inherit the user's global settings.**
///
/// Measured 2026-08-16: the owner's `~/.claude/settings.json` had `defaultMode: auto` and
/// 15 pre-allowed entries including `Bash(*)` · `Write(*)` · `Edit(*)`.
/// A session that inherited those settings wrote files **outside** the working folder while
/// **never asking once**, and even ran the terminal. Switching the session mode to
/// "confirm directly" changed nothing — pre-allowed entries pass regardless of mode.
///

     1	//! ACP harness — a layer to invoke coding agents already installed by the user within the app.
     2	//!
     3	//! This file's responsibility is **finding**: which executors are actually present on this
     4	//! machine, and what absolute paths are needed to launch them. Protocol (JSON-RPC) parsing
     5	//! does not happen here — the UI layer handles that.
     6	//!
     7	//! ## Why reconstruct PATH directly (measured 2026-08-16)
     8	//!
     9	//! Just because `which node` works in the terminal doesn't mean the **app** can find it.
    10	//! Apps launched via Finder·Dock on macOS do not go through shell initialization files (`.zshrc`, etc.),
    11	//! so the paths set by version managers are entirely missing. Actual measurement on this machine:
    12	//!
    13	//! ```text
    14	//! node · npx · codex → /Users/<me>/.nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/bin/
    15	//! claude            → /Users/<me>/.local/bin/
    16	//! ```
    17	//!
    18	//! Both are outside the default PATH for GUI apps. So saying "not found" would be a lie,
    19	//! and the user would see a screen stating the tool they just used in the terminal is unavailable.
    20	//!
    21	//! **We do not launch a shell to extract PATH.** Running a login shell executes the user's
    22	//! entire shell configuration, meaning we wouldn't know what gets executed. Instead, we only search **known locations** — exactly what is searched is written in the code, and that list
    23	//! is itself the inspection target.
    24	//!
    25	//! ## Why pin the npx version
    26	//!
    27	//! The adapters (`claude-agent-acp` · `codex-acp`) are separate programs from the CLI. To avoid asking the user
    28	//! to run `npm i -g`, we have two options — either the app bundles its own Node runtime and adapter
    29	//! (reference products take this path, costing 1.06GB), or we invoke `npx` with the existing Node.
    30	//! We chose the latter but **pin the version**: if not pinned, the adapter might update one day,
    31	//! causing the app to silently speak a different protocol.
    32	//!
    33	//! If already installed, use it as-is — npx is slow on first execution.
    34

    36	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

    98	#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Deserialize)]
    99	struct RegistrySnapshot {
   100	    agents: Vec<RegistryAgent>,
   101	}
   102	
   103	/// The snapshot baked into the build. If the file is corrupted, **the build (not runtime)** must fail,
   104	/// so we parse it only once here; if parsing fails, we leave an empty list — an empty list means
   105	/// the UI says "nothing found" rather than launching something invalid.
   106	fn registry() -> &'static [RegistryAgent] {
   107	    static REGISTRY: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<RegistryAgent>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
   108	    REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| {
   109	        serde_json::from_str::<RegistrySnapshot>(include_str!("acp-registry.json"))
   110	            .map(|s| s.agents)
   111	            .unwrap_or_default()
   112	    })
   113	}
   114	
   115	pub(crate) fn registry_agent(id: &str) -> Option<&'static RegistryAgent> {
   116	    registry().iter().find(|a| a.id == id)
   117	}

   119	/// How to isolate settings — **only executors we have actually verified** are here.
   120	///
   121	/// Isolation requires knowing different environment variables and credential files per executor; filling
   122	/// them in by guesswork causes login to silently break. So this table grows from
   123	/// actual measurement, not the registry.
   124	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
   125	pub(crate) struct IsolationSpec {

   130	    /// we **link** this file to the user's original (do not copy).
   131	    pub credentials_file: &'static str,
   132	    /// The user's original config directory (relative to home).
   133	    pub user_config_dir: &'static str,
   134	}

    15	## Definition
    16	The capability to apply ontology writing requested by a user directly correcting the map or an ACP agent into markdown frontmatter only after reviewing accurate typed change proposals. It keeps the map selection context and the user's final meaning decision authority in the same flow.
    17	
    18	## Boundaries
    19	Change proposals are volatile pre-write states, not separate approval ledgers or second drafts. Markdown written after confirmation becomes the draft immediately. The map editor handles only one relation at a time; ACP read tools proceed automatically, but write tools wait for `allow_once` or `reject_once`. Meaning writing does not provide `allow_always`. ACP's single/bundled changes preserve all items in protocol order. Bundled cards show the entire row as an accordion, previewing only the chosen relation as a dashed line between two nodes. Allow/reject applies to the entire bundle, not using the first item as a proxy for hidden ones. If allowed, it confirms as a solid line in place during the existing `--motion-settle` 240ms before proceeding with the tool; if rejected or the `toolCallId` ends, it retracts from the map.
    20

    22	- src/features/ontology-meaning-editor (relation editor for the same anchor as the selection node inspector)

    24	- src/entities/knowledge-graph/lib/ontology-relation-edit.ts (frontmatter before/after plan)

    16	
    17	## Definition
    18	
    19	The ability to detect ACP (Agent Client Protocol) v1 coding-agent executors already installed on the device, directly launch only those with a verified app-owned permission gate (currently Claude Agent), and apply scoped permission review. No new Atlas API key or vendor integration is needed: it uses the subscription authentication already held by the launched tool.
    20	
    21	
    22	## Behaviour Contract
    23	
    24	Ten things this capability actually does:
    25	
    26	1. **Detection.** The executor status of this device is divided into five categories: `ready`, `cli-missing`, `node-missing`, `uvx-missing`, and `binary-missing`. The reason for not collapsing the status into just "installed/not installed" is that the user's required actions differ for each state.
    27	2. **The list comes from a committed snapshot.** The ACP registry is fetched once at build time and saved to `src-tauri/src/acp-registry.json`; icons are also bundled into `public/acp-icons/`. The committed registry and icons require no runtime network lookup. Starting a selected coding agent is a separate boundary: that agent may communicate with its own provider.
    28	3. **Configuration isolation.** Sessions launched by the app use its own configuration directory within the app data folder (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`). Inheriting the user's global settings would mean the app cannot block anything for users who have set "allow all" in their terminal. Credentials are not copied but pointed to via symbolic links.
    29	4. **Permission judgment.** Atlas read tools inside the selected vault proceed automatically. Atlas write tools pause on the shared typed change review and continue only after `allow_once`; `reject_once` cancels them. Other requests are judged by scope: inside-vault paths may proceed, while outside or unresolved paths ask the user. The basis for path judgment is not the title string but the `toolCall.rawInput.file_path` (absolute path) from the original permission request. The vault root is verified and normalized by `acp_start` and bound to the native session rather than trusted from each screen request. If the session is missing or the root is invalid, the app asks. If the root path changes to an external symbolic link after session start, normalized-path mismatch rejects it so the boundary cannot shift during the session.
    30	5. **Working directory hygiene.** The working directory of a session must pass the same vault root judgment as the folder picker. Filesystem roots, the home directory itself, and OS/app directories are rejected.
    31	6. **Workflow safety state.** Modes provided by the adapter are categorized as verified, risky, or unverified. Verified modes are hidden by removing permission checks, while unverified modes are preserved in `AcpSessionChoices.unverifiedModeIds` to display "unverified" along with its meaning in the existing selector.
    32	7. **Process tree termination.** Children have their own process group; termination sends SIGTERM and waits up to 1 second before sending SIGKILL to terminate the entire group. Completion is determined by the survival of the original PGID, not the leader PID, so grandchildren that ignore TERM are not missed even if the leader is reaped first. If grandchildren launched by the adapter are not terminated together, processes will remain after the app is closed.
    33	
    34	8. **Map synchronization.** Compares the typed input of actually called Atlas `get_concept` and `find_path` in the current user turn against the current vault's slug table, then moves to the same HomePage node focus or exact shortest path lens. Natural language answers or non-existent slugs are not used as map movement grounds. The actual order in which the Claude adapter completes streamed input with status-less `tool_call_update.rawInput` after a pending `tool_call` is merged into the same tool action before determining intent.
    35	9. **Inset conversation surface.** Maintains the outer flex dock that actually yields map width, but displays the ACP/API-key conversation surface visible to the user within the top/bottom/right spacing ramp. It shares INDEX/node inspector's existing panel radius, border, surface, and shadow so it doesn't look like a black wall covering the window height without boundaries. The map control rail on the left of the panel is also pulled to 12px on the opposite side of the seam, limiting the gap between them to 24px, and moves with the same clock/curve as dock reflow.
    36	10. **First frame connection state.** Separates conversation scaffold from session booting; header, empty guidance, vault-derived suggestions, and composer are drawn from the first frame the dock opens. After the remaining 240ms landing of the camera live spring after width reflow, ACP start is allowed; in the meantime, only the spinner and `connecting` text of the same status badge change. For large panels, overlay fade is used without overlapping scale/translate chrome motion so that layout reflow becomes the primary action.
    37	
    38	## Boundaries
    39	- **The "Agents" destination (`/agents/`) and the conversation panel on the right of the home map are the current user surface.** Selecting a measured runtime for isolation gates opens `HomePage` which passes the current vault as working folder and MCP server to `AcpChatPanel`. "Open chat with this tool" at the destination puts the selected runtime id into a one-shot queue in sessionStorage, moves to the map, and is consumed only when HomePage confirms the same runtime's readiness. Paths that only send window events without subscribers in `/agents` are not used.
    40	
    41	  ⚠️ This line was *"The 'Runtime' section of settings … is neither a separate path nor a new screen"* until 2026-08-20. The archive (90) overturned it. Installation/connection is an operational task with progress status, not just picking values, so a blocking modal didn't fit the vessel. The same component (`AcpRuntimeSettings`) stands at both the destination and settings sheet; whether to draw an intro line is decided by the caller.
    42	- **Starter vault's project source comes first.** Without source binding, empty conversation recommendations open code folder connections from the project dataset instead of agent analysis, re-read sidecar transitions on the same screen, and only then provide the source-evidence-first build prompt.
    43	- **The session's vault MCP server maintains only one set.** Redundant injection is skipped only when a measured runtime already reads the same valid server from its vault config. That Codex self-read path is retained for external setup evidence, but it does not grant in-app chat eligibility.
    44	- **The app offers in-app chat only for a runtime with an app-owned permission gate, and today that is just `claude-acp`.** Others remain visible for detection and external connection setup. Codex `read-only` blocks direct file access, but an installed-app probe showed a self-registered Atlas MCP write could still run without a permission request, so Codex chat stays unavailable until the app owns that MCP checkpoint.
    45	- `isolated` reports Rust configuration isolation only. In-app eligibility additionally requires a proven ontology-write checkpoint and outside-folder gate; detection, external MCP setup, configuration isolation, and chat eligibility are distinct states. Unmeasured work modes in an eligible conversation remain explicitly unverified.
    46	- Permission verdict IPC receives only `sessionId` and request path. WebView has no argument to redeclare `vaultRoot` and change native session boundaries.
    47	- Browsers cannot launch processes. If `isAcpBridgeAvailable()` is false, the screen explains why it doesn't work and where it does.
    48	- Windows process tree ownership (Job Object) is outside this fragment. It attempts with `taskkill /T` and grandchildren may remain if it fails.

     2	 * **The app-owned write checkpoint.**
     3	 *
     4	 * ⚠️ Why this file exists (2026-08-24). The permission gate an agent shows is the

    17	 * performs the write**, not in a third party's config. A gate the vault owns holds
    18	 * for every client that ever connects, not just the one that was measured.

    23	 * `session/request_permission`, which is the same permission card the app already

    32	/** Same vocabulary as `OATLAS_READ_ONLY` so the two switches read alike. */
    33	export function parseConsentEnv(value) {
    34	  if (typeof value !== 'string') return false;
    35	  return ['1', 'true', 'yes', 'on'].includes(value.trim().toLowerCase());
    36	}
    37	
    38	/**
    39	 * A short, human-readable line naming what is about to change. It is the whole
    40	 * question a person answers, so it must say the vault-visible effect — not the
    41	 * tool's internal argument shape.
    42	 */
    43	export function describeWrite(toolName, args) {
    44	  const a = args && typeof args === 'object' ? args : {};
    45	  const slug = typeof a.slug === 'string' ? a.slug : null;
    46	  const from = typeof a.from === 'string' ? a.from : null;
    47	  const to = typeof a.to === 'string' ? a.to : null;
    48	  const count = (key) => (Array.isArray(a[key]) ? a[key].length : null);
    49	
    50	  switch (toolName) {
    51	    case 'add_concept':
    52	      return slug ? `Create concept ${slug}` : 'Create one concept';
    53	    case 'add_concepts': {
    54	      const n = count('concepts');
    55	      return n === null ? 'Create concepts' : `Create ${n} concept(s)`;
    56	    }
    57	    case 'add_relation':
    58	      return from && to ? `Link ${from} → ${to}` : 'Add one relation';
    59	    case 'add_relations': {
    60	      const n = count('relations');
    61	      return n === null ? 'Add relations' : `Add ${n} relation(s)`;
    62	    }
    63	    case 'remove_relation':
    64	      return from && to ? `Remove the link ${from} → ${to}` : 'Remove one relation';
    65	    case 'replace_relation':
    66	      return from && to ? `Replace the link ${from} → ${to}` : 'Replace one relation';
    67	    case 'patch_concept':
    68	      return slug ? `Edit concept ${slug}` : 'Edit one concept';
    69	    case 'rename_concept':
    70	      return from && to ? `Rename ${from} → ${to}` : 'Rename one concept';
    71	    case 'reclassify_concept':
    72	      return slug ? `Change the kind of ${slug}` : 'Change one concept kind';
    73	    case 'merge_concepts':
    74	      return from && to ? `Merge ${from} into ${to}` : 'Merge concepts';
    75	    case 'delete_concept':
    76	      return slug ? `Delete concept ${slug}` : 'Delete one concept';
    77	    case 'absorb_document':
    78	      return 'Absorb a document into typed nodes';
    79	    case 'connect_project_source':
    80	      return 'Connect a source folder to this vault';
    81	    case 'disconnect_project_source':
    82	      return 'Disconnect a source folder from this vault';
    83	    case 'git_snapshot':
    84	      return 'Commit the vault';
    85	    case 'finalize_project_meaning':
    86	      return 'Write the project meaning receipt';
    87	    case 'index_project':
    88	      return 'Write an index of the connected source';
    89	    default:
    90	      return `Run ${toolName}`;
    91	  }
    92	}
    93	
    94	/**
    95	 * A dry run asks for nothing: it reports a plan and leaves the disk alone, so
    96	 * pausing it would train people to click through the very card that matters.
    97	 * The flag name differs per tool, so both spellings are honoured.
    98	 */
    99	export function isDryRun(args) {
   100	  if (!args || typeof args !== 'object') return false;
   101	  return args.dryRun === true || args.dry_run === true;
   102	}
   103	
   104	export const CONSENT_DECLINED = 'consent-declined';
   105	export const CONSENT_UNAVAILABLE = 'consent-unavailable';
   106	
   107	/**
   108	 * Ask the connected client to put this write in front of a person.
   109	 *
   110	 * `server` is the low-level SDK `Server`; `elicitInput` is its push-style
   111	 * server→client request. Returns `{ allowed }` and, when refused, a `reason` the
   112	 * caller turns into an error the agent can read and act on.
   113	 */
   114	export async function requestWriteConsent({ server, toolName, args, enabled }) {
   115	  if (!enabled) return { allowed: true, asked: false };
   116	  if (isDryRun(args)) return { allowed: true, asked: false };
   117	
   118	  const capabilities =
   119	    typeof server?.getClientCapabilities === 'function' ? server.getClientCapabilities() : undefined;
   120	  if (!capabilities || !capabilities.elicitation) {
   121	    return {
   122	      allowed: false,
   123	      asked: false,
   124	      reason: CONSENT_UNAVAILABLE,
   125	      message:
   126	        `This vault requires a human decision before any write, and this client did not offer ` +
   127	        `a way to ask (no "elicitation" capability was declared at initialize). No change was made. ` +
   128	        `Use a client that can surface permission requests, or unset OATLAS_WRITE_CONSENT for a ` +
   129	        `vault where the client owns the gate.`,
   130	    };
   131	  }
   132	
   133	  const summary = describeWrite(toolName, args);
   134	  let result;
   135	  try {
   136	    result = await server.elicitInput({
   137	      mode: 'form',
   138	      /*
   139	       * ⚠️ **`confirm` is asked for, never required** (installed acceptance, 2026-08-24).
   140	       *
   141	       * It was `required: ['confirm']` at first, and that made the gate refuse **every** answer,
   142	       * including yes. A form-capable client fills the boolean; an ACP bridge does not have one to
   143	       * fill. `codex-acp` maps this request onto ACP `session/request_permission`, the app renders
   144	       * its ordinary permission card, and pressing 「allow once」 comes back as `action: 'accept'`
   145	       * with **no form content at all**. Codex reported it verbatim: *"the permission response was
   146	       * invalid because it lacked the required `confirm` field"* — the write was refused, twice,
   147	       * after a person had said yes.
   148	       *
   149	       * A checkpoint that cannot be passed is not a checkpoint, it is a wall, and a wall teaches
   150	       * people to route around the gate. So the boolean stays as the **form** spelling of the
   151	       * question, and `action` stays the answer.
   152	       */
   153	      message: `${summary}. Apply this change to the vault?`,
   154	      requestedSchema: {
   155	        type: 'object',
   156	        properties: {
   157	          confirm: {
   158	            type: 'boolean',
   159	            title: 'Apply this change',
   160	            description: `${toolName} — ${summary}`,
   161	          },
   162	        },
   163	      },
   164	    });
   165	  } catch (error) {
   166	    // A transport error, a timeout, or a client that advertised the capability
   167	    // and then refused the method all land here. None of them is a yes.
   168	    return {
   169	      allowed: false,
   170	      asked: true,
   171	      reason: CONSENT_UNAVAILABLE,
   172	      message:
   173	        `Asking for permission failed (${error?.message ?? 'unknown error'}). No change was made.`,
   174	    };
   175	  }
   176	
   177	  /*
   178	   * **`action` is the answer; the boolean only overrides it.**
   179	   *
   180	   * `accept` is the MCP elicitation spelling of "the person said yes" — `decline` and `cancel` are
   181	   * the other two, and neither reaches here as an approval. A client that *did* render the form and
   182	   * whose user unticked the box sends `accept` with `confirm: false`; that is a no, and it wins.
   183	   * Absence is not a no — see the schema comment above for what absence actually measured as.
   184	   */
   185	  const answered = result?.content?.confirm;
   186	  const accepted = result?.action === 'accept' && answered !== false;
   187	  if (accepted) return { allowed: true, asked: true };
   188	
   189	  return {
   190	    allowed: false,
   191	    asked: true,
   192	    reason: CONSENT_DECLINED,
   193	    message: `The change was not approved (${result?.action ?? 'no answer'}). No change was made: ${summary}.`,
   194	  };
   195	}

    14	## Definition
    15	The ability for humans to read in one flow the AI agent's product name, verified current stage, work goals and targets, and next actions from the map. Only when there is a fresh heartbeat does it speak of plan/edit/verify/approval waits in present tense; if only write logs are recent, it does not infer "in progress" but distinguishes by change detection or last work time.
    16	
    17	## Boundaries
    18	- The screen converts audit client/runtime IDs like `codex-mcp-client`·`codex-acp` to human product names like Codex·Claude Code, but preserves original logs and heartbeat values. Map status bars, global rails, and detailed activity surfaces all use the same display name boundary.
    19	- Current targets connect to map rings and focus only when heartbeats or tool inputs reveal actual vault slugs. Already on the map, it updates HomePage's selection state without remounting the vault; independent consumers use `/topology?mode=focus&p=…` fallback only. Unknown targets get no links or rings.
    20	- In-app ACP's `onTurnActivityChange` updates map focus and activity chips first in the same render cycle, with sidecar records following for external consumer/restart continuity. If there is no target for the current in-app turn, it does not revive the previous sidecar target.
    21	- When the right agent dock opens, INDEX does not change save preference but collapses for the session to yield map width. Closing the dock restores original preference; opening INDEX tab directly closes the dock.
    22	- Dock space first opens with existing `--agent-panel-reflow-duration` and camera follows new width with live spring of the same clock. The model rejects responses if it synthesizes capabilities/elements as non-existent when only one project root is selected or census confirms existence. Final synthesis preserves incompleteness of the verified scope without using count, fan-out, recommended node counts, or bridge evidence as defects.  20201	## 2026-08-24 — Codex returns to in-app chat, because the checkpoint moved to the server
 20202	
 20203	**Convened because**: decision (111) removed Codex from in-app chat and wrote down
 20204	the exact price of return. This record pays it, and records what the acceptance run
 20205	found on the way.
 20206	
 20207	**Prior decision**: (111) stands and is now satisfied, not overturned. Its restore
 20208	condition was *"an app-owned MCP proxy or server capability token reliably pauses
 20209	every Codex Atlas write… proves reject/allow on a disposable vault."* (113) built
 20210	that checkpoint inside the server that performs the write. This record is the
 20211	measurement.
 20212	
 20213	**What was measured** — installed build, disposable vault at `~/Downloads/atlas-accept`
 20214	(10 Markdown files), Codex registered by the **vault's own** `.codex/config.toml`,
 20215	which is the registration path (111) could not gate:
 20216	
 20217	| answer | wire | vault |
 20218	|---|---|---|
 20219	| reject | `Error: The change was not approved (decline). No change was made` | unchanged, 10 files |
 20220	| allow | `{"ok":true,"slug":"wire-probe","changed":true}` | the file appeared |
 20221	
 20222	**What the run caught that no unit test had**: the gate refused **yes**. The
 20223	elicitation declared `required: ['confirm']`, and an ACP permission card has no form
 20224	to fill — `codex-acp` maps 「allow once」 to `action: 'accept'` with no content, so a
 20225	person's approval arrived as a decline. Codex reported it verbatim: *"the permission
 20226	response was invalid because it lacked the required `confirm` field."* A checkpoint
 20227	that cannot be passed is a wall, and a wall teaches people to route around the gate
 20228	rather than answer it. `action` is now the answer; the boolean only overrides it.
 20229	
 20230	**Decision (accountable: owner)**: `codex-acp` joins `CHAT_ELIGIBLE`. `ISOLATION` and
 20231	`CHAT_ELIGIBLE` stay separate lists — controlling a config directory is not the same
 20232	claim as the resulting configuration holding a write, and conflating them is what
 20233	2026-08-24 was about.
 20234	
 20235	**Recorded dissent**: one green acceptance is a smaller sample than the two red
 20236	measurements that removed Codex, and the gate depends on a third party continuing to
 20237	forward `mcpServer/elicitation/request`. The counter is that the checkpoint no longer
 20238	lives in that third party's configuration: it lives in the server, fails closed when a
 20239	client declares no `elicitation` capability, and therefore degrades to refusal rather
 20240	than to a silent write.
 20241

  3417	TERM을 무시하는 손자를 실제 그룹으로 띄우고, 리더를 먼저 회수한 뒤 손자가
  3418	남는 것을 재현했다. 실패 경로에서도 원래 PGID를 강제 정리해 테스트가 고아

  3447	`ask`로 닫는다. 세션 시작 뒤 저장된 루트 경로가 외부 심볼릭 링크로 바뀌어도
  3448	새 대상을 같은 볼트로 승격하지 않는다.
  3449	
  3450	**어떻게 찾았나**: `acp_permission_verdict`가 WebView에서 받은 `vaultRoot`를 그대로
  3451	`starts_with` 비교에 사용했다. 빈 문자열은 현재 작업 폴더로 해석되고 `/`는 모든
  3452	절대 경로의 조상이므로, 둘 중 하나를 넘기면 볼트 밖 파일도
  3453	`allow-inside-vault`가 됐다. RED 테스트는 빈 루트가 실제 외부 파일을 허용하고,
  3454	화면이 네이티브 세션 ID 대신 `/vault` 문자열을 판정 함수에 보내는 두 경로를
  3455	각각 재현했다. 두 번째 RED 검사는 세션 시작 뒤 볼트 폴더를 외부 디렉터리 링크로
  3456	교체하면 그 외부 파일까지 자동 허용되는 TOCTOU 갈래를 재현했다.
  3457	
  3458	**적용 규칙**: 권한 경계는 검증한 쪽이 소유한다 · WebView는 루트를 재선언하지
  3459	않는다 · 알 수 없는 세션과 잘못된 경로는 실패 폐쇄한다 · 레지스트리 패키지 버전은
  3460	테스트에 두 번 적지 않고 현재 스냅샷에서 읽는다.
  3461	**서명**: Codex — 보안 감사·TDD·구현 · 진안 — 장기 보안·품질 목표 승인
  3462	
  3463	**기록된 반대**: 현재 호출자는 앱이 작성한 WebView 코드뿐이므로 루트 문자열도
  3464	같은 값일 가능성이 높다. 그러나 IPC는 신뢰 경계이고, 판정 함수가 권한을 직접
  3465	허용하는 이상 호출자가 정답을 보냈다는 전제는 관문이 아니다.
  3466	**반증 조건**: 하나의 살아 있는 ACP 세션이 의도적으로 여러 볼트로 권한 경계를
  3467	옮겨야 하는 사용자 흐름이 생긴다. 그러면 임의 문자열을 다시 받지 말고, 기존
  3468	세션 종료 또는 네이티브가 검증하는 명시적 재바인딩 계약을 설계한다.
  3469	**재검토**: ACP 세션이 다중 볼트 작업을 지원할 때.
  3470	
  3471	**상태**: 유효

  3474	
  3475	**소집**: 단독 패스 · **트리거**: 정적 HTML의 저장소 콘텐츠 신뢰 경계 반증 ·
  3476	**루브릭**: 23/24 (치명적 0: 없음)
  3477

  3479	하나가 직렬화를 소유하고, JSON 의미를 바꾸지 않으면서 HTML이 태그 경계로 읽는
  3480	`<` · `>` · `&` · U+2028 · U+2029를 JSON 유니코드 escape로 바꾼다.
  3481

  3483	프로젝트 상세은 `JSON.stringify` 결과를 `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`로 바로 넣고
  3484	있었다. 값이 `</script><script>…`를 포함하면 정적 HTML에서 첫 태그를 닫고 다음
  3485	태그를 실행 가능한 형제로 만들 수 있었다. RED 계약 검사는 download 라우트의
  3486	직접 삽입에서 먼저 실패했다. 구현 뒤에는 악성 값을 담은 정적 마크업에 script가
  3487	하나만 남고, 그 본문을 다시 `JSON.parse`하면 원래 값이 복원됨을 증명했다.
  3488	
  3489	**적용 규칙**: 저장소 콘텐츠도 HTML 코드가 아니다 · escape는 소비처마다 다시
  3490	쓰지 않고 한 경계가 소유한다 · 게이트는 raw script 0과 실제 `JsonLd` 소비자 1개
  3491	이상을 함께 확인한다.
  3492	**서명**: Codex — 보안 감사·TDD·구현 · 진안 — 장기 보안·품질 목표 승인
  3493	
  3494	**기록된 반대**: 현재 번들 샘플은 신뢰된 저장소 콘텐츠라 즉시 악용되는 사용자
  3495	입력은 아니다. 그러나 외부 볼트 흡수·기여 diff·생성 문서가 같은 빌드 입력이어서

   122	## 2026-08-24 (113) — The write checkpoint moves into the server that performs the write
   123	
   124	**Prior decisions**: (111) removed `codex-acp` from in-app chat because a Codex
   125	`read-only` session let an Atlas MCP write reach disk with no permission request,
   126	and named the way back: *"an app-owned MCP proxy or server capability token
   127	reliably pauses every Codex Atlas write."* This record builds that checkpoint. It
   128	does **not** restore Codex chat — (111) stays active until its installed-app
   129	proof exists.
   130	
   131	**Observed cause**: Codex's approval policy documents its own scope — it decides
   132	"when the model requires human approval before executing **a command**". MCP tool
   133	calls were never inside it. Reading `codex-acp` confirms the shape: the adapter
   134	builds permission requests from `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` and
   135	`item/fileChange/requestApproval`, and there is no MCP-tool equivalent. So the
   136	gate the screen promised did not exist on the wire, and no third-party
   137	configuration could have supplied it.
   138	
   139	**The lever we already own**: the same adapter forwards
   140	`mcpServer/elicitation/request` into ACP `session/request_permission`, and the
   141	MCP SDK this server runs on (`@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.0.0, latest
   142	published) implements `elicitation/create`. A gate placed in Atlas's own MCP
   143	server therefore reaches every client that ever connects, instead of one that was
   144	measured.
   145	
   146	**Solo PO pass**: 21/24 (problem 4, user moment 3, differentiation 3, ontology
   147	value 4, agent value 4, verification 3; no fatal zero).
   148	
   149	**Decision**: write tools ask before they write when `OATLAS_WRITE_CONSENT` is
   150	on. The switch is per session and set by whoever launches the server, so a vault
   151	whose client already owns the gate is unchanged. **One session, one checkpoint,
   152	held by whoever can actually hold it**: a runtime with app-owned config isolation
   153	(Claude) keeps its own gate and the server gate stays off, so nobody is asked
   154	twice; every other runtime — including one nobody has measured — gets the server
   155	gate, because an unasked write is worse than one question too many.
   156	
   157	**Fail closed**: if the gate is on and the client never declared the
   158	`elicitation` capability, the write is refused rather than performed. A
   159	checkpoint that waves traffic through when it cannot see is the failure this
   160	record exists to end.
   161	
   162	**Measured** (disposable vaults, wire evidence):
   163	
   164	| gate | client | asked | vault |
   165	|---|---|---|---|
   166	| off | no elicitation | no | **wrote** (7 → 8) |
   167	| on | no elicitation | no | refused (7 → 7) |
   168	| on | accepts | yes | wrote (7 → 8) |
   169	| on | declines | yes | refused (7 → 7) |
   170	| on | **real Codex** | yes | **refused** (7 → 7) |
   171	
   172	The Codex row used `codex exec` against an isolated `CODEX_HOME`: the same
   173	`add_concept` call that (111) measured writing unasked returned *"The change was
   174	not approved (decline). No change was made."* and left the vault untouched.
   175	
   176	**Recorded dissent**: a gate that asks per tool call will be clicked through, and
   177	batching would have produced one question for a whole plan instead of one per
   178	write. **Falsifier**: a session in which a person approves a long run of writes
   179	without reading them, or asks for the prompts to stop. Then the unit of consent
   180	is the plan, not the call, and this moves up to the plan layer.
   181	
   182	**Isolation is not gate ownership**: Rust's `ISOLATION` says the app can control
   183	a runtime's config directory. Owning the gate is the stronger claim that the
   184	resulting configuration actually asks *for MCP writes* — true for Claude, false
   185	for Codex, whose isolated `CODEX_HOME` was read while its approval policy was
   186	overridden. Conflating the two is how (111) happened;
   187	`runtime-gate.test.ts` holds the one-directional invariant.
   188	
   189	**Not in this change**: restoring Codex in-app chat. That needs the Rust
   190	isolation entry, a rebuilt app, and the installed-app acceptance (111) demands —
   191	reject and allow, for both self-registered and injected writes. Half of it is now
   192	measured; the direct-write half has not been re-measured with both gates live,
   193	and (111) says explicitly not to restore from a direct-file sandbox result.
   194

  1599	| CLI 설치 | `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh \| bash` — 원격 스크립트를 셸에 파이프. 버전 고정 없음, 해시 없음 | `npm install --prefix <앱전용> <pkg>@<정확한 버전>` |
  1600	| 어댑터(npm) | `npm install -g @agentclientprotocol/…` — **버전 고정 없음** | `@0.69.0` 고정 |
  1601	| Node | **sha256 박아 두고 대조** | 이 기록으로 같아짐 |
  1602	
  1603	즉 Buzz 가 앞선 것은 **Node 하나**였고, 이 기록이 그것을 메운다.
  1604	
  1605	**결정**: Node 를 **앱 전용 자리**에 받아 둔다. (88) 의 조건 넷을 그대로 지키되,
  1606	④(검증)를 **가장 센 형태**로 한다.
  1607	
  1608	1. **사용자가 누른다** — 「도구를 띄울 수 있나」가 막혔을 때만 제안한다.
  1609	2. **어디서 무엇을 받는지 먼저 보여 준다** — 주소 전문과 **해시 앞머리**가
  1610	   버튼 위에 있다. 「검증한다」가 말뿐이 아님을 화면이 스스로 댄다.
  1611	3. **`<app-data>/runtimes/node/` 안에만.** 시스템 Node 도 PATH 도 안 건드린다.
  1612	   탐색 경로에서는 **맨 뒤**라, 사용자가 자기 손으로 깐 Node 가 언제나 이긴다.
  1613	4. **버전을 박고 해시를 대조한다.** 값은 공식 `SHASUMS256.txt` 에서 직접 읽어
  1614	   옮겼다(Buzz 의 값과 같은데, 같은 원본을 각자 읽었기 때문이다). 안 맞으면
  1615	   **받은 것을 지우고 실패한다** — 반쯤 받은 것을 남기면 다음 실행이 그것을
  1616	   쓰려다 더 이상한 자리에서 죽는다.
  1617	
  1618	**적용 규칙**: 최소 슬라이스 · 헌장 우선 · 제거 요구(안 쓰는 플랫폼은 등재 안 함).
  1619	
  1620	**새 의존성 0.** 받는 것은 `curl`, 푸는 것은 `tar`(macOS/Linux)·`Expand-Archive`
  1621	(Windows), 해시는 이미 있는 `sha2`. 셋 다 OS 가 들고 있다.
  1622	
  1623	**등재 플랫폼은 우리가 배포하는 것만** — darwin-arm64 · darwin-x64 · win-x64 ·
  1624	linux-x64. 그 밖에서는 이 기능이 아예 없고 화면은 종전대로 공식 안내로 보낸다.
  1625	안 해 본 자리에 설치를 제안하면 화면이 확인한 적 없는 것을 해 주겠다고 말하는
  1626	것이 된다.
  1627	
  1628	**서명**: 소유자(지시로 확정)
  1629	
  1630	**기록된 반대** (지렛대 자리의 논점): *"버전을 올릴 때마다 해시 네 줄을 사람이
  1631	갱신해야 한다. 그 잡일은 잊히기 쉽고, 잊히면 앱은 낡은 Node 를 계속 받는다.
  1632	게다가 195MB 를 사용자 디스크에 얹는다 — 이미 Node 가 있는 사람에게는 순수한
  1633	낭비이고, 없는 사람도 그 크기를 예상하지 못한다."*
  1634	
  1635	**반증 조건**: 이 반대가 옳았다면 — ① 고정 버전이 6개월 넘게 안 올라가거나
  1636	② Node 를 이미 가진 사람에게 이 제안이 뜨는 사례가 관측되거나 ③ 받다가 실패한
  1637	제보가 설치 문의의 다수가 되면. 하나라도 관측되면 되돌리고 안내 링크로 간다.
  1638	
  1639	**재검토**: 위 셋 중 하나. 또는 다음 Node LTS 로 올릴 때(그때 해시 갱신이
  1640	실제로 잡일인지 아닌지가 드러난다).
  1641	
  1642	**상태**: 유효
  1643	
  1644	## 2026-08-20 (88) — 에이전트 CLI 를 앱이 대신 깔아 준다: 고정·검증·격리 셋을 갖출 때만
  1645	
  1646	**소집**: 단독 패스 · **트리거**: 소유자 —
  1647	*"설치 방법이 아니라 설치를 우리가 제공해야하는거 아닌가? buzz는 그렇던데?"* ·
  1648	*"이렇게 해도 이슈없는거면 해도될듯? 조사해보고? 금지를 변경하자"*.
  1649	직전 워크스루에서 **도구가 하나도 없는 사람의 유일한 다음 걸음이 막다른 길**
  1650	이었던 것이 발단이다(그 링크는 눌러도 아무 일도 안 났다 — 별건으로 수리됨).
  1651	
  1652	**먼저 정정한다.** 이 금지는 우리가 생각한 것보다 **좁았다.**
  1653	`forbidden.md` 의 「플러그인/확장」 조항은 **Atlas 에 남의 코드를 꽂는 플러그인
  1654	시장**에 관한 것이고, 오히려 이렇게 **전제**하고 있다 — *"그 에이전트가 도는
  1655	곳(Claude Code/Codex/Cursor)은 사용자가 이미 믿기로 결정하고 설치한 프로그램
  1656	이다."* 실제로 걸리는 것은 `acp.rs` 의 **주석 한 줄**뿐이었다:
  1657	*"남의 바이너리를 앱이 내려받아 실행하는 것은 이 제품이 안 하기로 한 일이다."*
  1658	
  1659	그리고 **우리 코드는 이미 그 선을 넘고 있다.** 대화를 열 때마다
  1660	`npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.69.0` 을 돌린다 — 남이 쓴
  1661	코드를 받아서 실행하는 것이다. 즉 금지된 것은 **CLI 설치**뿐이고 **어댑터
  1662	다운로드는 이미 하고 있었다.** 규칙과 코드가 어긋나 있었고, 이 기록이 그것을
  1663	맞춘다.
  1664	
  1665	**조사(참고: Buzz, Apache-2.0, `github.com/block/buzz`).** 같은 문제를 같은
  1666	프로토콜(ACP)로 푸는 제품이 어떻게 하는지 소스를 읽었다. 베낀 것은 없고 **설계
  1667	성질 셋**을 근거로 삼았다:
  1668	
  1669	| 성질 | Buzz 의 구현 |
  1670	|---|---|
  1671	| **고정** | Node `v24.18.0` · 어댑터 패키지 버전 명시 |
  1672	| **검증** | 플랫폼별 SHA-256 을 바이너리에 박아 두고 받은 뒤 대조, 안 맞으면 실패 |
  1673	| **격리** | 전역 npm 이 아니라 **앱 전용 prefix**(`<data>/Buzz/node-tools`). 카탈로그에는 `npm install -g` 로 적어 두고 **실행 직전에 앱 전용 prefix 로 바꿔 쓴다** |
  1674	
  1675	**결정**: 금지를 **없애지 않고 조건부로 바꾼다.** 앱이 도구를 대신 설치하는 것은
  1676	아래 넷을 **전부** 갖출 때만 허용한다.
  1677	
  1678	1. **사용자가 누른다.** 자동 설치는 없다. 앱이 켜질 때 무엇도 받지 않는다.
  1679	2. **무엇을 실행하는지 먼저 보여 준다.** 누르기 전에 명령 원문이 화면에 있다.
  1680	3. **앱 전용 자리에만 깐다.** 사용자의 전역 npm · 시스템 PATH · 다른 도구의
  1681	   설정을 건드리지 않는다. 지우면 흔적이 남지 않는다.
  1682	4. **버전을 고정하고, 검증할 수 있으면 검증한다.** 해시를 댈 수 있는 것(공식
  1683	   타르볼)은 해시를 대조한다. npm 패키지는 정확한 버전을 고정한다.
  1684	
  1685	**적용 규칙**: 최소 슬라이스 · 헌장 우선.
  1686	
  1687	**신뢰 헌장은 안 깨진다** — 여섯 줄을 하나씩 대조했다. ②(사용자 모르게 수집
  1688	하지 않는다 · 무엇을 보내든 사용자가 켠다)는 **밖으로 나가는 사용자 데이터**에
  1689	관한 것이고, 여기서 나가는 것은 없다. ④(데이터는 평범한 마크다운)도 무관하다.
  1690	①③⑤⑥ 모두 해당 없음.
  1691	
  1692	**첫 슬라이스에서 하지 않는 것**: **Node 를 우리가 받아 오지 않는다.** Buzz 는
  1693	하지만 그건 플랫폼 6종 × 해시 유지 + 50MB 대역이라 표면이 훨씬 크다. Node 가
  1694	없으면 종전대로 공식 안내로 보낸다. 조건이 갖춰지면 그때 다시 본다.
  1695	
  1696	**서명**: 소유자(지시로 확정)
  1697	
  1698	**기록된 반대** (지킴이 자리의 논점): *"우리 차별점은 「이미 쓰는 에이전트를
  1699	붙인다」이고, 도구가 하나도 없는 사람은 아직 우리 사용자가 아니다. 설치까지
  1700	떠맡으면 유지할 표면(버전·플랫폼·실패 모드)이 늘고, 그 표면은 우리가 잘하는
  1701	것과 무관하다. 막다른 길은 링크를 고치는 것으로 이미 해결됐다."*
  1702	
  1703	**반증 조건**: 이 반대가 옳았다면 — ① 설치 실패 제보가 연결 문의의 다수를
  1704	차지하거나 ② 앱 전용 prefix 로 깐 CLI 가 사용자의 터미널 것과 **버전이 갈려**
  1705	「앱에서만 다르게 동작한다」가 관측되거나 ③ 우리가 유지해야 할 설치 경로가
  1706	도구 하나를 넘어 늘어나기 시작하면. 셋 중 하나라도 관측되면 이 결정을 되돌리고
  1707	링크 안내로 돌아간다.
  1708	
  1709	**재검토**: 위 셋 중 하나가 관측될 때. 또는 Node 를 우리가 받아 오자는 제안이
  1710	다시 올라올 때(그건 이 결정의 범위 밖이므로 새 기록이 필요하다).
  1711	
  1712	**상태**: 유효

   316	/// The `bin` directories of Nodes installed by nvm — **the version the user chose to use comes first**.
   317	///
   318	/// nvm keeps a separate directory per version and the shell puts only one of them on PATH.
   319	/// The app does not go through that shell, so it must pick directly — and **picking the newest is the wrong answer.**
   320	///
   321	/// Measurement on this machine (2026-08-16) showed exactly that: `claude` remained only in
   322	/// the bin of `v22.15.0` while the user's real `claude` is `~/.local/bin`. Version
   323	/// directories are **where stale copies of globally installed CLIs pile up**, so rummaging

   520	/// Finds the **actual program to launch**. This is the single place where status display and execution
   521	/// use the same answer — if split, the UI says "launching this" but something else appears.
   522	///
   523	/// For npx: if a globally installed adapter exists, use it (npx is slow on first execution).
   524	fn resolve_program(
   525	    launch: &RegistryLaunch,
   526	    dirs: &[PathBuf],
   527	    probe: &FsProbe<'_>,
   528	) -> Option<PathBuf> {
   529	    match launch {
   530	        RegistryLaunch::Npx { package, .. } => adapter_bin_name(package)
   531	            .and_then(|bin| resolve_command(&bin, dirs, probe))
   532	            .or_else(|| resolve_command("npx", dirs, probe)),
   533	        RegistryLaunch::Uvx { .. } => resolve_command("uvx", dirs, probe),
   534	        RegistryLaunch::Binary { command, .. } => resolve_command(command, dirs, probe),
   535	    }
   536	}

Capability 소유권도 의도적으로 나뉩니다.

- **MCP Server**가 볼트 도구를 제공합니다. ACP는 이를 `session/new`에 연결할 뿐 대체하지 않습니다.
- **Reviewed Ontology Writing**이 정확한 변경 전후, 묶음 검토, `allow_once`/`reject_once`, `allow_always` 금지를 소유합니다. [reviewed-ontology-writing.md](/Users/stark/orca/workspaces/oh-my-ontology/main-2/docs/ontology/capabilities/reviewed-ontology-writing.md:15)
- **Vault Agent**는 API key나 local runner에 붙는 provider-neutral, vault-tool-only 루프입니다. 코딩 에이전트를 직접 띄우는 ACP와는 다른 정체성입니다. [vault-agent.md](/Users/stark/orca/workspaces/oh-my-ontology/main-2/docs/ontology/capabilities/vault-agent.md:27)
- **Agent Work Visibility**가 heartbeat와 제한된 작업 영수증을 맡습니다. 전체 대화·절대 경로·본문 값은 저장하지 않습니다. [agent-work-visibility.md](/Users/stark/orca/workspaces/oh-my-ontology/main-2/docs/ontology/capabilities/agent-work-visibility.md:17)

중요한 최신성 불일치가 두 군데 있습니다. ontology 노드는 아직 “상태 5종”과 “인앱 채팅은 Claude만”이라고 적지만, 현재 구현은 상태를 `ready`, `login-needed`, `cli-unknown`, `cli-missing`, `node-missing`, `uvx-missing`, `binary-missing`의 **7종**으로 구분합니다. [tauri-acp.ts](/Users/stark/orca/workspaces/oh-my-ontology/main-2/src/shared/lib/tauri-acp.ts:66)

또한 현재 인앱 채팅 적격 실행기는 **Claude와 Codex 둘 다**입니다. Claude는 격리 설정이 쓰기 관문을 소유하고, Codex는 Atlas MCP 서버의 fail-closed elicitation 관문을 사용합니다. [acp.rs](/Users/stark/orca/workspaces/oh-my-ontology/main-2/src-tauri/src/acp.rs:187), [write-consent.mjs](/Users/stark/orca/workspaces/oh-my-ontology/main-2/mcp/src/write-consent.mjs:114) Codex는 실제 reject/allow 설치 앱 검증 후 다시 적격 목록에 들어왔습니다. [DECISIONS.md](/Users/stark/orca/workspaces/oh-my-ontology/main-2/docs/DECISIONS.md:20201)
